packets.rationale: Six packets change Cargo.lock (CC.4b, CD.7a, CE.2a, CE.2c, CE.2e, CE.3b), four of them engine/Cargo.toml and two cli/Cargo.toml. stamp/build.rs hashes Cargo.lock whole (HASHED_FILES = ["Cargo.lock"], read at HEAD) and engine/ is a HASHED_ROOT, so each lock edit moves PARSER_STAMP and discards every parse cache; CE's verifier asked for the lock movers to land together, which the file-disjoint scheduler cannot do while they all claim Cargo.lock (6 claimants = 6 distinct waves). One wave-0 commit adds every new dependency with the exact spec its owner packet chose, so the lock moves once and the owners claim no manifest. Measured at HEAD 2170ff8: Cargo.lock has toml_edit 0.22.27 (toml's parser) and ureq 2.12.1 (through glia-doc-sources) but no lz4_flex, blake3 or toml_write; ~/.cargo/registry has blake3-1.8.5 and toml_write-0.1.2 cached, lz4_flex is not (first fetch needs crates.io). projection-text depends on core, code-domain, graph and activation only (projection-text/Cargo.toml, read), so engine -> projection-text adds no cycle. James 2026-09-30: the shared-cache transport is CLI-only, so the HTTP client (ureq, CE.2e) and the object MAC's blake3 (CE.2c) go into cli/Cargo.toml; the engine keeps blake3 only for the content-addressed keys (CE.2a), and no HTTP crate enters engine/Cargo.toml or the glia-py wheel (measured at HEAD with `cargo tree --offline -e normal`: ureq in glia-cli's tree once, through glia-doc-sources; in glia-engine's and glia-py's 0 times).

packets.title: Go calls inside func literals (sync.Once.Do, go func, defer func, errgroup.Go, t.Run) are CALLS of the enclosing function; a func-literal ROUTE handler keeps LA.18d's HANDLED_BY and adds no CALLS to the function that registers it
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs collect_calls_in (:1235) recurses into every child EXCEPT a func_literal (`if child.kind() != "func_literal"`, :1268), so no call inside a closure becomes a CallSite. visit_function (:767) and visit_method (:806) run collect_calls_in BEFORE collect_routes_in (:2057), and Acc.func_literal_handlers (:259), the set of route-handler literals, is only filled by emit_route_from_call (:2516-2519) during the route walk, so at call-collection time the parser cannot tell a route handler literal from a goroutine.
MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8 (target/debug/glia, GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 analyze --format json on a git-archive copy of quokka-stack a77d4cb, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CA/quokka-stack): all 12 FUNCTIONs `turps::Services::repository_provider::*Repository` have 0 outgoing CALLS; each builds its repository inside `xOnce.Do(func() { ... })` (repository_provider.go:33-139). Handoff dev-notes/handoff-dogfood-quokka-lapse.md section 5 gap 1: with the 12 overlay `[[edge]]` stanzas that stand in for these calls (reproduced on /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CA/quokka-ov: `[overlay] edges ... declared=12 applied=12`), feature-flow sinks go 3 -> 53. quokka's Go source holds 16 `Once.Do(func`, 10 `go func(`, 5 `defer func(`, 3 `.Go(func` sites and 53 func literals outside `func` declaration lines.

packets.area: CA-2 Go receivers from a call's return type
packets.rationale:
Go records FIELD types only (collect_field_types, parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:510, LA.23c): no parameter, local, package-var or return type reaches the graph, so a method call on anything but `recv.field` has no receiver type. classify_call (:1274) turns a chained call into ComplexReceiver with the operand's RAW text (`Services.UserRepository()`, args included for `repositories.NewX(client, db)`), which resolve_calls drops (graph/src/calls.rs:217) and receiver_field (:736) rejects. go_type_name (:590) returns None for a generic instantiation, so quokka's `collection *Collection[models.User]` field (turps/Services/Repositories/*_repository.go) records no type. TYPE TEXT (one helper, `fn go_type_ref(node) -> Option<String>`): unwrap every pointer (`*T`), then type_identifier -> `T`; qualified_type -> `pkg.T` (the file's local import name kept, so the graph resolves it through that file's imports); generic_type -> its base (`Collection[T]` -> `Collection`, `repositories.Page[User]` -> `repositories.Page`); anything else (slice, map, chan, func, interface{}, struct{}) -> None. Predeclared names (error, string, bool, byte, rune, int*, uint*, float*, complex*, any, uintptr) -> None: they own no in-repo method.
1. CodeNav.return_types: FUNCTION / METHOD / interface METHOD id -> its FIRST result's go_type_ref (`func X() (*repositories.UserRepository, error)` -> `repositories.UserRepository`). A result naming one of the function's own type parameters (`func Get[T any]() T`) is not recorded. Build-time only like field_types: NOT mirrored into store::CodeNavStore (resolution is over before the .gmap is written), so no FORMAT_VERSION change.
2. Parameters: every parameter_declaration of a function / method (names grouped `a, b T` all get T; a variadic `...T` records "") -> record_local_type(fn_id, name, go_type_ref or ""). The method receiver is not recorded (SelfMethod / `self.` already cover it). A func_literal drained by CA.1's collect_closure_calls records its own parameters the same way under the enclosing fn (its calls are that fn's CallSites); a route-handler literal is never drained, so its `c *gin.Context` records nothing.
3. Locals, inside collect_calls_in's walk (so CA.1's closure bodies count for the enclosing fn): short_var_declaration `a, b := r1, r2` pairs by position; `x, err := f()` (one right-hand call, several names) binds the first name to the call's value text and records every other name as "". var_declaration / var_spec inside a body: declared type, else the value. range_clause and type-switch bound names record "" (unknown type, still shadowing a same-named field). VALUE -> TYPE TEXT (`fn go_value_type`): call_expression -> chain_text(call) (ends in `()`, the call's result type); composite_literal `T{..}` / `pkg.T{..}` and `&T{..}` -> go_type_ref(type); `new(T)` -> go_type_ref(T); anything else -> "". `_` is never recorded. record_local_type's existing rule (a second, different record -> "") handles a name rebound to another type.
4. Package-level vars: emit_state_var_spec records, BEFORE state_var_is_noise (so `var userRepo *repositories.X` without an initialiser counts), record_local_type(module_id, name, text) with the declared type or go_value_type(value): a MODULE scope in local_types holds that file's package-level vars (doc added to CodeNav.local_types). A package var assigned in init() to another concrete type than its declared initialiser is typed by the initialiser (Go static type rules make the declared / initial type the var's type, so the method set is right even when the dynamic type differs). Methods promoted from an embedded struct field are not followed (one declared-method table per type, as A6.2a). Go's root-package imports are not recorded by the parser (record_import returns on an empty repo-local path), so a chain through the repository-root package (grpc-go's `grpc.NewServer()`) stays unbound - a CB-side gap, see cross_group_deps. packets.implementation:
`fn go_signature(params: TsNode, result: Option<TsNode>, src) -> Option<String>` renders `(<p1>,<p2>,..)(<r1>,..)`: every parameter_declaration contributes its type once per name (`a, b int` -> `int,int`; an unnamed parameter its type once), a variadic_parameter_declaration `...T` contributes `...<T>`; the result is a parameter_list (same rule) or a single type (one entry) or absent (`()`). `fn type_shape(node, src) -> String` renders a type with every package qualifier dropped (qualified_type -> its name), all whitespace removed and `interface{}` written `any`, keeping pointer / slice / array / map / chan / func structure (`*mongo.Collection` -> `*Collection`, `map[string][]*pb.X` -> `map[string][]*X`, `func(context.Context) error` -> `func(Context)error`). Byte-level walk over the tree, no regex, UTF-8 safe (identifiers come from node text).
Qualifiers are dropped because the two sides are written in different packages: the interface `Build(PickerBuildInfo) Picker` in package base and its implementation `Build(base.PickerBuildInfo) balancer.Picker` elsewhere are the same signature. Two same-named types from different packages then compare equal: a missed rejection, never a false one.
Not recorded (unknown -> CA.3b keeps the pair as today): a method whose receiver type is generic (`func (c *Collection[T]) InsertOne(..)`, its T is a type parameter) and every method_elem of an interface with type_parameters.

packets.title: Go implicit IMPLEMENTS checks signatures and, for a one-method interface or a test-file side, package reachability; method-level pairs inherit the type-level edge's confidence (a Go pair is Medium, not Strong)

packets.rationale:
Root cause emit_go_implicit_implements (graph/src/build.rs:1071): a name-set match with no signature, package or test-scope check. grpc-go's test-file interface `Closable { Close() }` (internal/xds/bootstrap/tlscreds/bundle_ext_test.go:53) is implemented by every type with a `Close()`: MEASURED at HEAD on the grpc-go 6f50403 copy, `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 glia implementors <copy> internal::xds::bootstrap::tlscreds::bundle_ext_test::Closable --json` -> 89 results; `xds::bootstrap::bootstrap::Credentials` (Build + Name) -> 45 IMPLEMENTS, 41 of them balancer / logger builders whose Build has another signature. Closable 89 -> 8 (keeps bundle_test::failingProvider, the one same-package type); Credentials 45 -> 4 (the xds::bootstrap::credentials builders + bootstrap_test::testCredsBuilder); three spot-checked true pairs kept (xds::server::GRPCServer -> reflection ServiceInfoProvider via a shared importer, experimental::shared_buffer_pool_test::checkBufferPool -> mem::buffer_pool::BufferPool via the import closure, failingProvider -> Closable). The plan's 'test-file interfaces match test files only' rule was measured and rejected: it drops the same-directory prod types an external test legitimately checks (3 such pairs on grpc-go) and file-level imports alone lose checkBufferPool.
Second bug, graph/src/calls.rs emit_method_level_implements (:946): every method pair is pushed through push_edge (:987), always Confidence::Strong, even when the type-level edge is a Medium Go inference. MEASURED: `glia why bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/go-implicit-iface mem::MemStore store::Store` -> confidence medium, rule method_set; `... mem::MemStore::Get store::Store::Get` -> confidence strong, rule same_name.
Probe fixture go-iface-scope (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CA/fixtures/go-iface-scope) graded at HEAD: IMPLEMENTS recall 4/4, FORBID VIOLATIONS 5. Graph query run: repo-graph find `_node_matches_exact` (unrelated) - the iface code was read directly.

packets.implementation:
SET: today's `set: HashSet<(&str, Option<&str>)>` becomes `BTreeMap<(&str, Option<&str>), Option>`: each name with the interface METHOD that declares it (first in the embed walk; the predeclared `error` contributes `Error` with the constant signature `()(string)`). R1 SIGNATURE (every pair): for each (name, iface_method) take sig_i = nav.method_sigs[iface_method] and sig_t = nav.method_sigs[class_methods[ty][name]]; both known and different -> reject (stats.signature += 1). All known and equal -> the pair is `signature_checked` (evidence rule `method_signature`); any unknown -> kept on names as today (rule `method_set`). R2 REACHABILITY (only when the interface's set has exactly ONE method, or the type or the interface is declared in a `_test.go` file; multi-method pairs without a test side skip it). Let dt / di be the two package dirs (go_package_dir). Same dir -> keep. Otherwise build once per graph from GoPackages: `imports_of_file[m]` = the in-repo dirs file m imports (import_path through imported_dir), `imports_of_dir[d]` = their union over d's files, `importers_of_dir[d]`, and a memoised transitive closure. T-side start set = imports_of_file[T's file] when T is in a test file (a test file is never importable), else imports_of_dir[dt]; I-side likewise. Keep when (I is not in a test file AND di is in closure(T-side)) OR (T is not in a test file AND dt is in closure(I-side)) OR (neither is in a test file AND importers_of_dir[dt] and importers_of_dir[di] intersect: a wiring package imports both). Reject otherwise (stats.scope += 1, split one_method / test_side). Go never records an import OF the repository-root package (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs record_import returns on an empty repo-local path), so a dir `""` target counts as reached (stats.root_assumed += 1) rather than losing every root-package pair (grpc-go's root package is `grpc`). Why transitive: Go lets a file pass a T to a function whose parameter is I without importing I's package; experimental::shared_buffer_pool_test passes checkBufferPool into an API typed mem.BufferPool that way. Pairs are still collected, sorted and deduped before any push; closures are BTreeSets; every map is only probed. MARKERS: the pinned `[iface] go implicit implements: E (interfaces=I types=T embedded=M open=O)` line is unchanged in shape (E counts kept edges); a second line, once per Go graph with an INTERFACE: `[iface] go implicit filtered: signature= scope=

(one_method= test_side=) signature_checked= root_assumed=`. METHOD LEVEL (calls.rs): collect `(impl_mid, iface_mid, confidence_of_class_edge)`; sort by (a, b, rank) with Strong < Medium < Weak and keep the first per (a, b), so a pair reached through an explicit Strong edge stays Strong and a Go implicit pair is Medium; push with that confidence and evidence graph:iface same_name. Java / C# / TS / Kotlin (explicit Strong heritage) are unchanged. COVERAGE caveat (Go, IMPLEMENTS) becomes: 'implicit interface satisfaction is inferred (Medium, DERIVED) from method names and, where the parser read both, signatures (parameter and result types; package qualifiers, parameter names and a type alias are not resolved); a one-method interface, or a pair with a side in a _test.go file, pairs only across an import path (same package, a transitive import either way, or a package importing both); an import of the repository-root package is not recorded, so a root-package side is assumed reachable; a method on a generic type and an interface with type parameters are matched by name only; pointer and value receivers are merged; methods promoted through an embedded struct field are not seen; an interface embedding one that does not bind is skipped as open; constraint type terms are ignored'. implementors.rs doc: Go method pairs are now stored Medium, so the owner walk and the pair agree. TESTS (graph/src/build.rs mod tests, where build_go_passes' stats are reachable; FileParses hand-built with method_sigs filled, or parsed with glia_parser_go::parse_file, graph's normal dependency, where real signatures read better): go_implicit_signature_mismatch_is_rejected (Wrong{Get(int) int, Put(int,int)} vs Store{Get(string) string, Put(string,string)} -> no edge, signature=1); go_implicit_unknown_signature_keeps_the_name_match (no sigs -> today's edge, rule method_set); go_implicit_scope_one_method_needs_an_import_path (a::Closer{Close}, b::File{Close} with no import either way -> no edge; with b importing a -> edge); go_implicit_scope_test_interface (tests::x_test::Closable vs a prod type in another dir the test file does not reach -> no edge; a type in the same dir -> edge); go_implicit_scope_shared_importer (main imports both dirs -> edge); go_implicit_root_package_is_assumed_reached; go_method_level_pairs_inherit_medium (the go-implicit-iface shape: MemStore::Get -> Store::Get is Medium); the existing go_implicit_implements_requires_full_method_set marker assertion stays byte-equal; go_implicit_implements_is_deterministic filters type-level edges (from a STRUCT) before asserting its 16, and asserts the method-level pairs are Medium too. calls.rs test: a Java explicit `implements` pair stays Strong.

packets.rationale:
`.Collection(` is already a data-entity needle (parsers/code/extractors/src/data_entities.rs COLLECTION_NEEDLES :2298), but collection_arg (:2470) takes only a literal first argument, and quokka's only driver call is inside the generic constructor `func NewCollection[T any](client *mongo.Client, database, name string) *Collection[T] { return &Collection[T]{col: client.Database(database).Collection(name)} }` (turps/Services/Repositories/collection.go:19-20). The wrapper stage (engine/src/external/wrappers.rs, LF.2e / LG.3d) mints exactly the right nodes, but WrapperPass::scan (:298) returns None without a `.glia/overlay.toml` `[[wrapper]]` stanza (:304-306), and Stanza (:172) borrows its WrapperDecl from the loaded config, so no stanza can exist without the file.

packets.implementation: DESIGN: reuse the wrapper stage's site reader and minting unchanged; add only a stanza source. Alternatives weighed: (a) teach the data-entity extractor to follow a parameter to its callers - it runs per file on source text and never sees other files; (b) a graph-time pass - DATA_ENTITY nodes and the DbResolver pairing need the nodes in the parse before the graph build, which is exactly where the wrapper stage already mints them (post-cache graft, so cached parses get it too and the cache never holds an inferred node). This extends the existing LF.2e graft, not a new build pass, so no PassSpec is added. INFERENCE `infer_entity_wrappers(parses_by_lang, files, modules, repo) -> InferredWrappers { wrappers: Vec, skipped_ambiguous, skipped_unparsed }`, Go files only (detect_language == "go"): 1. DIRECT: for each Go file, `collection_param_calls(source)` gives (offset, ident) for every `.Collection(` call whose first argument is a bare identifier. Find the file's parse by its MODULE id (the mint path's lookup, modules.module_id), its owner at `anchor::line_of(source, offset)` via `anchor::build_owner_index` + `owner_of_line` (a FUNCTION or METHOD, else skip) and the owner's name (nav.name_by_id). The owner's declaration text is read from the walked SOURCE over the owner's POSITION line span (the OwnerIndex entry), not from its CODE cell, so CD.7c's CODE-span storage cannot change what is read. Parameter names: find `func`, an optional receiver `(..)`, the name, step over one `[..]` type-parameter list, take the balanced `(..)` (wrappers.rs's quote-aware `arg_region` / `split_args`); split on top-level commas; an item's first token is its name, a one-token item is a grouped name (`database, name string` -> [database, name]). The ident's index in that list is `name_arg`; not a parameter -> skip (a package const `.Collection(tableName)` mints nothing). No parsable list -> skipped_unparsed. 2. FORWARDING (depth 2..3): for an inferred wrapper W, a Go call site `W(..)` (call_hits over Go files) whose argument at W.name_arg is a bare identifier that is a parameter of the site's owner makes that owner a wrapper too, name_arg = its index (`NewNamedCollection(c, db, name)` forwarding into NewCollection). At most 3 depths, deduped by call name. 3. PRECISION: drop a wrapper whose `call` names two or more FUNCTION / METHOD nodes in the repo's Go parses, or is shorter than 3 characters (skipped_ambiguous). Every inferred stanza carries `languages = ["go"]`. 4. Output, sorted by (call, def file): `InferredWrapper { decl: WrapperDecl { call, kind: "data_entity", flavor: Some("nosql"), name_arg: Some(i), languages: vec!["go"], .. }, def_file, def_line0, depth }` (WrapperDecl is Clone; its `origin` is ignored for an inferred stanza, see 5). 5. WRAPPER STAGE: Stanza { decl: Cow<'c, WrapperDecl>, kind, source }. An overlay stanza keeps rule `wrapper#`, its Origin's confidence, ORIGIN `{"provenance":"overlay:","rule":"wrapper#"}` and emitter `overlay:wrapper` - byte-identical to today. An inferred stanza: rule `inferred:`, confidence Medium, node ORIGIN cell `{"provenance":"inferred:wrapper","rule":"inferred:","def":":<1-based line>"}`, edge EVIDENCE emitter `pass:inferred_wrapper` (stage `pass`, which why.rs tiers DERIVED), rule `inferred:`, at the site (basis site) through evidence::attach. An overlay stanza naming the same `call` shadows the inferred one (counted `shadowed_by_overlay`), so quokka's hand stanza keeps its exact output. Sites, definitions, comments, non-literals and invalid names go through the existing scan_file / read_site / read_args unchanged; minted nodes and edges have LG.3d's shape, so DbResolver / SHARES_DATA_ENTITY pair them. 6. grafts.rs: `let inferred = crate::external::infer_entity_wrappers(parses_by_lang, files, &modules, repo);` then `WrapperPass::scan(wrappers, inferred.wrappers, files, parse_errors)` - inference runs under `--no-overlay` too (it is code-derived, not overlay). Mint phases unchanged (data_entity mints in the Queue half). 7. MARKER, once per repo with an inferred wrapper: `[wrappers] inferred repo=

Precision: only a DIRECT hand-over of a parameter into a known driver needle creates a wrapper, and a name defined twice (or shorter than 3 characters) is dropped; a wrapper with a very common name that IS unique (e.g. a single `get`) could mint from unrelated `x.get("...")` calls in the same language - the 3-character floor and the Go-only stanza bound it, and the marker counts every site. Determinism: wrappers sorted by (call, def file); files walked in the walked order; stanzas in a fixed order (overlay first, then inferred). The inferred ORIGIN/EVIDENCE strings are new values - a consumer with a closed provenance list needs one entry. Panics: infer runs per file under the stage's existing catch_unwind pattern (`<path>: PANIC (inferred wrappers)`). PARSER_STAMP moves (engine, parsers/code/extractors). packets.implementation:
`fn record_local_types(fun: TsNode, body: TsNode, from: NodeId, file: &File, acc: &mut Acc)`:
- each `parameter` of `function_value_parameters`: its `user_type` / `nullable_type` through field_type_name (a generic, value or non-injectable type -> "") -> `acc.nav.record_local_type(from, name, ty)`;
- each `variable_declaration` in the body (the walk skips nested class / object declarations like local_names): a declared type -> field_type_name; else its initializer (the `property_declaration`'s expression): a call_expression whose head is an `identifier` with an upper-case first letter (Kotlin constructor call, `AuditLog()`) -> that name; a bare identifier or `this.x` naming a property of the enclosing type -> `self.<x>` (LA.35a's alias form, so `val repo = repo` keeps binding through the field); anything else -> "" (a local of unknown type shadows a same-named field, LA.35a semantics). A variable_declaration with neither a declared type nor a property_declaration initializer (a lambda parameter `{ x -> .. }`, a `for (x in xs)` variable, a destructuring component) records "": it is a local of unknown type, never a typed receiver.
record_local_type's rule (a second, different type for one name -> "") handles shadowing. Nothing in graph/ changes: the JVM family builds through build_dotted, whose resolve_calls reads the caller's locals first (receiver_type), then resolve_type_name through the Kotlin file's import bindings (`import com.acme.store.ItemStore`), then the method table.
Marker in trace(): `[kotlin] local types: scopes=<S> typed=<T> unknown=<U> repo=<label>` (S = function scopes with a local, T / U = entries with a type / with ""), after the `[kotlin] refs:` line.
Coverage caveat rewrite: 'Kotlin calls are extracted from declared function bodies; a call on a variable binds when the variable is a typed property, a typed parameter, a typed `val` / `var` or one initialised by a constructor call (`val r = Repo()`); a local initialised any other way, a lambda parameter, bare calls in an INTERFACE default method, inherited methods called bare, calls inside a lambda with receiver (`with(x) { m() }`, `apply { }`), calls outside a function body (init blocks, secondary-constructor bodies, property initializers / accessors, default argument values) and a same-package call into another file with no import stay unresolved'. Test kotlin_reports_as_blind_spot: `note("CALLS").contains("parameter-typed receiver")` becomes `contains("typed parameter")` and `contains("lambda parameter")`.
Tests (parsers/code/kotlin/src/calls.rs): params_and_vals_record_local_types - the fixture's service.kt: listAll's locals {store: ItemStore}, audited {log: AuditLog}, inferred {log: AuditLog}, shadowed {store: ItemStore, log: ""}; alias_of_a_property_is_self - `class S(private val repo: Repo) { fun f() { val r = repo; r.x() } }` -> {r: `self.repo`}; generic_param_is_unknown - `fun f(xs: List<Item>)` -> {xs: ""}; the existing a_local_shadows_the_member test stays green.

GATE: `android::imports_ktor_client(acc)` is true when an import of the file (acc.imports, the `imports_android` pattern: ImportTarget::Symbol.module / ImportTarget::Module.path) starts with `io::ktor::client` (the Ktor client artifact namespace; the server DSL lives in io.ktor.server). No new File field: acc.imports is complete before any body is walked. Without it, nothing fires - a Javalin `app.get("/x", h)`, a Map `get`, a Ktor server route are all outside the gate. Inside the gate a call fires only with a receiver (the head is a navigation_expression): the server DSL's `get("/x") { }` is receiver-less and stays a ROUTE (routes::ktor_call).
VERB (`fn ktor_verb(name)`): get / post / put / delete / patch / head / options -> the upper-case verb; prepareGet .. prepareOptions -> the same; `request` / `prepareRequest` -> the trailing lambda's `method = HttpMethod.<X>` statement (endpoint::http_method_ref_verb on its right side), else GET (Ktor's default). URL: the first positional argument via android::client_url (a literal -> Strong, a `$x` / `${x}` template or `+` concatenation -> Medium with `${…}` placeholders), split by endpoint::client_url_split; a path not starting with `/` after the authority split emits nothing (the Spring rule). The builder form `client.get { url("..") }` has no positional URL and emits nothing (stated in the caveat).
EMIT: android::emit_client_endpoint(call, verb, path, host, strong, ctx.from, file, acc) - the ENDPOINT node, ENDPOINT_HIT cell and the CALLS edge from the enclosing function, deduped per file by seen_endpoints; acc.clients.ktor_clients += 1.

PRINCIPLE: timings go to stderr only; nothing reaches FileParse, the parse cache, the .gmap, the manifest, stdout or any answer, so byte_identical and every JSON / text output are untouched.
activation (domain-free, build-time): PassRegistry::run wraps `(spec.run)(g, ctx)` in `let t = Instant::now(); .. let d = t.elapsed();`, adds d to `report.elapsed[stage as usize]` and pushes `(spec.name, d)` onto pass_elapsed. PassReport is #[non_exhaustive] (additive); its derived PartialEq still compiles (Duration: Eq) and nothing compares reports (`grep PassReport` finds only activation/src and the engine call). DomainProfile::run_passes' `[passes]` line is unchanged.
engine/src/build/timing.rs: `pub(crate) struct PhaseTimes { walk, parse, const_scan, grafts, language_build: Duration }` with `fn repo_marker(&self, label) -> String` = `[timing] repo=<label> walk=<ms> parse=<ms> const_scan=<ms> grafts=<ms> language_build=<ms>`; `pub(crate) struct BuildTimes { repos: usize, report: PassReport-derived stage times, external_cells: Duration, total: Duration, slowest: Option<(&'static str, Duration)> }` with `fn marker()` = `[timing] build repos=<n> resolve=<ms> post=<ms> finalize=<ms> external_cells=<ms> total=<ms> slowest_pass=<name>:<ms>`; `fn ms(d) -> String` = milliseconds with one decimal (`12.3ms`). Pure formatters, unit-tested with fixed Durations.
Wiring: generate_one_inner times walk_source_files and takes PhaseTimes from build_graphs_for_repo, prints the repo line after the repo's graphs are built; times run_code_passes_with (keeping its PassReport) and apply_external_cells; total = Instant at function entry -> just before Ok; prints the build line. assemble_many_with: the par_map_ordered walk closure returns (root, walk, ident, walk_time), the per-repo line prints after each repo's build (argument order); generate_many_inner prints the build line. merge.rs (run_code_passes tail of a layout merge) prints `[timing] build repos=<n> ..` with walk / parse absent (it only runs passes). persist_graph / persist_layout: `[timing] persist writer=<w> <ms> dir=<dir>` around the write (orphan cleanup included in persist_graph).
Phases inside a repo run on the engine pool; each timer measures wall time of the phase call on the orchestrating thread, so the numbers are what a user waits for (not CPU sums).

packets.title: Contract YAML sniff scans every indent-0 line and requires a version value on `openapi:` / `swagger:` / `asyncapi:`
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/extractors/src/contracts.rs `const SNIFF_LINES: usize = 64` bounds both sniff() (`source.lines().take(SNIFF_LINES)`) and asyncapi_major(). swaggo (the dominant Go OpenAPI generator) writes docs/swagger.yaml by converting its JSON through ghodss/yaml, which sorts keys alphabetically: basePath, definitions (every model), host, info, paths, ... and `swagger: "2.0"` LAST. Any API with more than a handful of models pushes the marker past line 64 and the file declares nothing. New fixture contract-openapi-swaggo-yaml (110-line alphabetical swagger.yaml + the gin routes it documents) graded on HEAD 2170ff8: nodes 0/2, edges 0/2, no `[contract]` line. The same file with `swagger: "2.0"` moved to line 1 (scratch copy) yields DOC_SECTION contract::docs::swagger::GET:/api/orders and ::GET:/api/orders/{id}, 2 DOCUMENTS edges, `[contract] files=1 ops=2 (openapi=2 ...)`, `[contract-link] ops=2 exact=2`. LB.12 names a yaml op by its file (dir_stem_qname), so a swaggo swagger.yaml and its swagger.json twin in the same dir merge onto the same DOC_SECTION ids - no new identities.
Scanning the whole file removes the only thing that kept an application config's `swagger:` section (Spring Boot application.yml: `swagger:
  enabled: true`) from sniffing as a contract when it sits past line 64, so the marker must carry a version: a scalar value starting with a digit, quotes stripped.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): SNIFF_LINES (:179), sniff (:284) and asyncapi_major (:486) re-read; grade.py on the draft fixture: nodes 0/2, edges 0/2, forbid 1/1 OK. Moving `swagger: "2.0"` to line 1 in a scratch copy grades nodes 2/2, edges 2/2 with `[contract] files=1 ops=2 (openapi=2 asyncapi=0 pact=0 feature_yaml=0) collided=0` and `[contract-link] ops=2 exact=2`. The version rule also removes a HEAD false positive the draft called unmeasured: the fixture's config/application.yml with its `swagger:
  enabled: true
paths:
  /internal: ...` block moved to line 1 (scratch copy) grades FORBID VIOLATIONS 1 on HEAD - DOC_SECTION contract::config::application::GET:/internal, `[contract] files=1 ops=1`. So a config yaml with an indent-0 versionless `swagger:` / `openapi:` / `asyncapi:` key and a `paths:` / `channels:` block in its first 64 lines mints a contract op today; after this packet it mints nothing (declared edge_removal). Every contract yaml in bench and every contracts.rs test puts a literal version on the marker line (grep `^(openapi|swagger|asyncapi):`), so none moves.

parsers/code/extractors/src/contracts.rs:284 sniff - every indent-0 non-skippable line; a marker counts only when its value is a version (new private fn version_value)
parsers/code/extractors/src/contracts.rs asyncapi_major - reads the `asyncapi:` key on every indent-0 line, same version rule
parsers/code/extractors/src/contracts.rs #[cfg(test)] - four new tests

packets.implementation:
1. Delete SNIFF_LINES. sniff(source): iterate `source.lines()`; skip is_skippable lines and any line with indent_of != 0; on the first indent-0 line whose key (split_key) is `openapi` / `swagger` / `asyncapi` AND whose value passes version_value, return the Sniffed kind; keep scanning otherwise (a document's key order is not its meaning). Still allocation-free and one pass; a non-contract yaml pays one line walk (the extractor already walks the whole file for feature_dir / scan_openapi when it sniffs).
2. `fn version_value(v: &str) -> bool`: trim, strip one pair of matching `"` / `'`, then true iff the first char is an ASCII digit (`2.0`, `3.0.3`, `"3.1.0"`, `'2.6.0'`). An empty value (a map key: `swagger:` followed by an indented block), `true`, `~` or text is not a marker.
3. asyncapi_major: `lines.iter().find_map(..)` over every line (no take), same indent-0 + version rule; unchanged result for every existing test.
4. Tests: swaggo_alphabetical_swagger_yaml_is_sniffed (the fixture's docs/swagger.yaml text -> Sniffed::OpenApi and scan_openapi returns 2 ops with basePath /api; HEAD: None); a_config_swagger_map_key_is_not_a_contract (application.yml with `swagger:\n  enabled: true` at line 76 and a `paths:` block -> None; also None when that block is at line 1: the version rule, not the line count, now decides); asyncapi_marker_after_line_64 (an AsyncAPI 2.6.0 doc whose `asyncapi: 2.6.0` follows 70 lines of `x-` extensions -> AsyncApi with its channel ops); a_quoted_version_counts (`openapi: '3.0.3'`). Every existing contracts.rs test stays green unchanged (they all put a version on the marker line).

packets.title: Event sides read a real name or mint nothing: no more verb-named EVENT_* (`Subject.next`, `emit`, `@OnEvent`, `eventBridge.putEvents`, `handle_event`); a constant-keyed site is keyed by its constant path, which CB.3b folds to the constant's literal
packets.area: CB-g verb-fallback event nodes (extractor half; CB.3b resolves constants)
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs event_name_at returns verb_name(pattern) whenever the needle has extract_name == false (EventBridge.putEvents / eventBridge.putEvents / handle_event) or no quoted literal follows (LiteralAt::Absent). Those nodes name the API, not an event: every file's `emit(x)` is `event_emit:emit`, every RxJS subject is `event_emit:Subject.next`, and verb-named emitters and handlers never pair with each other (the key `emit` is not the key `@OnEvent`), so they are orphan entry points (repo-graph server.py lists event_handler in _ENTRY_KINDS).
New fixture event-verb-fallback graded on HEAD 2170ff8: nodes 0/4, edges 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 5 - event_emit:Subject.next (RxJS), event_emit:emit and event_handle:@OnEvent (a NestJS pair keyed by the constant `OrderEvents.Created`, which do not pair), event_emit:eventBridge.putEvents (whose DetailType is `OrderPlaced`), event_handle:handle_event (Phoenix LiveView `def handle_event("inc", ...)`). Real repos, debug CLI json on git-archive copies: quokka-stack mints `event_emit:Subject.next @quokka_web`; lapse and repo-graph mint no EVENT_* (LA.29 / LA.39 / LA.41 already removed the others).
The fix is one rule for every string needle: a quoted literal (unchanged, LA.41), else a CONSTANT REFERENCE argument (`OrderEvents.Created`, `Events::ORDER_PLACED`, `ORDER_PLACED`) - the name both sides of a constant-keyed bus share - else nothing. Two needles get a needle-specific real name: EventBridge.putEvents reads its entry's `DetailType` literal, LiveView `def handle_event(` reads its first-argument literal.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): EMITTER_PATTERNS / HANDLER_PATTERNS (:33 / :44; `EventBridge.putEvents`, `eventBridge.putEvents`, `handle_event` are the three extract_name=false rows), event_name_at (:469), verb_name (:481) and find_gated (:661) re-read. grade.py on the draft fixture: nodes 0/4, edges 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 5 (all five verb nodes minted). quokka-stack (debug CLI json of a git-archive copy): exactly two EVENT_* nodes, `event_emit:DISCONNECTED @quokka_web` and `event_emit:Subject.next @quokka_web`. No key.json expect row names a verb event (the verb names appear only in forbid rows: event-publish-precision, event-name-shape, event-verb-receivers, matrix broker probes); no engine / graph test names one. In-file tests that change: transport_needles_mark_their_nodes (:2132) asserts `event_emit:eventBridge.putEvents` for `putEvents({ Entries: [] })` - it becomes `[]` (no DetailType) plus a DetailType case. graph/src/resolvers/eventbus.rs normalise_event_key's doc still lists the tag fallbacks; it is fixed here because this packet makes it stale.
SPLIT (James 2026-09-30, 0.5.1 decision 3): an event keyed by a constant must be keyed by the constant's RESOLVED LITERAL through the engine's repo const table, falling back to the constant path, so there is no second identity change later. Resolution reads other files, so it cannot live in this per-file, cached extractor (parsers/code/extractors/src/constants.rs CACHE RULE: parsers extract, the engine resolves). This packet keys a constant site by its constant path - the fallback identity - and CB.3b folds it post-cache in engine/src/build/grafts.rs, the seam LA.4 already uses for queue topics. CB.3a never ships in a release without CB.3b.

packets.title: A decorated TypeScript method's POSITION and CODE start at its first decorator, so decorator-line markers anchor to the method; GraphQL root nouns anchor at their class line
packets.rationale:
tree-sitter-typescript 0.23 puts a method's decorators in class_body BESIDE the method_definition (`seq(repeat(field('decorator', $.decorator)), $.method_definition)`), so parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs build_cells / position_json give a decorated method a span that starts at its name. The A5.8 anchor pass (parsers/code/extractors/src/anchor.rs attach) owns a marker by the method span holding the marker's line; a decorator-line marker (NestJS `@OnEvent(...)`, `@EventPattern(...)`, `@MessagePattern(...)`, Bull `@Process(...)`) lies outside every span and falls back to the module CONTAINS edge. Java includes its annotations (they sit inside method_declaration's modifiers).
New fixture ts-decorator-anchor graded on HEAD 2170ff8: edges 2/3, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1 (CONTAINS src::orders.gateway -> event_handle:order.shipped), POSITION cell start_line 9 (the name row, not the decorator row 8); debug CLI `[marker-anchor] 1 anchored to methods, 2 to module`. Also on HEAD: rpc-event-monorepo-owner's `@EventPattern("orderShipped")` handler is `CONTAINS services::notify::listener -> event_handle:orderShipped @services/notify` (debug CLI, scratch copy), and fixtures/event-name-shape pins the fallback as its expected edge.
Widening the span needs one guard: parsers/code/extractors/src/graphql.rs ts_root_decorators anchors the type-level root noun (`graphql_resolver:Query`) at the `@Query(` decorator line of the first field method; once that line is inside the method span the root noun would become HANDLED_BY a field method. It moves to its class declaration line (inside the class, outside every method), keeping today's module CONTAINS.
DECIDED (James 2026-09-30): widen the span, a declared cell_value break. In TypeScript a decorator is part of its class element (the grammar merely puts it beside method_definition), POSITION / CODE are what locate, read and blast radius slice, and a route or event decorator is the part of a NestJS handler a reader most needs. It is a TypeScript rule, not a cross-language one: the premise that Python already includes decorators is FALSE - verifier probe (probe/CB/verify/p_pydeco, installed wheel): a Python method decorated on rows 4-5 has POSITION start_line 6 (parsers/code/python/src/lib.rs hands visit_method the inner function_definition of the decorated_definition), so the Python twin is listed as a gap.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): grade.py on the draft fixture: edges 2/3, cells 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1, `[marker-anchor] 1 anchored to methods, 2 to module`; the TS method arm is `"method_definition" => visit_method(..)` (:338) and visit_method builds its cells with build_cells(&n, ..) packets.title: In-process events pair across nested projects that link into one process: a project dependency closure (manifest DEPENDS_ON -> nested PROJECT) feeds the eventbus owner rule
packets.area: CB-f in-process events across one-process projects
packets.rationale:
graph/src/resolvers/eventbus.rs pairing() (LB.8b) keeps an emitter / handler pair only for the same owner, an unowned side or a transport side; two different owners on in-process buses are dropped. That is right for two deployable services and wrong for a library project linked into an app: a workspace lib's EventEmitter2 emit and the app's @OnEvent handler run in ONE process. New fixture event-monorepo-process (npm workspaces: apps/api depends on @shop/orders = libs/orders; services/billing does not) graded on HEAD 2170ff8: edges 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0; debug CLI `[eventbus-owner] same-owner=0 unowned-side=0 transport=0 cross-owner-dropped=2`. The graph already holds the link: `DEPENDS_ON apps::api::package.json -> package:npm:@shop/orders` (packages.rs extract_for_path) and the nested PROJECT `project:libs/orders` whose ORIGIN names `"label":"@shop/orders"` (walk.rs project_roots). graph/src/resolvers/package.rs pairs same-qname PACKAGE_DEPs across repos only; nothing maps a dependency onto an in-repo project. PACKAGE_DEP ecosystems (npm, pypi, cargo, gomod, rubygems, composer - packages.rs) differ from PROJECT ecosystems (npm, go, python, ...), so the match goes through the project's manifest basename.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): pairing (:98) and the Pairing enum (:87) re-read; debug CLI on the draft fixture: `[roots] 4 project roots (npm=4)`, `[eventbus-owner] same-owner=0 unowned-side=0 transport=0 cross-owner-dropped=2`, DEPENDS_ON `apps::api::package.json -> package:npm:@shop/orders`, PROJECT `project:libs/orders` named `@shop/orders`. Two draft errors fixed: (1) a manifest MODULE carries NO cells (engine/src/route.rs synthetic_parse is called with `module_cells = vec![]` for the manifest branch), so the depender project is matched by qname - the manifest MODULE's qname is extract.rs synthetic_module_qname (the path with `/` read as `::`: `apps::api::package.json`), which equals the PROJECT ORIGIN's repo-relative `manifest` with `/` read as `::`; (2) engine/tests/channel_owner_rpc_event.rs monorepo_markers_count_every_side_and_pair (:275-291) asserts the exact line `[eventbus-owner] same-owner=2 unowned-side=2 transport=1 cross-owner-dropped=2`, so the new field moves that assert in the same commit (rpc-event-monorepo-owner's service manifests declare no dependencies: same-process=0).

packets.implementation:
1. PROJECT TABLE (per graph, graph order): every PROJECT node's ORIGIN cell (JSON, read with a local substring field reader like eventbus.rs is_transport - the graph crate has no serde_json): `path` (the owner string LB.4a uses; skip "" / "."), `label`, `manifest`. Map the manifest basename to the PACKAGE_DEP ecosystem: package.json -> npm, go.mod -> gomod, Cargo.toml -> cargo, pyproject.toml | setup.cfg | setup.py -> pypi, composer.json -> composer, Gemfile | *.gemspec -> rubygems; others skipped. Index `(repo, eco, normalised label) -> path`, where pypi names are PEP 503-normalised (lowercase, runs of `-_.` -> `-`) and every other ecosystem compares exactly.
2. EDGES: for every DEPENDS_ON edge (intra-graph, graph order) whose `to` is a PACKAGE_DEP with qname `package:<eco>:<name>`: the depender project = the project whose ORIGIN `manifest`, with `/` read as `::`, equals the from-MODULE's qname (a manifest MODULE has no cells; its qname is engine extract.rs synthetic_module_qname of the manifest path, e.g. `apps::api::package.json`); the dependee = the index hit for (repo, eco, name). A self-edge is dropped. links[(repo, depender)] gets dependee.
3. CLOSURE: reach(p) = p plus every project reachable over links (BFS over the BTreeMap, visited set; the table is tens of projects, so this is a local walk, not a general algorithm - it stays out of activation::algo, which works over GraphSource node ids, while this is keyed by owner strings). shares_process(repo, a, b) = exists project p in the repo's table with a in reach(p) and b in reach(p). Precomputed once per resolve: `process_of: BTreeMap<(RepoId, String), BTreeSet<String>>` = for each project, the set of root projects whose reach contains it; shares_process is a non-empty intersection.
4. pairing(e, h, closure): unchanged arms first (SameOwner, UnownedSide, Transport); then `(Some(a), Some(b)) if e.repo == h.repo && closure.shares_process(e.repo, a, b) => Pairing::SameProcess`; else Dropped. The closure is built on first need (the first candidate the old rule drops), so a build whose owned pairs are all same-owner pays nothing. The EVIDENCE rule of a SameProcess edge is `same_process` (RuleTally::new("eventbus", &["exact", "folded", "same_process"])); the exact / folded key counters still count it, so `[eventbus] <n> pairs (exact= type-folded=)` counts every pushed edge. Confidence weakest of the two sides as today.
5. MARKER: `[eventbus-owner] same-owner=<n> unowned-side=<n> transport=<n> same-process=<n> cross-owner-dropped=<n>` (the new field before `cross-owner-dropped`, which keeps the line's tail stable for grep).
6. TESTS: a_library_emit_reaches_its_app_handler (apps/api depends on libs/orders -> SameProcess); a_sibling_service_stays_dropped (services/billing, no dependency -> Dropped); two_libs_linked_into_one_app_share_it (apps/api depends on libs/a and libs/b; emitter in a, handler in b -> SameProcess); transitive_dependency (app -> lib1 -> lib2); pypi_name_normalisation (`My_Lib` dependency vs project label `my-lib`). The existing LB.8b tests stay green (their fixtures carry no workspace dependency); engine/tests/channel_owner_rpc_event.rs monorepo_markers_count_every_side_and_pair's expected line becomes `[eventbus-owner] same-owner=2 unowned-side=2 transport=1 same-process=0 cross-owner-dropped=2`.

A `declaration` child (a bodiless member: `Money load();` in an abstract class, `const Money(this.cents);`, a redirecting factory) is ignored entirely, and visit_enum keeps enum constants only as names for LA.34's member set.
New fixture dart-members graded on HEAD 2170ff8: nodes 0/8, edges 0/5, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1 - the only edge out of the class is `CALLS lib::src::money::Money -> round2` (the operator body's call credited to the CLASS); `Money.zero()` / `Money.parse('1')` from `total()` resolve to nothing (no such member); `validate()` from the constructor body is lost.
QNAME DECISION (declared break for the class-level CALLS): the unnamed constructor (and an unnamed factory) is METHOD `<Class>::<Class>` - the Java / C# constructor qname (their parsers name a constructor_declaration by its name, the class name); a named constructor or factory `C.name` is METHOD `<Class>::name` - Dart calls it `C.name(...)`, so resolve_attribute_target binds it through class_methods exactly like a static method, and Dart forbids a static member and a named constructor sharing a name; an operator is METHOD `<Class>::operator<op>` with the operator token verbatim and no space (`operator+`, `operator==`, `operator[]`, `operator[]=`, `operator~/`), the C++ spelling. packets.title: Swift: calls inside infix expressions (`a + f(x)`), init / deinit / subscript / computed-property bodies as METHODs, stored-property field types, and `@testable import` read from the AST
packets.rationale:

S2 - tree-sitter-swift 0.7.3 parses `1 + tax(3)` as call_expression(additive_expression(lhs=1, rhs=tax), call_suffix); classify_call takes `n.named_child(0)` (the additive_expression) and falls to the whole-callee ComplexReceiver arm, so the call is lost (probe: no CALLS to tax from `let base = 1 + tax(3)`).
S3 - visit_type's body loop matches only function_declaration and class_declaration; class_body also holds init_declaration, deinit_declaration, subscript_declaration and property_declaration (node-types.json), so initialisers, deinitialisers, subscripts and computed properties mint no node and their calls vanish (probe: no Cart::init / deinit / subscript / total, no CALLS to reset / scale / tax from them).
S4 - no field type is recorded (the Swift parser calls no record_field_type), so graph/src/calls.rs's A6.2a receiver pass cannot type `self.repo.load()` (a ComplexReceiver `self.repo`).
S6 - collect_import trims the text `@testable import App` with trim_start_matches("import "), which does not match, so the import path is the whole text: the file's IMPORTS cell reads ["@testable import App","XCTest"] (wheel node_cells on probe swift1).

SCOPE: the draft also recorded parameter and `let` local types - that is beyond S4 ("field types"; Kotlin's parameter / val types are a separate item, CA-6) and moves to the group's gap list. packets.implementation:
1. S2 classify_call: `let mut f = func_node; while BINARY.contains(&f.kind()) { match f.child_by_field_name("rhs") { Some(r) => f = r, None => break } }` then classify f. The stack walk in collect_calls_in already descends into the lhs, so `f(x) + g(y)` yields both calls (the lhs call_expression is its own node).
2. S3 members (qnames under the type, METHOD kind, DEFINES from the type, POSITION / CODE of the declaration, calls collected from the member):
   - init_declaration -> `<Type>::init` (every overload one node: cells stack, the Acc's existing per-file dedup rule for types applies to members through a declared-ids set);
   - deinit_declaration -> `<Type>::deinit`;
   - subscript_declaration -> `<Type>::subscript`; its computed_property child's statements / getter / setter blocks are the body;
   - property_declaration with a `computed_value` (computed_property: getter / setter / modify / statements) or a willset_didset_block -> `<Type>::<name>`, and the id goes into FileParse.properties (Kotlin `val x get()` / Python @property precedent: read as `x`, not `x()`). A stored property with neither mints no node (S4 records its type instead).
   The same arms apply inside an extension body (visit_type already folds `extension T`).
3. S4 field types: for a stored property_declaration in a type body with a type_annotation, record_field_type(type_id, name, simple type) - the annotation's type text with generic arguments, `?` / `!` and module qualifiers stripped (`[Int]` / `[K: V]` / tuples / closures record nothing); with no annotation but a `value` that is a call whose callee is a Capitalised simple_identifier (`= Repo()`), that identifier. Parameters and body locals record nothing (out of this item; see the group's gap list).
4. S6 collect_import: path = text of the first `identifier` named child (tree-sitter-swift import_declaration children: identifier, modifiers). `@testable import App` -> `App`; `import struct Foundation.Date` -> `Foundation.Date` (the identifier child; the kind keyword is anonymous).

TESTS: infix_callee_is_its_rhs (`let b = 1 + tax(3)` -> Bare(tax)); nested_infix (`a + b * f(x)` -> Bare(f)); init_deinit_subscript_are_methods (each owns its `self.x()` SelfMethod call); computed_property_is_a_property_method (in FileParse.properties); stored_property_records_its_type (`let repo: Repo`, `var s = Service()`); testable_import_path (`@testable import App` -> Module{path: "App"}); extension_members_hang_on_the_type (init in `extension Cart`).

packets.title: Python GraphQL field resolvers: strawberry `@strawberry.field` methods and attributes and graphene `x = graphene.Field(..)` / `resolve_x` pairs are GRAPHQL_RESOLVERs named by their schema field (camelCase by default)
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/extractors/src/graphql.rs decorator_scan reads Python root CLASSES only (py_root_classes, ~:753: `@strawberry.type class Query`, graphene `class Query(ObjectType)`) and reads field methods only for the TypeScript family (decorator_method_names). New fixture py-graphene-fields graded on HEAD: nodes 0/2, edges 0/2.
CAMELCASE DECISION (the matrix probe's key deferred it: "both spellings are forbidden because the future extractor's choice is not yet made"): a Python field resolver is minted under its SCHEMA name. strawberry (StrawberryConfig.auto_camel_case) and graphene (Schema auto_camelcase) both camelCase by default, the SDL scan mints the schema name for the same field, and gql_key lowercases before matching, so the snake spelling (`current_user` -> key `current_user`) could never pair with a client's `currentUser` (key `currentuser`). An explicit `name=".."` wins; a file that sets `auto_camel_case=False` / `auto_camelcase=False` keeps the Python name.

1. BLOCKS: for each root class py_root_classes found (Query / Mutation / Subscription, strawberry or graphene), its body is the following lines indented deeper than the `class` line, up to the first non-blank line at or above the class's indent.
2. STRAWBERRY (lib == Strawberry): inside a block, a line starting (trimmed) with `@strawberry.field`, `@strawberry.mutation` or `@strawberry.subscription` (bare or called; `name="x"` read from the call's text with a quoted-literal scan) followed - past further decorators and blank lines - by `def <ident>(` or `async def <ident>(` -> field; anchor line = that `def` line: the Python parser's method POSITION starts at `def`, NOT at its decorators (verifier probe p_pydeco: decorators on rows 4-5, POSITION start_line 6), so a decorator-line anchor would fall outside the method span and take the module CONTAINS fallback. An attribute `<ident>: <T> = strawberry.field(...)` / `strawberry.mutation(...)` -> field, anchor = that line.
3. GRAPHENE (lib == Graphene): inside a block, `<ident> = graphene.<Type>(` or `<ident> = <Type>(` where Type is a graphene field type (Field, List, NonNull, String, Int, Float, Boolean, ID, JSONString, DateTime, and `<X>.Field(` for a Mutation class) -> field (`name=` kwarg honoured); anchor = the `def resolve_<ident>(` line of the same block when present (so HANDLED_BY lands on the resolver method), else the attribute line (module / class fallback).
4. NAMES: schema_name = explicit name, else camel_case(py_name) unless the file (any line) contains `auto_camel_case=False` or `auto_camelcase=False`. camel_case: split on `_`, drop empty parts, first part as written, later parts with the first char uppercased (`current_user` -> `currentUser`, `user_by_id` -> `userById`, `_private` -> `private` is NOT produced: a leading underscore keeps the name verbatim - graphene / strawberry keep it too).

packets.title: A namespace PACKAGE shared by several files keeps its FIRST file as nav parent, and every member resolves calls against its OWN file's `use` / `using` bindings (a per-node home-module table)
packets.rationale:
graph/src/build.rs merge_nav does `dst.parent_of.extend(src.parent_of)`, so a PACKAGE id that several parses emit (a C# `namespace Shop.Orders` or a braced PHP `namespace App\Orders { }` opened in two files) takes the LAST merged file as its nav parent. graph/src/calls.rs enclosing_module (:686) walks parent_of from a call's `from` up to the first MODULE, so a method of a class in that namespace resolves its calls against the last file's module_import_bindings - the wrong file's `use` / `using` statements. New fixture php-shared-namespace-bindings graded on HEAD 2170ff8 (three runs, identical): edges 1/2 - `CALLS App::Orders::ShipmentService::ship -> App::Billing::Ledger::issue` exists, `OrderService::place -> Invoicer::issue` does not (OrderService.php's `use App\Billing\Invoicer` is never consulted: its class's enclosing module is ShipmentService.php). Also: the PACKAGE's nav parent disagrees with its first POSITION cell (append_cells keeps the first file's POSITION first), so locate / arch place it in the first file while nav hangs it under the last.
C# has the same nav shape (probe cs1: `CONTAINS Orders::OrderService -> Shop::Orders` and `CONTAINS Orders::ShipmentService -> Shop::Orders`); its `using Shop.Billing;` binds only the package name today, so the misresolution is observable in PHP.

packets.implementation:
1. home_module: in merge_parses, before merging a parse, find its file MODULE (the node the parse records with kind MODULE and no nav parent; every code parser records exactly one) and, for every non-PACKAGE node of the parse whose PARSE-LOCAL parent chain reaches a PACKAGE before a MODULE, insert home_module[node] = module (first insert wins). Every such node gets its own entry, not only a PACKAGE's direct children: a C# partial class opened in two files is one CLASS id (first file wins), and a METHOD declared in the second file must still resolve through the second file's `using`s - its own entry is found first by the walk.
2. enclosing_home_module(g, id): `let mut cur = id; loop (bounded by nav size) { if let Some(m) = g.symbols.home_module.get(&cur) { return Some(*m) } if kind(cur) == MODULE { return Some(cur) } cur = parent_of(cur)? }`. For every language that emits no shared PACKAGE (Python, TS, Go, Rust, Java, ...) home_module is empty or its entries equal what the walk finds, so their resolution is unchanged.
3. resolve_calls uses enclosing_home_module for from_module (the bindings lookup and bare_call_target's module symbol). enclosing_package (the PackageSymbol branch) keeps walking parent_of: a namespace-level symbol is shared by design. CppCallScope and the Go / Rust hooks keep calling enclosing_module on their own (their packages are per file).

packets.title: Dart: an unnamed extension on a type declared elsewhere is a CLASS container `<module>::extension<T>`, top-level initialisers and `var` lists are walked from their STATE_VAR, and imports read `as` / `show` / `hide` from the AST
packets.area: CB-D4 unnamed extensions + CB-D5 top-level initialisers + CB-D6 import combinators
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/dart/src/lib.rs, measured on HEAD 2170ff8 with the new fixture dart-extensions-imports (nodes 0/4, edges 0/5):
D4 - visit_extension hangs an unnamed extension's members on its on-type only when THIS file declares it (LA.37b); an import-prefixed (`on m.Money`), core (`on String`) or other-file type -> `acc.members.unnamed_ext_skipped += 1` and the members (real code with bodies and calls) are dropped.
D5 - G19's visit_top_level_consts mints a STATE_VAR for `final` / `const` top-level declarations but never walks their initialiser (`final int defaultTax = seed();` -> no CALLS), and a `var a = .., b = f();` list (the root's initialized_identifier_list) is not matched at all.
D6 - collect_import (:1045) keeps the raw text after `import `, so `import 'money.dart' as m show Money, round2;` asks for the module `money.dart' as m show Money, round2` and binds nothing: `[evidence-lines] lang=dart ... imports=0` on probe dart1, and `m.round2(1)` resolves to nothing.
QNAME DECISION (D4): the container is CLASS `<file module>::extension<T>` where T is the on-type's simple name (import prefix, type arguments and `?` dropped; `Function` for a function type, `Record` for a record type); its members are METHOD `<container>::<name>`. Rejected: hanging the members on an other-file on-type (needs build-time binding, and a core type has no node); Dart's own `_extension#0` (positional, unstable under edits). `<` / `>` cannot occur in a Dart identifier, so no declared class can collide; two unnamed extensions on one type in one file merge into one container (same qname, cells stack), which Dart treats as two anonymous extensions - accepted.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): visit_extension (:502; `unnamed_ext_skipped += 1` at :520), extension_on_type (:546), visit_top_level_consts (:923, the noise gate drops only undocumented primitive literals) and collect_import (:1045, raw text) re-read; tree-sitter-dart: import_specification has fields uri / alias and combinator children (identifiers), initialized_identifier has name / value. grade.py on the draft fixture: nodes 0/4, edges 0/5. The draft MISSED stale consumers of the D4 change: parsers/code/dart/src/lib.rs unnamed_extension_on_a_foreign_type_is_skipped (:3400) and body_owners_fixture_members (:3546, exact METHOD list: gains `lib::app::extension<String>::whisper`), engine/tests/dart_body_owners.rs's module doc ("one on a foreign type mints nothing") and dart-body-owners/key.json's two forbid notes ("its members are skipped (counted in the marker), not hung on an invented node"). The forbid rows themselves stay true (CLASS `lib::app::String` / METHOD `lib::app::String::whisper` are still never minted: the container is `lib::app::extension<String>`).

packets.implementation:
1. D4: when `name` is absent and the on-type is not in file_types: qname = format!("{parent_qname}::extension<{T}>"); push CLASS (entity_cells of the declaration, DEFINES from the module, nav record name `extension<T>`), then visit_members with Owner { qname, id, members: class_member_names(body) } (only the extension's own members: the on-type's are unknown). acc.members.unnamed_ext_containers += 1 (renamed counter).

packets.title: `build_swift`: a bare call inside a type binds the type's own member first (implicit self, across extensions in other files), and a static call / construction on a type declared elsewhere in the same module binds
packets.area: CB-S1 implicit self + CB-S5 same-module static calls
packets.rationale:
Swift has no builder of its own: engine/src/build/lang_build.rs build_solo (:178) sends every `_`-arm language, Swift included, to glia_graph::build_typescript, whose resolve_calls tries a Bare call as the module's import binding, then the module's own symbol, then the package's; the extra_hook is `|_, _| None`. Two Swift semantics are lost: (S1) inside a method an unqualified call names the enclosing type's member before any free function; (S5) every file of a Swift module sees every type of the module without an import, so `Formatter.money(n)` on a type declared in another file of the target has no binding.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): the draft fixture's forbids passed vacuously on HEAD (its free `helper()` sat in a file of its own, which nothing sees). The Swift type is one node for `class Cart` and every `extension Cart` of the directory (debug CLI: CLASS Sources::App::Cart with METHODs helper / checkout / withTax). This packet is independent of CB.10 (different files; every call in its fixture classifies on HEAD) and of CB.22.

packets.implementation:
1. extern "C": linkage_specification's `body` is a declaration_list (walk children with the same Scope), a function_definition or a declaration (visit_one it). Linkage changes nothing about C++ naming, so the contents keep the enclosing scope (`legacy_entry` -> FUNCTION `src::cart.cpp::legacy_entry`).
2. Anonymous namespace: visit_children(body, .., scope) with the SAME Scope (no PACKAGE node: it has no name); its free functions keep the file scope qname (`src::cart.cpp::clamp`) - exactly a .cpp free function's qname - and each records NavFact::InternalLinkage { name } on the file MODULE (internal linkage).
3. template_declaration: visit its named child that is a class_specifier / struct_specifier / union_specifier (type), function_definition (function / out-of-line member), declaration (a prototype or a variable) or another template_declaration; the Scope is unchanged. The entity is named without template arguments (`template <class T> class Box` -> `shop::Box`); a specialisation's `template_type` name reads its `name` field (`Box<int>` -> Box), so the primary and its specialisations merge into one node (cells stack) - one entity per template, as today for overloads.
4. union_specifier -> visit_type with kind STRUCT (no new id).
5. Nested types: visit_type(.., enclosing: Option<(&str, NodeId)>): with an enclosing type the qname is `format!("{outer}::{name}")` (a nested type is scoped by its outer type in every TU, header or not), nav parent / DEFINES the outer type, and its members are visited under that qname; local_types gets `join(scope.ns_path, "<Outer>::<Inner>")` so an out-of-line `int Cart::Line::total() const` in a .cpp binds in-file (visit_out_of_line looks q = `Cart::Line` up through ns_prefixes). A nested type in a SOURCE file keeps the file-local rule for its outermost type (`src::a.cpp::Outer::Inner`).
6. C3: Acc.module_qname = the parse's module qname; collect_include(node, src, &acc.module_qname, acc).
7. TYPES for the receiver pass (graph/src/calls.rs resolve_via_receiver_type reads field_types / local_types): field_declaration in a class body -> record_field_type(class_id, declarator identifier, simple type); parameters of every function / method definition and `declaration` statements in bodies (`Cart c;`, `shop::Cart c(1);`, `auto c = Cart();`, `Cart* p = new Cart();`) -> record_local_type(fn_id, name, simple type). SIMPLE TYPE: the type_specifier text with qualifiers (`const`, `struct`, `class`), `*` / `&` and template arguments removed, the last `::` segment kept (`std::unique_ptr<Cart>` records `unique_ptr` - no container peeling, the Rust caveat's rule); primitive types (void, bool, char, short, int, long, float, double, signed, unsigned, size_t, auto without an initialiser) record nothing.
8. PROTOTYPES: a `declaration` at file or namespace scope (not in a class body) whose declarator chain holds a function_declarator records NavFact::DeclaresFn { ns: scope.ns_path, name } on the file MODULE (a friend declaration or a member declaration inside a class does not).
9. USING: `using namespace a::b;` -> NavFact::UsingNamespace { within: scope.ns_path, ns: "a::b" }; `using a::b::f;` -> NavFact::UsingName { within, ns: "a::b", name: "f" }; recorded on the file MODULE wherever they appear (file, namespace or function scope - a function-scope using is approximated as file-wide). `using X = Y;` (alias_declaration) is not a using-directive.
10. TESTS: extern_c_block_and_definition; anonymous_namespace_functions_are_file_scoped_and_internal; template_class_and_function; template_specialisation_merges; union_is_a_struct; nested_type_and_member (`class Cart { struct Line { int total() const {..} }; }` -> STRUCT shop::Cart::Line, METHOD shop::Cart::Line::total); out_of_line_nested_member_binds_in_file; include_inside_namespace_is_the_files; field_and_local_types_recorded; prototypes_usings_and_static_recorded.

packets.title: Go route mounts resolved at build time: provisional mount ROUTEs take every prefix their parameter or field receives through resolved calls (a fixpoint over MountArg / FieldMount facts), one ROUTE per mount, unmounted ones keep their local path
packets.area: CB-c2 Go group prefixes through fields / parameters (1/2: graph pass)
packets.rationale:
A Go group prefix reaches a route only inside one function body today (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs collect_routes_in's per-body prefix_map). The dominant gin / echo / chi layout mounts per-feature register functions on groups built elsewhere: quokka-stack turps/Server/server.go `public := r.Group("/api"); protectedRoutes := public.Group("/protected"); controllers.RegisterUserProtectedRoutes(protectedRoutes)` - 14 such calls; Kina backend/cmd/server/main.go `userH.RegisterRoutes(protected)` with protected = `/api`. Every one of those routes is minted without its prefix. Measured on HEAD 2170ff8 (debug CLI, git-archive copies): quokka-stack ROUTEs `POST /activity @turps`, `GET /user/2fa @turps`, ... while the app serves /api/protected/activity; `[http] routes=64 endpoints=49 paired=47 (exact=10 any=0 eprefix=37 ...)`; `glia spec-status` matches 72 of quokka's feature.yaml ops only by `prefix, medium` (10 exact). Kina: `[http] routes=90 endpoints=110 paired=89 (exact=0 ... eprefix=47 ... base=42)`.
The calls that carry a mount are already resolved for quokka (`CALLS turps::Server::server::SetupRouter -> ...::RegisterUserProtectedRoutes` and 14 siblings, 15 edges, debug CLI); Kina's method-on-local (`userH.RegisterRoutes`, userH from a constructor) needs CA-2's return-type receivers. So the prefix flow is a graph step AFTER resolve_go_calls, reading the resolved CALLS edges (their EVIDENCE line) - it cannot be a post-cache graft, which runs before any call is bound. The parser half (CB.23) emits the provisional qnames and facts; this pass is written first and is a no-op until they exist (no intermediate commit ships a provisional qname).
VERIFIER (2170ff8): build_go_passes (graph/src/build.rs:82) runs merge_parses -> bind_split_go_receivers (re-parents, never renames) -> build_symbol_table -> resolve_go_calls -> refs partition -> resolve_refs, so a pass between resolve_go_calls and the partition sees every resolved CALLS edge and every pending HANDLED_BY ref. rename_nodes (:1674) takes (g, calls, refs, renames) and documents that it moves ids and nav records, not qname strings. A Go ROUTE carries no parse-time edge (emit_route_from_call pushes the node, its nav record and refs only) and its ROUTE_METHOD cell holds no path (route_method_cell :2665), so a rename moves nothing stale. quokka-stack HEAD (debug CLI, git-archive copy): `[http] routes=64 endpoints=49 paired=47 (exact=10 any=0 eprefix=37 rprefix=0 base=0 suffix=0)`; turps/Server/server.go builds `public := r.Group("/api")`, `protectedRoutes := public.Group("/protected")` and passes it to 15 Register*Routes functions (every one `func X(router *gin.RouterGroup)`). SECURITY: this names routes (structural identity, the A11 const-fold family); it tracks no input to any sink.
entry_points: graph/src/go_mounts.rs (new; slot `graph mod go_mounts`, private, declared by C0.6) - pub(crate) fn bind(g: &mut RepoGraph, refs: &mut Vec<UnresolvedRef>) -> MountStats
graph/src/build.rs:82 build_go_passes - calls go_mounts::bind(&mut g, &mut all_refs) after resolve_go_calls and before the refs partition / resolve_refs; build_go prints its marker
graph/src/build.rs:1674 rename_nodes - becomes pub(crate) (go_mounts renames provisional ROUTEs through it)
code-domain/src/lib.rs endpoint::parse_mount_route_qname / Mount / NavFact::{MountArg, FieldMount} - read (defined by CB.6)
packets.implementation:
1. PROVISIONAL ROUTES: every ROUTE node whose qname, after split_owner, parses with parse_mount_route_qname -> (method, Mount::Param { fn_qname, index, .. } | Mount::Field { owner, field, .. }, local_path, owner suffix). Collected in g.nodes order. 2. CALL INDEX: for every CALLS edge (g.edges order) take (from, Evidence::of(edge).line, nav name of `to`) -> to (resolve_calls pushes one edge per call site with `ev.line(site.line)`; push_edge does not dedupe, so two calls on two rows are two keys). MountArg facts are keyed by their scope (the caller fn id); nav_facts is a HashMap, so scopes are visited in g.nodes order, never map order - with the round / prefix caps the visiting order must be fixed for the result to be. 3. FIXPOINT (BTreeMap / BTreeSet throughout): slots are ParamSlot(fn NodeId, index) and FieldSlot(owner `::`, field). resolve(mount, scope) -> BTreeSet: Const(p) -> {p}; Param { fn_qname, index, suffix } -> { join_path(m, suffix) | m in slot(ParamSlot(id of fn_qname, index)) }; Field { owner, field, suffix } -> { join_path(m, suffix) | m in slot(FieldSlot(owner, field)) }. Each round: for every MountArg { line, callee, arg, mount } of scope C, the callee T = CALL INDEX[(C, line, callee)] (none -> skipped, counted `unbound_args`), slot(ParamSlot(T, arg)) |= resolve(mount, C); for every FieldMount { owner, field, mount } of scope F, slot(FieldSlot(owner, field)) |= resolve(mount, F). Stop when no slot grows; hard cap 16 rounds and 32 prefixes per slot (a mount loop or explosion stops growing, counted `capped`). join_path is the Go parser's rule (one `/` between, a relative literal kept relative), then canonical_http_path. 4. RE-KEY: for each provisional route (method, base, local, owner): finals = sorted { canonical(join_path(p, local)) | p in slot(base) }; empty -> { canonical(local) } (no caller mounts it: today's qname exactly). New qname = with_owner(route_qname(method, final), owner). The first final renames the provisional id through rename_nodes(g, &mut [], refs, &[(old, new)]) - it rewrites nodes, edges, refs[].from and nav records, and merges into an existing ROUTE with that id (two registrations of one full path); rename_nodes moves ids, not strings, so qname_by_id[new] is then set to the final qname (with owner). Each further final CLONES the renamed node (cells cloned), records its nav (qname = the final qname, kind ROUTE, no parent - the parser's ROUTE nav shape), clones every edge incident to the renamed id with the clone as that endpoint (each keeps its EVIDENCE cell), and clones every UnresolvedRef whose `from` is the renamed id with `from` = the clone, so resolve_refs binds each clone's HANDLED_BY (evidence graph:refs, as every route's). 5. The parser records a ROUTE's nav name as its (owner-free) qname and LB.4a's owner rekey keeps that name; rename_nodes keeps `name` too, so after a rename (and for each clone) set name_by_id = the final qname WITHOUT the owner suffix - the name every other owner-qualified ROUTE carries. 6. MARKER (build_go, once per Go graph with a provisional route): `[go-mounts] provisional=

mounted= extra_mounts= unmounted= mount_args= unbound_args= field_mounts= capped=`. 7. packets.implementation:
1. prefix_map: HashMap -> BTreeMap (lookup-only today; BTreeMap keeps any future iteration deterministic). Seeded with the fn's ROUTER-TYPED parameters only: a parameter whose declared type (pointer stripped) is a qualified type of gin / echo / chi / mux / fiber / httprouter, or `http.ServeMux`, or whose type name is RouterGroup / IRouter / IRoutes / Router / ServeMux / Group / Engine / Echo -> Param { fn_qname, index: i, suffix: "" }, where i counts parameter NAMES (a grouped `public, protected, kycProtected *gin.RouterGroup` - Kina's shape - is indices 0, 1, 2; the receiver excluded). Seeding every parameter would record a MountArg for every forwarded `ctx` / `id` in a Go repo (parse-cache bloat, no route); every Register* function in quokka-stack and Kina takes `*gin.RouterGroup`. A Const mount behaves exactly as the old String prefix (a routes-in-one-body file is byte-identical to HEAD). 2. emit_route_from_call: prefix = the receiver's Mount (identifier -> prefix_map; selector x.f -> the file's FieldPrefixes from CB.11 when Const, else Mount::Field { owner: `::` (the file's module qname minus its last segment, so a field assigned in server.go and read in admin_routes.go names one owner), field: f, suffix: "" }). Const -> route_qname(method, join_path(p, local)) (today). Param / Field -> mount_route_qname(method, &mount_with_local_suffix, local): a provisional ROUTE the build's go_mounts pass (CB.20) turns into one ROUTE per mount, or the plain local path when nothing mounts it. HANDLED_BY refs and POSITION / ROUTE_METHOD cells are pushed exactly as today, from the provisional id. 3. record_mount_args, called from walk_routes for every call_expression that is not itself a route registration or Group call: callee = the function identifier or the selector's field name (`api.RegisterUsers` -> RegisterUsers, `userH.RegisterRoutes` -> RegisterRoutes); for each argument index i: identifier with a Mount in prefix_map -> that mount; selector x.f with a field mount -> Field / Const mount; call `x.Group("/p")` -> x's mount + `/p`. Record NavFact::MountArg { line: 0-based row of the call, callee, arg: i, mount } on the fn id (the same row LC.3b gives the CALLS edge's EVIDENCE, so CB.20 can match it). 4. FieldMount: scan_field_prefixes records every `x.f = ` / `&T{f: }` as FieldMount { owner: `::`, field, mount } where mount is Const, Param (the assigning fn's param) or Field. 4b. packets.title: GraphQL and tRPC client base URLs narrow their project's operations: a literal Apollo / urql / graphql-request / tRPC link URL is recorded per MODULE, spread post-cache to the project's GRAPHQL_OPERATION / RPC_CALL sides as ENDPOINT_HIT hosts, and the graphql / rpc resolvers narrow by host
packets.rationale:
A GraphQL operation or a tRPC call names only a field / procedure path; the service it goes to is decided by the CLIENT the project builds once - `new ApolloClient({ uri: "http://users-svc/graphql" })`, `createClient({ url })` (urql), `new GraphQLClient("..")` (graphql-request), `httpBatchLink({ url: "http://catalog-svc/api/trpc" })` - usually in a different file than the operations. graph/src/resolvers/graphql.rs keys resolvers by the owner-free field (LB.8b) and rpc.rs pairs every same-path procedure across owners (its test rpc_call_owner_is_stripped pins one edge per owner). New fixture graphql-rpc-host-narrowing (services/users and services/catalog both serve getUser and item.list; apps/web's Apollo client targets users-svc, its tRPC client catalog-svc) graded on HEAD 2170ff8: edges 2/2 but FORBID VIOLATIONS 2 (each op / call pairs both services). No extractor reads a client base URL today (grep of graphql.rs / trpc.rs for `uri:` / `httpBatchLink`: only the op / hook scans).
VERIFIER (2170ff8): grade.py on the draft fixture: edges 2/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 2 (each op / call pairs both services).
