packets.implementation:
1. EXTRACTORS: within the balanced `(...)` of a listed constructor / link call, find the key `uri` or `url` followed by `:` and a single string literal (quote or template WITHOUT `${`); the authority is code_domain::endpoint::url_split(literal).0 (absolute URLs only; a relative `/graphql` or an env-var names no host). graphql-request's first positional string argument likewise. Lines are 0-based rows of the literal. Returned in source order.
2. ENGINE extract.rs: `for (host, line) in graphql::graphql_client_hosts(source) { fp.nav.record_fact(module_id, NavFact::ClientHost { via: "graphql".into(), host, line }) }` and the same for trpc (`via: "rpc"`), in the TS-family / code branch that already runs those extractors. Cached with the parse.
3. GRAFT stamp_client_hosts (grafts.rs, after owners qualify - the LB.4a ordering rule): group ClientHost facts by (via, owner_of(module file)), owner None for a file under no nested root; per group the sorted, deduped host list. Then for every GRAPHQL_OPERATION (via graphql) and RPC_CALL (via rpc) node of a parse whose file is in that owner (its POSITION file; the node's ` @owner` suffix is the same owner) and that carries no ENDPOINT_HIT yet, push ONE ENDPOINT_HIT per node id per repo (on the first parse in walk order that holds the id: an op node several files of one owner share merges their cells, and a second identical cell would only bloat it) `{"via":"graphql","hosts":["users-svc"]}` (a single host still in `hosts`, the A11.4 array shape hit_hosts already reads). A project with no ClientHost fact stamps nothing (no narrowing, today's behaviour). Deterministic: facts in parse order, BTreeMap by (via, owner), hosts sorted.
4. RESOLVERS (host.rs is the module CB.12 creates (new there); nothing is added to it here beyond use): graphql.rs - for each op with >= 2 targets, build scoped targets (owner from the resolver's qname via host::owner_from_qname_suffix, interned in a per-resolve host::Owners), aliases = build_service_alias_index(graphs, &owners), narrow_by_host(&aliases, hit_hosts(&op.cells).as_deref(), &mut targets); rpc.rs - the same per RPC_CALL. A narrowed edge carries rule `host` (RuleTally) instead of the default; nothing narrows without positive evidence (unknown alias, no host, no kept target).
5. MARKERS: grafts `[client-hosts] graphql=<g> rpc=<r> sides=<s> repo=<label>` (facts / stamped sides), once per repo with a fact; resolvers `[graphql-resolve] ... narrowed-by-host=<n>`, `[trpc-link] ... narrowed-by-host=<n>`.
6. TESTS: extractors - apollo_client_uri, http_link_uri, urql_create_client_url, graphql_request_ctor, trpc_http_batch_link_url, relative_or_dynamic_url_is_none; engine grafts - stamp_client_hosts_spreads_within_an_owner (a fact in apps/web/src/apollo.ts stamps apps/web ops, not apps/admin's); graph - graphql_host_narrows_to_the_named_project, rpc_host_narrows_to_the_named_project, no_host_keeps_every_target (rpc_call_owner_is_stripped stays green).

packets.title: C++ call scope: a bare call in a member binds the class's own member first (implicit this), `Type::m()` / `ns::f()` bind through C++ name lookup, typed receivers resolve with `using` directives, and a call through a header prototype binds the one external definition
packets.area: CB-C5 implicit-this / static / object calls + CB-C6 header prototypes + CB-C7 using (graph half)
packets.rationale:
graph/src/build.rs build_c_cpp resolves calls with the generic resolve_calls plus CppCallScope (:1870) as extra_hook, which only handles a Bare call: the definition's own file (LB.10c) and headers the file DIRECTLY includes (LB.10a). Measured on HEAD 2170ff8 with the new fixture cpp-call-scope (edges 0/6) and probe cpp1:
C5 - a bare `reset()` inside Cart::clear / Cart::add is never tried as a member of the enclosing class (probe cpp1: no CALLS Cart::clear -> Cart::reset); `Cart::count()` is an Attribute whose base names a class no import binds; `c.add(1)` / `box.get()` need receiver types (recorded by CB.19) and, with two classes named Cart in the build (shop::Cart, legacy::Cart), C++ name lookup rather than unique_global_function.
C6 - `codec_encode("a")` in cart.cpp reaches codec.h through cart.hpp (an include of an include) and is DEFINED in codec.c; the header only declares it, so no module lists the name and CppCallScope finds nothing.
C7 - `using namespace shop;` decides that run()'s `Cart` is shop::Cart; nothing reads it.
The parser half (CB.19) records field / local types, DeclaresFn / InternalLinkage / UsingNamespace / UsingName facts; CB.22 gives angle and search-root includes their IMPORTS edges.
VERIFIER (2170ff8): build_c_cpp (graph/src/build.rs:238), CppTypes (:1290), cpp_name (:1384), cpp_ns_prefixes (:1415), is_cpp_type (:1447), CppCallScope (:1870) re-read. grade.py on the draft fixture: edges 0/6, forbids 0 violated. Every include in the fixture is quoted and includer-relative, so its IMPORTS edges (and the transitive closure this pass walks) exist on HEAD: CB.22 is not a prerequisite. depends_on keeps CB.19 (types and facts recorded), CB.15 (enclosing_class_or_struct pub(crate)), CB.6 (NavFact) and C0.6 (the `mod cpp_scope;` facade line).

packets.implementation:
1. why.rs: `pub(crate) fn tier_of(ev: Option<&Evidence>, e: &Edge) -> (&'static str, Option<String>)` and `pub(crate) const FACT / DERIVED / HEURISTIC`; nothing else in why changes (its rows, marker and tests stay).
2. check.rs: `pub const HEURISTIC: &str = "heuristic";` beside FACT / DERIVED. ViolationEdge { .., tier, note } (#[non_exhaustive] already, so additive). A private `fn tier_rank(t) -> u8 { fact 0, derived 1, heuristic 2 }`.
3. Ctx::row(from, category, to, ev: Option<&Evidence>, tier: (&'static str, Option<String>)): forbid_edge passes `crate::why::tier_of(ev.as_ref(), e)`; its dedup key is unchanged (first edge of a key wins, so its tier is the first edge's, in all_edges order - the order why's rows use).
4. forbid_edge sort key becomes (tier_rank, file.is_none, file, line.is_none, line, category) then qnames: the MAX_EVIDENCE truncation keeps fact rows first. Violation.tier = the minimum-rank row's tier: ONE observed (fact) edge proves a forbidden dependency exists; a rule broken only by resolver-paired edges is derived, only by overlay / name-only edges heuristic.
5. no_cycle: the tier is computed where the site is recorded, not at row time: `Sites` becomes `BTreeMap<(u64, u32, u64), (Option<Evidence>, &'static str, Option<String>)>` and each `or_insert_with` stores `(ev, tier, note)` from `why::tier_of(ev, e)` over the edge it is looking at - the REAL graph edge on the node-level branch (so an overlay hop's ORIGIN provenance reaches the note), the lifted `module_import_graph` edge on the imports branch (that edge carries no cells: an overlay IMPORTS hop keeps its heuristic tier and gets the stanza note without the provenance). Ctx::row therefore takes the `(tier, note)` pair instead of an `&Edge` (forbid_edge computes it from `e` inline). Violation.tier = DERIVED (the cycle is computed) unless any hop is HEURISTIC, then HEURISTIC: every hop is needed for the cycle, so its weakest hop bounds it.
6. `pub(crate) fn check_rules(merged: &MergedGraph, rules: &[(NodeId, ConstraintRule)]) -> CheckReport` holds today's check() body and marker; `pub fn check(merged) -> CheckReport { check_rules(merged, &declared_constraints(merged)) }`.
7. Marker: after the unchanged `[check] rules=..` line, when violations is non-empty, one more line `[check] tiers fact=<F> derived=<D> heuristic=<H>` counting Violation records by tier (the existing line's format is asserted verbatim by cli/tests/check_cli.rs:126 and py/tests/surface/test_check.py:45, so it is not touched).

Module docs of check.rs: the tier paragraph rewritten (per-edge why tiers; forbid_edge strongest, no_cycle weakest-hop). py/src/check.rs docstring updated; its unit test asserts the evidence rows carry `tier`.
9. CONFIDENCE (why.rs tier_of, James 2026-09-30): after the NAME_ONLY_RULES check and the basis-None check, `if tier == FACT && stage == "graph" && e.confidence != Confidence::Strong { return (DERIVED, Some(format!("inferred binding ({}, {} confidence)", rule.unwrap_or("-"), confidence_name(e.confidence)))) }`. Only the graph stage: parser / extractor / docs edges are read at a site the source spells out. Every tier_of reader moves with it - why's rows, check (steps 3-5: a forbid_edge matched only by a Go implicit IMPLEMENTS tiers derived) and CE.1e's SCIP confirmation (a Medium graph edge a SCIP index confirms is upgraded, not counted confirmed_fact). packets.title: Context packing to a token budget in the engine: seeds from find, a PPR neighbourhood, a greedy value-per-token climb up the fidelity ladder, a measured re-render loop and a located, tiered manifest
packets.rationale: "Give me the context for X in N tokens" is the question every agent consumer asks, and today the answer is assembled outside glia: repo-graph's orient(seed) runs find_records -> activate(seed, 50) -> dense_text_subset -> _truncate(chars) (server.py:257-266), a char cut that ignores rank, drops the highest-ranked node if it sorts late by qname, and has no notion of tokens. The pieces exist in glia: find::find_nodes (engine/src/find.rs:112, tiered exact / fuzzy), MergedGraph::activate (graph/src/traversal.rs:322) with the domain's weights (CODE_TABLES.activation_config), and CC.4a's ladder. Cross-consumer logic belongs in glia (the wrapper is transport). TOKEN COUNTING DECISION: Cargo.lock holds no tokenizer crate (grep tiktoken / tokenizers / bpe: 0 hits) and none reproduces Claude's tokenizer anyway; a tokenizer crate would add a Cargo.lock change (a PARSER_STAMP input). MEASURED bytes per token with a local code BPE (Qwen2.5-coder tokenizer.json, python `tokenizers` 0.22.2): engine/src/*.rs 3.93, substrate-gap python fixtures 4.18, typescript 4.17, go 3.73. The estimate is `ceil(bytes * 10 / 37)` (3.7 bytes per token, the lowest measured, so it over-counts on every sample: a pack never overflows by estimate on these languages), configurable per call, and the manifest reports the exact byte count so a caller with a real tokenizer can re-count. Verified: `glia pack` is an unrecognized subcommand at 2170ff8; engine has no pack module.

```rust pub const DEFAULT_BUDGET_TOKENS: usize = 8000; pub const DEFAULT_BYTES_PER_TOKEN_X10: u32 = 37; // 3.7 bytes per token (rationale) pub const DEFAULT_SEEDS: usize = 5; pub const DEFAULT_CANDIDATES: usize = 200; #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct PackArgs { pub budget_tokens: usize, pub bytes_per_token_x10: u32, pub seeds: usize, pub candidates: usize, pub preset: Option, pub scope: Option } // impl Default #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct PackedNode { pub id: u64, pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str, pub file: Option, pub line: Option /* 1-based, LD.1 Locator */, pub fidelity: &'static str, pub tokens: usize, pub rank: usize, pub tier: &'static str /* fact|derived|heuristic */, pub reason: &'static str /* seed|neighbour */, pub matched: Option<&'static str> /* find tier of a seed */ } #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Pack { pub query: String, pub text: String, pub budget_tokens: usize, pub used_tokens: usize, pub bytes: usize, pub bytes_per_token: String /* "3.7" */, pub candidates: usize, pub nodes: Vec, pub dropped: usize, pub rerenders: usize, pub absence: Option } pub fn estimate_tokens(bytes: usize, bytes_per_token_x10: u32) -> usize // (bytes * 10).div_ceil(x10), x10 >= 10 pub fn pack(merged: &MergedGraph, query: &str, args: &PackArgs) -> Pack pub fn pack_ids(merged: &MergedGraph, seeds: &[NodeId], args: &PackArgs) -> Pack // explicit seeds (a diff-impact's, a trace's) ``` 1. SEEDS: find_nodes(merged, query, top_k = args.seeds, scope). Tiers exact_qname / exact_name / exact_ci / qname_suffix -> tier fact; every fuzzier find tier -> heuristic; `matched` = the find tier name. No row -> Pack with no nodes and find's own absence (LD.8a). pack_ids seeds are tier fact, matched None. 2. CANDIDATES: `merged.activate(&seed_ids, &cfg)` with cfg = CODE_TABLES.activation_config(args.preset.as_deref()) and cfg.top_k = args.candidates, cfg.direction = Direction::Undirected (the domain default is Forward, which from a leaf seed reaches nothing: a context is its callers AND its callees; damping stays the domain's 0.5, local around the seeds); the seeds first in find order, then the rest by (score desc, id asc); a neighbour's tier is derived (a walk over extracted edges). Scope keeps candidates node_in_scope accepts. Each candidate gets an integer weight w = seeds: 2_000_000_000 - rank; neighbours: (score * 1e9).round() as u64 (scores are in [0, 1]), so every comparison below is integer. 3. GREEDY CLIMB: rung values V = [Qname 1, Outline 3, Preview 6, Full 10]; cost(n, f) = estimate_tokens(render_node(n, f).len() + 1). State: each candidate absent or at one rung. Repeat: over every candidate and every rung ABOVE its current one (jumps allowed, so a cheap first rung never traps a node), the step with the largest gain / extra_cost, gain = w * (V[to] - V[from]) (V[absent] = 0), compared by u128 cross-multiplication, ties to (rank, lower rung); apply it if running + extra_cost <= budget_tokens. Stop when no step fits. O(candidates^2 * 4) = at most 160k comparisons at the defaults. 4. RE-RENDER: text = render_pack(merged, title, picks in rank order); used = estimate_tokens(text.len()). The title (`context for `), section headers and the `## links` lines are not in the per-node costs, so while used > budget_tokens: move the pick with the smallest w * V[rung] / cost down one rung (Qname -> removed), re-render, rerenders += 1 (bounded by 4 x picks). used_tokens, bytes = text.len() of the final render. 5. MANIFEST: nodes in rank order with fidelity name, own tokens (cost at its rung), rank, tier, reason, matched, located through ONE Locator; dropped = candidates - packed. budget below the cheapest Qname line -> no nodes and an Absence reason `budget_too_small` naming the smallest cost. Marker per call: `[pack] query= seeds= candidates= packed=

(full= preview= outline= qname=) tokens=/ bytes= bpt= rerenders=`. engine/Cargo.toml gains the projection-text path dependency (no cycle: projection-text depends on core, code-domain, graph, activation only; its `research` feature stays off). Cargo.lock: glia-engine's dependency list gains glia-projection-text - the lock changes, so PARSER_STAMP moves once (declared below). packets.risks: The estimate over-counts on the measured samples; on minified JS or long base64 literals bytes per token can fall below 3.7 and the pack can overflow a real tokenizer by that ratio - the manifest's `bytes` and the configurable bytes_per_token are the escape hatch, documented. packets.title: Reflexion model declarations: overlay [[component]] (name, paths) and [[layer]] (ordered, optional strict) sections plus [[constraint]] kind = "allow", validated by the loader and stored as CONSTRAINT entries of three new kinds
packets.rationale: check v1 (LE.8) evaluates forbid_edge / no_cycle rules, one pair of scopes at a time: a team that wants to say 'the architecture is web -> api -> store and nothing else' writes N^2 forbid rules and still cannot see the dependencies it expected but lost. A reflexion model (Murphy / Notkin / Sullivan) states the high-level model once - components mapped to paths, the dependencies allowed between them - and the checker reports convergences, divergences and absences. Verified at 2170ff8: code-domain/src/glia_config.rs:64 CONSTRAINT_KINDS = [forbid_edge, no_cycle, invariant]; SECTIONS (:48) has no component / layer; GliaConfig is #[serde(deny_unknown_fields)], so a `[[component]]` table is a load error today; external_inputs::ConstraintKind (:439, #[non_exhaustive]) has three variants and constraint_rule (:487) skips any other kind (`_ => return None`) - so a 0.5.0 reader of a 0.5.1 graph drops the new entries silently, which is the declared compatibility. Rules travel in the graph as CONSTRAINT cells (LF.4a, declared.rs apply_declared_cells :289, read back only through declared_constraints :412), so a loaded .gmap can be checked without the overlay file: the model must be stored the same way. Anchoring: a constraint without `anchor` binds the PROJECT at its scope (declared.rs module docs, ANCHOR 2); a repo with no root manifest has no root PROJECT (measured: `glia projects /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CC/tier` lists only `api` and `web`), so a component needs a fallback anchor.

OVERLAY SCHEMA (version stays 1):
```toml
[[component]]
name = "web"
paths = ["web", "shared/ui"]   # repo-relative paths or project labels
[[component]]
name = "api"
paths = ["services/api"]
[[layer]]
name = "ui"
components = ["web"]           # layers in file order, top first
[[layer]]
name = "core"
components = ["api"]
strict = false                  # true: may use the NEXT layer only
[[constraint]]
id = "web-uses-api"
kind = "allow"
from = "web"
to = "api"   # component names

packets.title: review in the engine: one RevDelta -> changed nodes, ranked impact, tests to run, every added / removed edge with its why tier, and the working tree's rules checked on both sides (new vs resolved violations)
packets.rationale: A PR reviewer asks four questions at once: what changed, what does it reach, which tests prove it, and did it break a declared rule. 0.5.0 answers each separately and each rebuilds the before + after pair: diff_impact_vs_rev, tests_for_rev and patterns --base each call graph_delta_vs_rev (engine/src/delta.rs:305); `glia check` builds the working tree only, so it cannot say whether a violation is NEW in this change or was already there. The edge rows `glia delta` prints carry emitter and basis (DeltaEdge, delta.rs) but no tier, so a reviewer cannot tell a new observed call from a new name-guessed one. With CC.1 (diff_impact_from_delta / tests_for_delta), CC.3 (why::tier_of pub(crate), check_rules) the review is a composition over ONE RevDelta: one working-tree build and one rev build. ```rust
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct ReviewArgs { pub blast: BlastOptions /* BlastOptions::default(): both directions, depth 4 */,
    pub tests: TestsForArgs, pub max_impact: usize /* 50 */, pub max_tests: usize /* 50 */ }   // impl Default
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct ReviewEdge { pub change: &'static str /* added|removed|reconfidenced */,
    pub from_qname: String, pub to_qname: String, pub category: &'static str, pub tier: &'static str, pub note: Option<String>,
    pub site_file: Option<String>, pub site_line: Option<i64>, pub emitter: Option<String> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone, Default)] pub struct ReviewCounts { pub nodes_changed: usize, pub seeds: usize,
    pub edges_added: usize, pub edges_removed: usize, pub impact: usize, pub tests: usize, pub untested_seeds: usize,
    pub new_violations: usize, pub resolved_violations: usize, pub edges_by_tier: BTreeMap<&'static str, usize> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Review { pub base: String, pub counts: ReviewCounts,
    pub changed: Vec<ChangedNode>, pub impact: BlastRadius, pub tests: TestsFor, pub edges: Vec<ReviewEdge>,
    pub new_violations: Vec<Violation>, pub resolved_violations: Vec<Violation>, pub check_errors: Vec<(String, String)>,
    pub blocking: bool }
pub fn review(rev: &RevDelta, args: &ReviewArgs) -> Result<Review, String>
pub fn review_vs_rev(repo_path: &str, base: &str, args: &ReviewArgs) -> Result<Review, String>   // graph_delta_vs_rev once + review
```
1. IMPACT + CHANGED: `let di = diff_impact_from_delta(rev, &args.blast);` changed = di.changed; impact = di.impact with results truncated to max_impact (the engine ranking kept; counts.impact = the untruncated length).
2. TESTS: `tests_for_delta(rev, &args.tests)?`, tests truncated to max_tests (counts.tests untruncated); counts.untested_seeds = its untested.len().
3. EDGES: for each key in rev.delta.added_edges / removed_edges / reconfidenced_edges, the first edge with that EdgeKey in the after graph (added / reconfidenced) or the before graph (removed) - one BTreeMap<EdgeKey, &Edge> per side built once over all_edges() (delta.rs's first_edges shape; not shared because it is private there) - and `why::tier_of(Evidence::of(e).as_ref(), e)`; located like DeltaEdge (1-based site line). Sorted (tier rank, change, category, from, to) so a reviewer reads facts first. counts.edges_by_tier over them.
4. RULES: `let rules = declared_constraints(&rev.after.merged);` (the rules as the change leaves them) -> `check_rules(&rev.after.merged, &rules)` and `check_rules(&rev.before.merged, &rules)`. A rule whose scope is empty on the BEFORE side (a directory the change creates) errors there: that side counts as no violation for it (its after-side result stands); errors of the after side go to check_errors. Violation identity: forbid_edge / divergence -> per evidence edge (from_qname, category, to_qname) under the rule id; no_cycle -> the component's sorted member set (the witness is one cycle, the members are the cycle's identity). new_violations = after-side violations with at least one identity absent before, each reduced to its NEW evidence rows (count = new rows); resolved_violations = before-side identities absent after, reduced the same way. NodeIds match across sides (the rev is built under the working tree's identity, LE.1b), and identities use qnames so a move still matches. blocking = !new_violations.is_empty().
5. Marker, once per review: `[review] base=<rev> changed=<C> seeds=<S> impact=<I> tests=<T> untested=<U> edges +<a> -<r> (fact=<F> derived=<D> heuristic=<H>) violations new=<N> resolved=<R> blocking=<true|false>`; the component answers print their own markers once each (one `[delta]` line in total).
No renderer here: CC.6b owns the markdown.

```rust
pub const DEFAULT_QUIET_DAYS: u32 = 90;
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct FlagArgs { pub quiet_days: u32, pub scope: Option<String> }   // impl Default
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct FlagSite { pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str,
    pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64> /* 1-based: the EVIDENCE site, else the node */ }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct FlagFinding { pub status: &'static str, pub tier: &'static str, pub note: String }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct FlagRow { pub key: String, pub providers: Vec<String>,
    pub definitions: Vec<FlagSite>, pub reads: Vec<FlagSite>, pub readers: usize, pub last_read_change: Option<i64>, pub findings: Vec<FlagFinding> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct FlagsReport { pub flags: Vec<FlagRow>, pub definitions_in_graph: usize,
    pub quiet_evaluated: bool, pub history_now: Option<i64>, pub quiet_days: u32, pub counts: BTreeMap<&'static str, usize>, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
pub fn flags(merged: &MergedGraph, args: &FlagArgs) -> FlagsReport
```
GROUPING: every CONFIG_KEY whose qname starts `config:flag:`, grouped by key across repos (BTreeMap). providers = the distinct ENV-cell `source` values (sorted). definitions = DEFINES_CONFIG edges into the key's nodes; reads = READS_CONFIG edges into them (SHARES_CONFIG ignored); each FlagSite located at the edge's EVIDENCE file / line (0-based + 1) when it names a file, else at the source node through one Locator; sorted (file, line, qname). readers = distinct source nodes of reads. definitions_in_graph = distinct files holding any flag definition.
FINDINGS (a row may hold several; order dead, undefined, single_site, quiet):
- dead, tier derived: definitions non-empty, reads empty. Note: `defined in <file>:<line>; no literal read of the key is extracted (a key built at runtime is not captured)`.
- undefined, tier derived: reads non-empty, definitions empty, definitions_in_graph > 0. Note: `read, but none of the <n> flag definition file(s) in the graph defines it; a provider console keeps definitions outside the repo`. With definitions_in_graph == 0 no undefined finding is raised and the report says so.
- single_site, tier fact: readers == 1. Note: `read only in <qname> (<file>:<line>)`.
- quiet, tier heuristic: history_now (signals::history_now) is Some, EVERY reader has recency (symbol_blame `last` for a FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS reader, module_churn `last` for a MODULE reader), and last_read_change = max(those) <= history_now - quiet_days * 86_400. Note: `no reading line changed in <d> days before the snapshot's newest change (git blame, not runtime use)`. The reference time is the graph's own newest history change, never the wall clock, so the answer is a function of the graph. quiet_evaluated = history_now.is_some() && some reader had recency.
scope keeps a row when any definition or read sits under it (node_in_scope's path rules). Rows sorted by (no finding last, key). counts = per status. No flag node at all -> flags empty and absence::empty(reason "no_match", note `no feature-flag read or definition was extracted (SDKs: LaunchDarkly, OpenFeature, Unleash, Flagsmith, Split; Flipt flags: yaml)`, mechanisms ["READS_CONFIG", "DEFINES_CONFIG"]).
Marker: `[flags] keys=<K> defined_files=<D> dead=<a> undefined=<b> single_site=<c> quiet=<d> quiet_evaluated=<true|false>`.

packets.title: Contract breaks vs a git rev in the engine: every schema copy / contract op paired old -> new (same identity FACT, through a move DERIVED) and judged by its format's evolution rules, plus orphaned clients; SCHEMA_FIELDS joins the delta's content cells
packets.rationale: LE.10c's contract_fields compares a PRODUCER against a CONSUMER at one point in time; nothing compares a contract against ITSELF across a change, which is the question a provider asks before merging ('did I just break my clients?'). MEASURED on HEAD: a git repo with openapi.yaml `GET /orders/{id}` returning {id, total}, committed, then `total` removed in the working tree (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CC/cbreak): `glia delta <repo> --base HEAD --json` -> counts all 0, no node row - the op's DOC_SECTION `contract::openapi::GET:/orders/{id}` keeps its CODE cell (`GET /orders/{id} — getOrder`) while its SCHEMA_FIELDS cell changes from `{"format":"openapi","response:200":[{id},{total}]}` to `[{id}]` (read from a scratch layout with glia_py.load_from_gmap(rebuild=False).node_cells), because engine/src/delta.rs:191 passes `content_cells: &[cell_type::CODE]` only. `glia contracts --fields` on it -> fields [] (no consumer pairs it). `glia contract-breaks` -> unrecognized subcommand. The rule machinery exists and is format-correct in engine/src/contract_fields.rs: collect_holders (:389), Holder::schema (:340), proto_rules (:751, symmetric), avro_rules (:913, writer vs reader), json_section (:1218) with truncation handling - all private today. Language-level public API (cargo-semver-checks parity) stays out: the graph has no visibility / signature cell.

packets.implementation:
```rust #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct ContractBreakArgs { pub avro_mode: &'static str /* backward (default) | forward | full */, pub breaking_only: bool } #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct SchemaChange { pub kind: &'static str /* message|operation|channel */, pub key: String, pub format: String, pub before: Option, pub after: Option, pub status: &'static str /* breaking|compatible|identical|unknown */, pub change: &'static str /* modified|removed|added|moved */, pub tier: &'static str, pub note: Option<&'static str>, pub changes: Vec /* producer = before, consumer = after */ } #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct OrphanedClient { pub client_qname: String, pub file: Option, pub line: Option, pub category: &'static str, pub target_qname: String, pub reason: &'static str /* target_removed|pairing_lost */, pub tier: &'static str } #[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct ContractBreaks { pub base: String, pub schemas: Vec, pub orphaned_clients: Vec, pub breaking: usize, pub absence: Option } pub fn contract_breaks(rev: &RevDelta, args: &ContractBreakArgs) -> ContractBreaks pub fn contract_breaks_vs_rev(repo_path: &str, base: &str, args: &ContractBreakArgs) -> Result ``` PAIRING: holders of both sides (collect_holders over rev.before.merged / rev.after.merged). The rev is built under the working tree's identity (LE.1b), so an unchanged qname is the SAME NodeId: pair by id -> tier fact. A holder id that rev.delta.moved_nodes maps (before -> after) pairs through the move -> tier derived, change moved. Before-only -> change removed: status breaking for a MESSAGE_TYPE and for an OpenAPI / AsyncAPI op (whoever used it loses it), tier fact; Pact ops (consumer contracts) are skipped. After-only -> added, compatible. Holders whose payloads are equal -> identical, not listed unless breaking_only is false and the caller asked for all (listing identical pairs is noise: they are counted, not rowed). EVOLUTION RULES (old = before, new = after): proto -> proto_rules(old, new) (wire rules are symmetric) plus `field_removed_unreserved` (compatible, note): a field number present before, absent after and not in the new `reserved` list - a later reuse of the number would break old readers. avro -> avro_rules(writer = old, reader = new) for backward, (new, old) for forward, both for full (a change breaking either direction breaks). openapi -> a new private fn openapi_evolution(old, new): request - a field required in new and absent or optional in old = breaking `new_required_request_field`; a shared field whose type changed = breaking `request_type_changed`; a field only old declares = compatible `request_field_removed`; response: - a section old has and new lacks = breaking `response_removed`; a field old has and new lacks = breaking `response_field_removed`; a changed type = breaking `response_type_changed`; a field only new has = compatible `response_field_added`. asyncapi payload -> old fields absent in new = breaking `payload_field_removed`, new fields = compatible `payload_field_added`, type change breaking. Every rule goes through json_section's truncation guard: a field absent from a TRUNCATED side is never reported removed (status unknown, note truncated). Formats differing across the pair -> unknown `format_mismatch`. ORPHANED CLIENTS: every key in rev.delta.removed_edges whose category is HTTP_CALLS / GRPC_CALLS / RPC_CALLS / GRAPHQL_CALLS / WS_CONNECTS and whose client end still exists in the after graph (directly or through a move) with NO edge of that category in the after graph: reason target_removed (the before target is in delta.removed_nodes) tier fact, else pairing_lost (the target survives but the resolver no longer pairs - a path / verb / host change) tier derived. Client located in the after graph, target named from the before graph. DELTA CONTENT CELLS: delta.rs gains `pub(crate) const CONTENT_CELLS: &[CellTypeId] = &[cell_type::CODE, cell_type::SCHEMA_FIELDS];` and locate_delta passes `content_cells: CONTENT_CELLS` (one list, so CD-5's rev chaining reads the same one), so a schema-only change is a `modified` row in `glia delta`, diff-impact and review (it was invisible: rationale). tests_for::rev_seeds / diff_impact's own-text rule compare CODE only, so a DOC_SECTION op or MESSAGE_TYPE that is modified is a seed as a non-container (CodeText::is_container false) - the intended effect: a contract change seeds its impact. ORDER: schemas by (status rank breaking < unknown < compatible, kind, key); orphans by (category, client, target). breaking = breaking schema rows + orphans. Absence (reason no_match, FACT) when neither side holds a contract and no client edge was removed. Marker: `[contract-breaks] base= pairs=

breaking= compatible= unknown= removed= added= orphaned_clients=`.

packets.title: Predictive test selection: tests_for rows carry failure and co-change signals (failed in the latest run, a covered seed on a failing trace, the test module co-changes with a seed's module), are ranked by them, gain co-change-only HEURISTIC rows and a --limit
packets.area: CC-6a tests_for re-rank by failure / trace / co-change
packets.rationale: tests_for orders purely structurally: (tier, depth, file, qname) (engine/src/tests_for.rs answer_for's final sort). The strongest predictors of a failing test - it failed last run; the changed code sits on a failing trace; the test file historically changes with the code file - are in the graph already (FAIL cells from LF.6b with role test / implicated; CO_CHANGES edges + module ATTN from LF.5b) and unused. MEASURED on HEAD (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CC/pts: shop/a.py price + place, tests/test_price.py calls price, tests/test_place.py calls place; a JUnit report with test_place_prices FAILED ingested by `glia tests ingest --junit`): `glia tests-for <pts> shop::a::price --json` -> [tests::test_price::test_price_doubles fact tests_edge 1, tests::test_place::test_place_prices derived reaches 2] - the test that just failed is listed LAST, and the `[tests] fail-cells ... mapped=1 (file_line=1 ...) fail_cells=1` line proves the FAIL cell sits on it. With a --limit (CI budgets), the failing test is the one cut. No test-report or history input changes the order today (grep FAIL / ATTN in tests_for.rs: 0 hits).

packets.implementation:
SIGNALS (computed once per answer from one pass over the graph's FAIL / ATTN cells and CO_CHANGES edges; skipped entirely when args.signals is false):
- `failed_last_run`: the test node (or, for a MODULE row, a FUNCTION / METHOD it DEFINES) carries a FAIL entry with role test (signals::fail_entries). With CC.9b's window this becomes 'failed in the newest run'; here every role-test entry is the latest run (a v1 snapshot holds one run).
- `seed_on_failing_trace`: a seed the row covers carries a FAIL entry with role implicated.
- `cochange`: the test's MODULE (the node itself or its nearest MODULE up nav.parent_of) and a covered seed's MODULE are joined by a CO_CHANGES edge; `cochange_permille` = 1000 * cochanges / commits of the seed's module (signals::pair_counts on the edge, signals::module_churn on the seed module): the directional confidence 'when the seed's file changed, this test file changed too', the best over covered seeds.
CO-CHANGE-ONLY ROWS: for each seed module, every CO_CHANGES neighbour MODULE whose ORIGIN provenance is test_fixture and that no row covers yet becomes a row: the MODULE itself (co-change is file-level, like the module TESTS pairing), tier heuristic, reason `cochange`, depth 1, path [(module, CO_CHANGES)], signals [cochange]. Never promoted: history is not a code reference.
ORDER (replaces the structural sort when any signal fired; with no FAIL / ATTN / CO_CHANGES in the graph every key below is equal and the order is exactly HEAD's): (failed_last_run desc, seed_on_failing_trace desc, tier rank, cochange_permille desc (None last), depth, file.is_none, file, qname).
LIMIT: after scope and sort, `limit` keeps the first N rows; omitted = the rest; test_files is computed AFTER the cut (what a runner is handed); untested is unaffected (computed before scope, as today).
MARKER: the `[tests-for] seeds=..` line is unchanged in format (cli/tests/tests_for_cli.rs:44 pins it); a second line when signals ran: `[tests-for] signals failed_last_run=<a> on_failing_trace=<b> cochange=<c> cochange_only=<d> omitted=<e>`.
CLI tests-for: `--limit N`, `--no-signals`; the table gains a `signals` column (comma-joined, `—` when none); `--files-only` prints the post-limit files. pyo3: `limit=None, signals=True` keywords on the three functions; rows carry `signals` and `cochange_permille`. Surfaces regenerated in this commit.

packets.title: Hotspots in the engine: churn rank x centrality rank for modules and symbols, from history ATTN cells and one global PageRank over the domain's centrality preset, ranks shown, no bare score
packets.rationale: Code that changes often AND sits where much depends on it is where defects and review effort concentrate (Tornhill's hotspots; Nagappan / Ball churn metrics). glia has both halves and never joins them: module churn and symbol blame recency are ATTN cells (LF.5b, engine/src/external/history.rs), and centrality is one PPR call away (MergedGraph::activate, graph/src/traversal.rs:322; with every node as a seed the personalisation is uniform, i.e. classic PageRank). MEASURED on a `git clone --no-hardlinks` copy of Kina (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CC/kina-git; 281 commits at a448fb3): `glia history sync <copy> --blame` -> `[history] sync ... commits=278 files=836 ... blame_files=300 runs=7511`; `glia analyze <copy> --format json` -> `[history] ingest ... commits=278 modules=528 unmapped=308 attn=528 blame_symbols=1251 cochange_pairs=82` - the inputs exist on a real repo and no answer ranks them (grep hotspot engine/src: 0 hits). The domain owns weights (CLAUDE.md: a new weight is one table row in CODE_TABLES), so the centrality lens is a preset there, not a list in the engine: structural DEFINES / CONTAINS, DOCUMENTS and TESTS edges must not make code 'central' (every module DEFINES its functions; a heavily tested function is not more depended on). No bare score: a composite float invites over-reading; the answer shows the two ranks and the population they rank in.

packets.implementation:
```rust
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct HotspotArgs { pub top: usize /* 20 per kind */, pub level: &'static str /* module|symbol|both */,
    pub min_churn: u32 /* 2 */, pub include_tests: bool /* false */, pub scope: Option<String> }   // impl Default
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Hotspot { pub level: &'static str, pub qname: String, pub kind: &'static str,
    pub file: Option<String>, pub line: Option<i64>, pub churn: u32 /* module commits | symbol span_changes */, pub lines_changed: Option<u64>,
    pub last_change: i64, pub churn_rank: usize, pub centrality_rank: usize, pub ranked: usize /* population both ranks range over */, pub tier: &'static str }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Hotspots { pub modules: Vec<Hotspot>, pub symbols: Vec<Hotspot>,
    pub history_head: Option<i64>, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
pub fn hotspots(merged: &MergedGraph, args: &HotspotArgs) -> Hotspots
```
POPULATIONS: modules = MODULE nodes with module_churn (source git) and commits >= min_churn; symbols = FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS nodes with symbol_blame and span_changes >= min_churn. Nodes with ORIGIN provenance test_fixture / generated / generated_proto are dropped unless include_tests (test code churns with its code and would crowd the list). scope keeps nodes under it (node_in_scope).
CENTRALITY: ONE `merged.activate(&all_ids, &cfg)` where all_ids = every node id in graph order, cfg = CODE_TABLES.activation_config(Some("centrality")) with damping 0.85 (classic PageRank: every node is a seed, so the restart is uniform), direction Forward (importance flows to what is called / used), top_k = all_ids.len(). A symbol's centrality = its PR; a module's = its own PR + the PR of every node whose nearest MODULE up nav.parent_of is it (a module is as central as what it defines). The domain preset (new row in code-domain/src/profile.rs activation_presets): `ActivationPreset { name: "centrality", overrides: &[(DEFINES, 0.0), (CONTAINS, 0.0), (DOCUMENTS, 0.0), (TESTS, 0.0)] }`; CO_CHANGES is 0 in the base already.
RANKS: per population, competition ranking (1 = highest; equal values share the lower rank: 1, 2, 2, 4), churn by (churn desc, lines_changed desc for modules / last_change desc for symbols), centrality by PR desc; PR ties are compared on the f64 bits' total order (`f64::total_cmp`), then qname, so the order is total and platform-stable. Order = (churn_rank * centrality_rank asc, max(churn_rank, centrality_rank) asc, qname asc); the product only orders, it is never emitted. Cut to `top` per level. Every row tier heuristic (history is not a code reference; centrality is a model).
Located through one Locator (1-based). history_head = signals::history_now. No population (no snapshot) -> both lists empty and Absence reason "no_history" (FACT): note `no git-history ATTN in the graph; run `glia history sync <repo>` (add --blame for symbol rows) and rebuild`.
Marker: `[hotspots] modules=<m>/<M> symbols=<s>/<S> pagerank_iterations=<i> head=<t>` (shown / ranked).

packets.title: Co-change suggestions in the engine (ROSE, pairwise): for changed files, the files that usually change with them, with DIRECTIONAL confidence from CO_CHANGES + module churn, support, and whether any static link joins them
packets.rationale: 'You changed X; Y usually changes with it' (Zimmermann et al., ROSE, ICSE 2004) is the reminder a reviewer wants, and it is strongest exactly where the graph is blind (no static link between X and Y). ```rust
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Clone, Debug)] pub struct CochangeArgs { pub min_confidence_permille: u32 /* 300 */, pub min_support: u32 /* 3 */,
    pub top: usize /* 20 */, pub unlinked_only: bool }   // impl Default
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct CochangeRow { pub file: String, pub module_qname: String,
    pub antecedent: Vec<String>, pub support: u32, pub antecedent_commits: u32, pub confidence_permille: u32,
    pub link: &'static str /* direct|bridged|none */, pub source: &'static str /* pairwise|multi */, pub tier: &'static str, pub note: Option<String> }
#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(serde::Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct Cochange { pub query_files: Vec<String>, pub unmapped: Vec<String>,
    pub rows: Vec<CochangeRow>, pub absence: Option<Absence> }
pub fn cochange(merged: &MergedGraph, files: &[String], args: &CochangeArgs) -> Cochange
```
1. Query files -> MODULE nodes by their POSITION file (exact repo-relative match, any repo; history.rs's mapping rule); a file with no MODULE goes to `unmapped`.
2. For each query module Q (file F): every CO_CHANGES edge with Q at either end gives the other module G (file H, H not a query file). support = pair_counts(edge).cochanges; antecedent_commits = module_churn(Q).commits; confidence_permille = 1000 * support / antecedent_commits - DIRECTIONAL (F -> H). Keep rows with support >= min_support and confidence >= min_confidence_permille.
3. link: LinkIndex over the whole graph (built once), link(repo, H, F') for every query file F' of the same repo, best of direct > bridged > none - LF.5c's exact semantics (bounded BFS through file-less nodes).
4. One row per consequent file: the antecedent with the highest confidence (ties: support, then antecedent path). Order: (confidence desc, support desc, file asc); unlinked_only keeps link == none. Cut to top. tier heuristic; note on link none: `no static link joins them (a blind spot, or coupling outside code)`.
DENOMINATOR NOTE (documented on the field): module churn counts every commit touching the file, while pair counts come from commits of 2..=MAX_COMMIT_FILES (30) mapped files, so confidence is a lower bound when mass commits touched F. Absence: no CO_CHANGES in the graph -> reason "no_history" (the `glia history sync` hint); no row passes the floors -> reason "no_match" naming the floors.

1. commit_file_sets: exactly ingest's alias walk (newest to oldest, alias[old] = current(new)), returning each commit's current-path set (unmapped paths included - the consumer filters); ingest keeps its outputs byte-identical (history_ingest.rs green).

Antecedents: Q (the query files of that repo) when |Q| >= 2, plus every Q \ {x} when 3 <= |Q| <= 8 (|Q| > 8: Q only; the cap keeps the lattice at 9 antecedents). For antecedent A: n_A = #sets ⊇ A; if n_A >= min_support, every file H outside Q in those sets gets support = #sets ⊇ A ∪ {H}, confidence_permille = 1000 * support / n_A. Then CC.11a's pairwise rows (single-file antecedents) are merged in; one row per consequent, the best rule by (confidence, support, larger antecedent, antecedent paths); source `multi` for |A| >= 2. Consequent files with no MODULE are kept with module_qname empty (a yaml or migration file co-changing is exactly the useful case); link is computed only for mapped files (else `none`).

packets.title: Weighted undirected view + seeded label propagation + modularity in activation::algo::community (the community substrate, integer weights, SplitMix64)
packets.rationale: CD-1 puts community detection in the domain-agnostic algorithm home. MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8: `ls activation/src/algo` = cycles.rs delta.rs mod.rs reach.rs, and `grep -rniE 'leiden|louvain|label.propagation|modularity' activation/src engine/src graph/src store/src` finds nothing, so no community code exists anywhere. The algo home only has a DIRECTED, UNWEIGHTED CSR (`Adjacency`, activation/src/algo/mod.rs): community quality (modularity) needs an undirected weighted view with merged parallel edges and per-node strengths, which Leiden (CD.1b), the split cuts (CD.2a) and the quotient graphs all share, so it lands first as its own module. packets.title: Seeded Leiden (fast local moving, refinement, aggregation) over WeightedGraph with exact integer gains, the LPA fallback over an edge cap, and WeightedGraph::quotient
packets.rationale: The plan picks Leiden over Louvain because Louvain can return DISCONNECTED communities (a community whose only bridge node moved out) - a 'community' in a code answer must be a connected set someone can read. Leiden's refinement phase guarantees connected, locally optimal communities. Nothing implements either at HEAD (see CD.1a's grep). Reference behaviour to beat on real code (networkx Louvain on Kina at HEAD): modularity 0.841 over 137 communities in 0.23 s; the largest groups are vertical feature slices (backend::internal::{services,repository,handlers} of one feature; frontend::src::app pages) - the shape a community summary should surface. Aggregation is the quotient graph CD-2 also needs, so `WeightedGraph::quotient` is public here.
entry_points: activation/src/algo/community.rs (CD.1a) - add leiden(), communities() dispatcher, WeightedGraph::quotient()
activation/src/algo/community.rs (new)
packets.implementation:
```rust
pub fn leiden(g: &WeightedGraph, opts: &CommunityOptions) -> Partition;
pub fn communities(g: &WeightedGraph, opts: &CommunityOptions) -> Partition; // leiden unless the view has more than opts.leiden_edge_cap pairs -> label_propagation
impl WeightedGraph { pub fn quotient(&self, membership: &[u32], k: usize) -> WeightedGraph; } // node i of the result = community i; ids NodeId(i as u64)
```
Gain (move node v with strength k_v, weight k_vC into community C of total strength K_C, resolution num/den, 2m = total): compare `den * 2m * k_vC - num * k_v * K_C` as i128 - every decision is an exact integer comparison, identical on every platform. 1. Fast local moving: a VecDeque of all nodes in SplitMix64(seed) shuffled order plus an in-queue bitmap; pop v, remove it from its community, score every neighbouring community (a Vec<u64> scratch indexed by community + a touched list, cleared after), take the best strictly positive gain over staying (ties: the smaller community id; staying wins a tie), move, and enqueue neighbours not in the new community and not queued. 2. Refinement (deterministic Leiden): inside each community S from step 1, start from singletons; visit S's nodes in the seeded order; a node still a singleton that is well connected to S (`den * 2m * k_{v,S\v} >= num * k_v * (K_S - k_v)`) merges into the refined sub-community T within S with the best non-negative gain among WELL-CONNECTED T that v has an edge into (k_vT > 0: a merge always follows an edge, so every refined sub-community is connected; a strength-0 node never merges) (T well connected: `den * 2m * w(T, S\T) >= num * K_T * (K_S - K_T)`), ties by smallest id; randomised selection (theta) is replaced by this greedy choice and the substitution is documented in the module doc. 3. Aggregate: the refined communities become nodes of `quotient()` (self weights carry internal weight); the initial partition of the aggregate is step 1's (the Leiden trick), then repeat from 1 until a level changes nothing or max_levels. Flatten memberships back to the original nodes. Connectivity pass (the guarantee test (3) pins, independent of how many levels ran): one BFS per community over its induced subgraph; a community with k > 1 components is split into k communities. Splitting never lowers modularity (no internal edge is lost, the (K_c/2m)^2 penalty only shrinks), so this is a pure improvement that makes 'every community is connected' hold by construction even when max_levels stops the loop early. Then renumber canonically as CD.1a. communities(): pairs > leiden_edge_cap -> label_propagation, Method::LabelPropagation in the result so the caller can say which ran.

packets.title: Min cuts in activation::algo::cut: heap-based Stoer-Wagner (global min cut plus every phase cut) and iterative Dinic s-t max-flow / min cut, u64 capacities, over WeightedGraph
packets.rationale: CD-2 suggests where a service could be cut: Stoer-Wagner finds the cheapest unsupervised bisection of the module / community quotient, Dinic answers the anchored question 'what is the least coupling I must cut to separate X from Y'. MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8: `grep -rniE 'stoer|dinic|max.?flow|min.?cut' activation/src engine/src graph/src` finds nothing; activation::algo has reach / delta / cycles only. Raw global min cuts are notoriously unbalanced on code graphs (the cheapest cut peels one leaf module), so the algorithm also returns every PHASE cut Stoer-Wagner computes on the way - CD.2b chooses the best balanced one among them instead of inventing a heuristic partitioner.
entry_points: activation/src/algo/cut.rs (new, C0.3 slot `activation mod algo::cut`) - stoer_wagner, min_st_cut, MinCut, PhaseCut, StCut
activation/src/algo/community.rs (CD.1a) WeightedGraph - read-only input type
packets.acceptance: Unit tests in activation/src/algo/cut.rs: (1) sw_matches_brute_force - 300 LCG weighted graphs with n 2..10: the Stoer-Wagner weight equals the minimum over all 2^(n-1)-1 bipartitions; (2) sw_phases_cover_the_min - one phase cut has the global weight; every phase cut's weight is the true weight of its side; (3) dinic_matches_brute_force - same graphs, every (s, t) pair: flow == min s-t cut by enumeration, and the source_side separates s from t with exactly that weight; (4) multi_terminal - sources {0,1} / sinks {6,7} on a ladder graph gives the rung-count flow; (5) disconnected_is_zero - two components -> weight 0, side = one component; (6) path_100k_no_stack_overflow - a 100,000-node path (weights 1) runs Dinic end to end in a debug build; (7) deterministic - repeat runs identical. Gate: `cargo test -p glia-activation algo::cut`; `grep -c code_domain activation/src/algo/cut.rs` prints 0. PRE-FIX BASELINE (HEAD 2170ff8): no min-cut or max-flow routine in the workspace.

packets.title: glia_engine::splits (global mode): the module or community quotient of a scope, Stoer-Wagner bisection chosen among the phase cuts by ratio with a balance floor, recursive to N parts; cut edges located at their evidence sites; each part diffed against `glia arch`
packets.rationale: Microservice decomposition suggestions (the Mono2Micro / Service Cutter use case in the research list) need three things glia already has - the structural graph, the `arch` service keying and located edge evidence - and one it lacks: a cut. At HEAD there is no split answer (`glia splits` -> unrecognized subcommand, exit 2, measured on a Kina archive copy) and `glia arch` only reports the services that exist (Kina: 5 services, backend 1,761 nodes / 151 files, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/kina_arch.txt). The unit of a split must be something a team can move: the default quotient is the MODULE (the file), with nodes that have no module parent (ROUTE / ENDPOINT via HANDLED_BY, etc.) attached to their strongest neighbour's module; communities (CD.1d) are the alternative unit. Data nodes stay out of the quotient - they are the shared resources CD.2c reports.

packets.title: splits, anchored mode and the blockers: Dinic s-t cut between two seeds or scopes, shared-write data entities across the proposed parts (ACCESS_MODE), and the dependency cycles between parts with located witnesses
packets.area: CD-2 service splits - s-t mode, shared writes, part cycles
packets.rationale: A cut is only half the answer: what stops the split is (a) a database both sides WRITE (a shared-write entity forces a shared schema or a new API) and (b) calls in both directions between the proposed services (a distributed cycle). glia already records both facts: ACCESSES_DATA edges carry the LE.4a ACCESS_MODE cell (read / write / read_write; engine/src/effects.rs ~725 reads it) and algo::cycles has Tarjan SCC (LE.6a). The anchored question ('separate services/payments from services/orders at the least coupling') is a min s-t cut, which Stoer-Wagner cannot answer. MEASURED at HEAD: no answer computes any of the three; on Kina the most-accessed data entities are data_entity:sql:users (fan-in 73) and data_entity:sql:trades (57) (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/kina.json) - exactly the shared resources a backend split would trip over. VERIFIED at HEAD by the verifier (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/vfy_split, `glia effects --json`): Python sqlite3 `conn.execute("INSERT INTO orders ...")` -> data_entity:sql:orders mode write, `UPDATE orders ...` -> write, `SELECT * FROM ledger` -> read, each an ACCESSES_DATA edge located at the execute line - so the fixture below mints the ACCESS_MODE cells this packet reads.

packets.area: CD-3 suspected edges - engine gaps category
packets.rationale:
`glia gaps` lists orphans (an ENDPOINT with no HTTP_CALLS, a queue producer with a tag-only topic) and the overlay section that could repair them, but never proposes the missing edge itself. MEASURED at HEAD on a git-archive copy of Kina (`GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 glia gaps <kina> --json`, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/kina_gaps.json, re-read by the verifier): unpaired_endpoint=21 and unpaired_route=11, and the pairs are visible by eye - `endpoint:POST:${…}/read-all @frontend` (frontend/src/app/features/notifications/notifications.service.ts:86) vs ROUTE `POST /notifications/read-all @backend` (backend/internal/handlers/notifications.go:35); `endpoint:POST:${…}/${…}/read` (:77) vs `POST /notifications/:id/read` (:37); `endpoint:GET:${…}/smr${…}` vs `GET /smr` - each endpoint got suggest=constants because its base is `${environment.apiUrl}/notifications` (an imported env object), so the HTTP resolver could not pair it. The graph already knows how these mechanisms pair (Kina has 89 ENDPOINT -HTTP_CALLS-> ROUTE edges), which is the learned triple the plan names. `glia gaps --category suspected_edge` fails at HEAD: `error: invalid value 'suspected_edge' for '--category <CATEGORY>'` (exit 2). The overlay loop (CE-3) is the verifier: a row is a suggestion, always HEURISTIC. OVERLAP FIXED BY THE VERIFIER: CE.3a (this run) adds `draft: Option<String>` - a pre-filled, HEURISTIC overlay stanza - and a stable `id` to every GapRow; the draft of this packet added a second field (`overlay`) for the same thing. One field: suspected_edge rows fill CE.3a's `draft` and a CE.3a-style id, so CE-3's propose / try / accept loop consumes them with no special case.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.1 merge): CE.3a's FINAL dropped `draft` (its verifier: 'CD.3b already adds GapRow.overlay') while this packet's FINAL dropped `overlay` (assuming CE.3a's `draft`), so neither added the field. Resolved: THIS packet adds `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] pub draft: Option<String>` to GapRow after CE.3a's `id` (None on every other row, so no other row's JSON changes). The gap link follows CE.3b's `# gap: <id>` COMMENT convention, not a `gap =` key (glia_config's deny_unknown_fields would default the whole overlay.toml on an unknown key), so the draft is directly pasteable and no overlay_text() helper is needed.

packets.implementation:
1. Learned triples: over all_edges() of the FLOW_MECHANISMS categories, count (kind(from), category, kind(to)) in a BTreeMap<(u32,u32,u32), usize>; a triple is learned at support >= 2 (MIN_SUPPORT). Nothing is hard-coded per mechanism except HTTP's method rule. 2. Orphans: nodes x whose kind is the source kind of a learned triple (k_x, c, k_y) and that have no outgoing c edge (for an ENDPOINT also not `<unresolved>`: those are unresolved_endpoint's job). Targets: nodes of kind k_y; `target_unpaired` = no incoming c edge. 3. Channel similarity: tokens of channel_of(qname, name), lower-cased, split on non-alphanumerics; a `${…}`, `:id`, `{id}`, `<id>` segment becomes the wildcard PARAM; drop the fixed stop list [api, v1..v9, http, https, www]. Score (per-mille) = suffix-aligned match: walk both token lists from the end, PARAM matches any one token, count matches until the first mismatch; score = 1000 * matches / known_tokens(orphan) when the orphan path starts with a PARAM (its prefix is unknown), else 1000 * matches / max(len). `matches` counts non-PARAM equalities only, and an orphan with no non-PARAM token is skipped. HTTP: the method must equal the route's (or the route is ANY). Candidates: an inverted index token -> targets (BTreeMap<String, Vec<u32>>), each orphan scores only targets sharing >= 1 non-PARAM token - never all pairs. 4. Structural: `Neighbourhoods` over the carry adjacency (Adjacency::carry); score_pairs(owner, handler) where owner = the orphan's CALLS / USES predecessor (gaps' `callers` view) and handler = the target's HANDLED_BY successor; boost = min(1000, AA / 2); RA is printed in the detail. 5. Co-change: a CO_CHANGES edge between the owner's MODULE and the handler's MODULE -> 1000. 6. score = (600 * channel + 150 * structural + 150 * cochange + 100 * [target_unpaired] * 1000) / 1000, kept when >= 500 and channel >= 500; top 3 targets per orphan; rows sorted with the gaps row order. Row: category suspected_edge, qname / kind / file / line of the ORPHAN (Locator, 1-based), detail = `<CATEGORY> -> `<target qname>` (<file>:<line>) score=0.87 channel=1.00 aa=<n> ra=<n> cochange=no target_unpaired=yes triple=ENDPOINT-HTTP_CALLS->ROUTE seen 89x`, suggest `edge`, tier HEURISTIC, draft = `# gap: <id>
[[edge]]
from = "<orphan qname>"
to = "<target qname>"
category = "<CATEGORY>"
note = "glia suspected_edge score=0.87"
` (the first line is CE.3b's gap-link comment; qnames exactly as QnameIndex binds them, TOML basic-string escaped; origin left to its default `llm`). A suspected row never mutates the graph. packets.title: Seeded MinHash signatures and LSH banding in activation::algo::minhash, integer-only hashing, plus exact Jaccard over sorted id sets
packets.rationale: Near-duplicate flows need set similarity at scale: comparing every pair of entry flows is quadratic (Kina already has 135 non-trivial flows and 16 pairs at Jaccard >= 0.8, measured with an exact pairwise Python pass over HEAD's analyze JSON, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/kina.json); a big repo has thousands. MinHash + LSH banding finds candidate pairs in near-linear time and an exact Jaccard check verifies them. MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8: `grep -rni minhash` over the workspace is empty. The hash must be integer-only so signatures are identical on every platform.
entry_points: activation/src/algo/minhash.rs (new, C0.3 slot `activation mod algo::minhash`) - MinHasher, lsh_candidates, jaccard_sorted
activation/src/algo/community.rs (CD.1a) pub(crate) SplitMix64 - reused for the per-permutation seeds
packets.implementation:
```rust
pub struct MinHasher { seeds: Vec<u64> }
impl MinHasher { pub fn new(k: usize, seed: u64) -> Self; pub fn signature(&self, set: &[u64]) -> Vec<u64>; } // min over the set of mix64(x ^ seed_i); empty set -> all u64::MAX
pub fn lsh_candidates(sigs: &[Vec<u64>], bands: usize, rows: usize) -> Vec<(u32, u32)>; // sorted, deduplicated, i < j; sigs.len() <= u32::MAX
pub fn jaccard_sorted(a: &[u64], b: &[u64]) -> (u32 /*intersection*/, u32 /*union*/);
```
mix64 = the SplitMix64 finaliser (xor-shift-multiply, wrapping) - integer only. seeds = k draws of SplitMix64(seed). LSH: for each band, hash its `rows` values with mix64 chaining into a u64 key; bucket (key -> Vec<u32>) in a BTreeMap per band (no HashMap iteration); every bucket with >= 2 members emits its pairs; a bucket over 2,000 members is skipped and counted (a degenerate band - every flow sharing a hub) rather than emitting millions of pairs. bands * rows must equal k (asserted).
packets.acceptance: Unit tests in activation/src/algo/minhash.rs: (1) estimate_tracks_jaccard - 50 LCG set pairs with true Jaccard in [0.1, 0.9], k = 256: |estimate - true| <= 0.125 for every pair and the mean absolute error <= 0.03 (the estimate's standard deviation is at most 0.5/sqrt(256) = 0.031, so the draft's 0.08 bound is 2.6 sigma and over 50 pairs would fail about 40% of seed choices; 0.125 is 4 sigma); (2) identical_sets_identical_signatures and empty_set_all_max; (3) lsh_finds_near_pairs - 200 random sets with 10 planted pairs at Jaccard >= 0.85, bands 32 x rows 4: all 10 planted pairs are candidates; (4) deterministic_and_order_free - a set's signature is independent of its element order; same seed -> same seeds vector; (5) jaccard_sorted_exact - hand-checked sets. Gate: `cargo test -p glia-activation algo::minhash`. PRE-FIX BASELINE (HEAD 2170ff8): no MinHash / LSH in the workspace.

packets.title: Edge and node validity intervals in activation::algo::timeline: fold N consecutive snapshots and their move maps through algo::delta into [valid_from, invalid_at) intervals keyed by each item's newest identity
packets.rationale: The time-travel graph (Graphiti-style bi-temporal edges, from the research list) is a fold over consecutive graph deltas. LE.1a already computes one delta domain-free (activation/src/algo/delta.rs graph_delta: added / removed / moved nodes, added / removed edges keyed before any move) and LB.6 already pairs moved files (graph/src/identity.rs detect_moves_with -> MoveMap.nodes: old_id / new_id). What is missing - MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8, `grep -rniE 'valid_from|invalid_at|as_of|interval' activation/src engine/src store/src` finds nothing time-related - is the chaining: carrying each open interval's key through every later move so that one edge that survives a file rename is ONE interval, not a removal plus an addition. That fold is generic (ids, categories, move pairs), so it lives beside delta in activation::algo.

packets.implementation:
Frame: `[0..8) b"GLIAPCZ1" | u64 LE stamp_len | stamp bytes | u64 LE raw_len | lz4_flex::block::compress(bincode bytes)`. Dependency: `lz4_flex = { version = "0.11", default-features = false, features = ["std", "safe-encode", "safe-decode", "checked-decode"] }` (block API only, no unsafe, no frame format). load: magic mismatch -> try raw bincode (a 0.5.0 sidecar) just to print today's `[incremental] cache stamp mismatch (disk=... build=...)` line, return empty; stamp != CACHE_VERSION -> the same line, no decompression; raw_len > 64 x compressed length or > 4 GiB -> empty (a hostile or truncated file never allocates unbounded memory); decompress_into a Vec of raw_len; bincode error -> empty. save: bincode as today (BTreeMap order, deterministic), compress (lz4_flex block compression is deterministic for equal input), frame; the LC.11 comparison runs on the framed bytes, so an unchanged cache still writes nothing. The saved marker gains the sizes: `[incremental] saved <n> entries (btree, lz4 <raw> -> <framed> bytes) via <tmp>`. CACHE_VERSION is unchanged (still the build stamp: the new binary's stamp differs anyway).

packets.area: CD-7 format 3 - CODE cells as spans
packets.rationale: CODE cells copy the source text of every entity into the store. MEASURED at HEAD on glia's own layout (loaded read-only from a scratch copy through the 0.5.0 wheel with rebuild=False, node_cells over all 19,242 nodes, compared with the files at HEAD): 17,316 CODE cells totalling 20,291,052 bytes - 16,786 of them (20,213,210 bytes, 99.6%) are verbatim slices of their POSITION file starting on the POSITION start line; 79 cells (18,378 B) are not verbatim, 424 are JSON metadata (56,257 B, the queue / cron `sites` payloads), 17 have no POSITION, 10 match elsewhere in the file. So ~20 MB of every glia layout is a second copy of the repo. VERIFIER RE-MEASURE (same method, /tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CD/meas_code2.py over the scratch copy vs the files at HEAD): 17,235 CODE text cells / 20,281,991 bytes, 20,231,807 bytes verbatim on their POSITION start line; by file type .rs 18,930,448 (18,896,207 verbatim), .py 925,219, the rest < 101 KB each - so the largest shard (the Rust one) carries ~18.9 MB of CODE. The plan's decision: 'Rescope + CODE spans' - CODE becomes a span on disk, the text is fetched from the source. Readers of CODE text: projection-text node_doc_or_code (dense-text previews, projection-text/src/lib.rs ~132), graph identity's MODULE body hash (graph/src/identity.rs ~655 code_text), algo::delta content (Text only), engram-export code_cell (engram-export/src/lib.rs:532), neuropil's code viewer (crates/neuropil-app/src/code_viewer.rs renders Text / Json / Bytes payloads), py node_cells; the repo-graph wrapper's `read` tool already slices files by line span (repo_graph/server.py _read_one) and never reads CODE. Rehydrating on read from the manifest's recorded roots (LC.7) keeps every in-process reader unchanged whenever the source is present - the normal case, since a layout lives in its repo.

packets.implementation: Encode (with a source): for each node, its first POSITION cell gives (file, 0-based start_line); for each CODE cell with a Text payload, read the file through the source (once per file per shard), compute the byte offset of start_line, and look for the text's bytes starting at any byte of that line (a bounded scan: at most the line's length of start positions, each an exact slice compare). Found -> payload `Bytes([0x02, varint(file_ix), varint(start), varint(len), xxh64 as 8 LE bytes])` with the path interned in the STRINGS table (CD.7b). Not found / no POSITION / Json payload / no source -> stored as today (lossless). Decode (with a source): Bytes tag 0x02 under CODE -> slice [start, start+len) of the file, check xxh64 -> CellPayload::Text(String::from_utf8(slice)); missing file, short file, hash mismatch or invalid UTF-8 -> CellPayload::Json(CodeSpan::to_json()) = `{"code_span":{"file":"src/a.rs","start":120,"end":480,"xxh64":"<16 hex>"}}` and count it unresolved. Decode without a source (decode_repo_graph, inspect) -> the same Json span for every span. packets.title: SCIP importer in glia-snapshots (no protobuf): rebase document paths onto the repo, read each source, convert UTF-8 / UTF-16 / UTF-32 offsets without slicing mid-char, take the identifier at every definition and the call paren at every reference, drop locals and forward definitions, write `.glia/scip-snapshot/`
packets.rationale: The snapshot step is the non-deterministic half kept out of the build (history_sync / tests_ingest in snapshots/src/lib.rs are the model: build rows, write through code-domain, ensure the gitignore, print one marker). Three things need the source text and must happen here, never at build: (a) the name check - binding a SCIP definition 'by position, checked by name' needs the identifier text at its range, and the range's character offsets are in the document's PositionEncoding (scip.proto ~108-146: UTF-8 bytes, UTF-16 or UTF-32 code units; the proto says JVM/.NET/JS indexers use UTF-16, Python ones UTF-32, Go/Rust/C++ UTF-8), which must never be applied as byte offsets (UTF-8 byte-offset panics are a standing risk); (b) SCIP has no call role (SymbolRole, scip.proto ~524-547: Definition 0x1, Import 0x2, WriteAccess 0x4, ReadAccess 0x8, Generated 0x10, Test 0x20, ForwardDefinition 0x40), so whether a reference is a call is read at the site: the next non-blank char after the range on its line is `(` (after an optional `::` and a balanced `<...>` generic list); (c) staleness - each document records the hash of the bytes it was indexed against. Putting this in glia-snapshots (not the CLI) keeps the CLI to wire decoding and transport, and lets it be tested without protobuf; the group rule forbids a protobuf DEPENDENCY in snapshots, and this module has none (Cargo.lock unchanged). GLIA_GITIGNORE (snapshots/src/lib.rs ~42) lists vectors.jsonl, docs-snapshot/, history-snapshot/, test-snapshot/ and is written only when `.glia/.gitignore` is absent (ensure_glia_gitignore never overwrites), so a repo that already has one would commit a large SCIP snapshot unless the dir also ignores itself (the LC.9 `*` pattern).

INPUT TYPES (pub, plain data; the CLI decoder, CE.1c, fills them from protobuf): `ScipIndexInfo { tool, tool_version, project_root: String /* the file:// URI as the index gives it */ }`; `enum PositionEncoding { Unspecified, Utf8, Utf16, Utf32 }` with `from_proto(i32)`; `ScipOccurrenceIn { start_line, start_char, end_line, end_char: i32, symbol: String, roles: i32 }`; `ScipSymbolIn { symbol: String, implements: Vec<String> }` (Relationship.is_implementation targets); `ScipDocumentIn { relative_path, language, encoding, occurrences, symbols }`. `#[non_exhaustive] ScipImportOptions { prefix: Option<String>, surface: &'static str }` (Default: None, "lib"). `#[derive(Serialize)] #[non_exhaustive] ScipImportSummary { documents, skipped, defs, refs, calls, symbols, locals, forward, bad_ranges, encoding_unspecified: usize }`.
ScipImporter::new(repo_root, info, opts): canonicalize the repo; base = --prefix when given (validated: relative, no `..`), else project_root parsed as `file://` + percent-decoded absolute path, canonicalized, made relative to the repo when inside ("" when equal); outside or unparsable -> base "" and one stderr line `[scip] warning: project_root <uri> is outside <repo>; document paths read as repo-relative`.
document(d) (called once per decoded document, so memory is one document plus the kept rows): path = base joined with relative_path, `/`-normalised; an absolute path or a `..` component -> skipped (never read outside the repo); read `<repo>/<path>` through symlink_metadata + canonicalize with a prefix check (a symlink is followed only when its target stays inside); missing, not a regular file, over 8 MiB or not UTF-8 -> skipped. lines = split on '\n', a trailing '\r' stripped. Encoding Unspecified reads as UTF-16 (the LSP default) and counts encoding_unspecified once per document. `pub fn unit_offset_to_byte(line: &str, units: i32, enc) -> Option<usize>` walks char_indices summing len_utf8 / len_utf16 / 1 and returns None when the offset lands inside a char, is negative or passes the line end - a str is never sliced by a unit count. Occurrences: an empty symbol or a `local ` symbol -> locals += 1, dropped (document-local variables have no graph node); roles & 0x40 (ForwardDefinition) -> forward += 1, dropped (a prototype is neither the definition nor a use). roles & 0x1 (Definition): single-line range only, name = line.get(start..end) -> def row; else a reference row { line: start_line, call: next_is_call(line, end_byte), write: roles & 0x4 != 0, import: roles & 0x2 != 0 }. `pub fn next_is_call(line, end_byte) -> bool` skips spaces / tabs, then an optional `::` and a balanced `<...>` of at most 256 bytes on the same line, and is true iff the next char is `(`. A range on a line the file does not have, or whose offsets do not convert, is dropped (bad_ranges). Symbols are interned into a BTreeMap<String, tmp id>; ScipSymbolIn.implements recorded per symbol. The document's source_hash = code_domain::snapshots::source_hash(bytes).
finish(): keep only symbols some kept row or kept implements names; assign final ids 0..n in symbol-string order (deterministic whatever the index order); rewrite every row / implements to final ids (implements sorted, deduped); documents sorted by path, rows by (line, s, flags); a document with no kept row is dropped (counted skipped); write_scip(root, meta, ...) (meta.project_root = base); ensure_glia_gitignore (now listing scip-snapshot/) and `<dir>/.gitignore` = "# written by glia scip import - regenerable\n*\n" when absent; print once `[scip] import repo=<label> tool=<tool>@<version> documents=<d> skipped=<k> defs=<n> refs=<r> calls=<c> symbols=<s> locals=<l> forward=<f> bad_ranges=<b> encoding_unspecified=<u> surface=<surface>` (label = repo_label(root), the history marker's). Nothing is written unless finish runs, so a caller that fails mid-index writes nothing.

packets.implementation:
DECODER (James 2026-09-30): a hand-written wire reader for the ~20 fields read, CLI-side - no dependency, no Cargo.lock change, streams one Document at a time, unknown fields skipped by wire type so schema additions cannot break it. The snapshot format (CE.1a) is the contract between the decoder and the build.
WIRE (wire.rs): varint of at most 10 bytes (the 10th may carry bit 0 only, else Err 'varint overflow'); tag = varint, field = tag >> 3, wire type = tag & 7: 0 varint, 1 fixed64 (skip 8), 2 LEN, 5 fixed32 (skip 4); 3 / 4 (groups) -> Err. int32 fields read as u64 and cast `as i64 as i32` (a negative int32 is a 10-byte varint). Every LEN is checked against the bytes left in its parent BEFORE any allocation (past the parent -> Err 'truncated <message> at byte <n>'); top-level LEN fields are capped at MAX_FIELD_BYTES = 256 MiB. Nested messages decode from `&[u8]` slices of the already-read field with a cursor, so recursion depth is fixed by the schema (Index > Document > Occurrence > range), never by input. Top level: tags from a BufReader until clean EOF at a tag boundary (EOF inside a tag, length or payload is Err); field 1 -> Metadata -> sink.metadata; field 2 -> the LEN payload read into one reused Vec<u8>, decoded -> sink.document(doc)?; field 3 (external_symbols) -> skipped and counted (targets outside the repo have no node); any other field skipped, counted unknown_fields. Metadata after a document is accepted and counted late_metadata. Ranges: `range` (field 1) packed (LEN of varints) or unpacked (repeated varint) - 3 elements = [line, start, end], 4 = [sl, sc, el, ec], other counts -> malformed_ranges and the occurrence dropped; single_line_range / multi_line_range win over `range` when both are set (the proto's rule). Structs: `WireMetadata { tool_name, tool_version, project_root, text_document_encoding }`, `WireDocument { relative_path, language, position_encoding, occurrences, symbols }`, `WireOccurrence { sl, sc, el, ec, symbol, roles }`, `WireSymbol { symbol, implements: Vec<String> }` (Relationship.is_implementation targets only), `DecodeStats { documents, occurrences, symbols, external_symbols, unknown_fields, malformed_ranges, late_metadata }`; `trait IndexSink { fn metadata(&mut self, m: WireMetadata) -> Result<(), String>; fn document(&mut self, d: WireDocument) -> Result<(), String>; }`.
COMMAND (mod.rs): `glia scip import <REPO> <INDEX> [--prefix <DIR>]` (variant doc: 'SCIP index snapshot (CE-1): decode a compiler-grade SCIP index (scip-python, scip-typescript, scip-java, scip-go, rust-analyzer scip) and write <repo>/.glia/scip-snapshot/, which the next build ingests as FACT-tier CALLS / USES / IMPLEMENTS / INHERITS_FROM evidence; the build itself never reads the index. Exits 1 when the index cannot be decoded (nothing written).'). packets.implementation:
`scip_edges(merged, input)`: `let snap = read_scip(&input.root)?` (absent dir: silent, nothing changes, the build is byte-identical). SPAN INDEX (per repo, once): for every graph with g.repo == input.repo, every node with a POSITION cell (history::position: file, 0-based start_line, end_line inclusive) and a nav kind / name: `BTreeMap<file, Vec<Span { start, end, id, kind, name }>>`, each Vec sorted by (end - start, start, id) so the first containing span is the innermost and ties break by id. DEF_KINDS = [FUNCTION, METHOD, CLASS, STRUCT, INTERFACE, ENUM, ATTRIBUTE, STATE_VAR]; OWNER_KINDS = FUNCTION / METHOD first, then CLASS / STRUCT / INTERFACE / ENUM; a file's MODULE from history::module_files.
STALE: per document, read `<root>/<path>` and compare code_domain::snapshots::source_hash with the row's source_hash; unreadable or different -> the document is skipped whole (stale += 1). No offset slicing happens at build: the importer stored names and call flags.
BIND DEFS: for each def row, the innermost span in its file with kind in DEF_KINDS, start <= line <= end and nav name == row.name exactly; none -> unbound += 1. A symbol whose rows bind two different nodes is ambiguous (removed, counted) - never guessed. Result BTreeMap<u32, NodeId>.
REFERENCES: rows whose symbol is bound to T; import rows are counted `imports` and emit nothing (parser IMPORTS are already FACT). owner = innermost OWNER_KINDS span containing the line, else the file's MODULE, else skipped (unowned). Category / rule: T is FUNCTION / METHOD and row.call -> CALLS `call_site`; T callable and !call -> USES `callable_ref`; otherwise USES `reference` (`reference_write` when row.write). owner == T with call_site is kept (recursion). Dedup on (owner, T, category) keeping the smallest (file, line): documents iterate by path and rows by line, so the first seen wins.
EXISTING EDGES: one pass over the repo graphs' edges and every cross edge builds a lookup-only HashMap<(NodeId, NodeId), Vec<EdgeCategoryId>> (never iterated for output). Same (from, to, category) present -> confirmed += 1 (CE.1e decides what the one EVIDENCE cell then says); same (from, to) with another category -> category_differs += 1, nothing added (glia's own classification stands); otherwise push onto merged.cross_edges `Edge::new(owner, T, category, Confidence::Strong)` with the cell `Evidence::emitter(format!("scip:{tool}")).rule(rule).at(path, line).to_cell()`, tool = the meta's tool lowercased with every char outside [a-z0-9_-] as '_' (empty -> `index`): one EVIDENCE cell, basis site, 0-based line; the Finalize fill leaves it and the sort orders it.
TIER: STAGES += "scip"; why.rs stage_tier: "parser" | "extractor" | "docs" | "graph" | "scip" => FACT (the target is bound by a type-aware indexer and the call / non-call split is read at the site); tier_of adds the note `resolved by a SCIP index (<tool>)` for stage scip.
MARKER once per repo with a complete snapshot: `[scip] ingest repo=<label> tool=<tool> documents=<d> stale=<s> defs=<n> bound=<b> unbound=<u> ambiguous=<a> refs=<r> imports=<i> unowned=<o> added=<e> (calls=<c> uses=<x>) confirmed=<f> category_differs=<k>`.
