packets.risks: False binding: containment + exact name can pick the wrong node when two same-named members share one span (overloads on one line) - the ambiguity rule drops a symbol that binds two nodes. Edge inflation: references to types and attributes add USES edges; they are real references, and blast radius follows USES, so impact answers grow - the marker counts them; measure on one real index before release. DELTA CAVEAT: a delta build of a rev reads the same untracked snapshot (git_rev copy_untracked_inputs), but the per-document hash check skips every file that differs from the indexed bytes, so a file changed between the rev and the working tree carries SCIP edges on the side the index was made for only - `glia delta` / diff-impact then list those edges as added (or removed); documented in docs/overlay.md (CE.1c) and an open question. Determinism: every output-bearing iteration is over sorted Vecs / BTreeMaps; the existing-edge HashMap is lookup-only; the stage runs in the single-threaded Post stage. Panic isolation: the stage never slices strings; a malformed snapshot is rejected whole by read_scip. Same files as other groups: engine/src/external/mod.rs (CA.4 declares infer_wrappers there; CE.3b edits repo_inputs) and engine/src/why.rs (CC.3 makes tier_of pub(crate)) - sequence, not one wave.

EDGE POSITIONS: CE.1d's lookup map becomes `HashMap<(NodeId, NodeId, EdgeCategoryId), Vec<EdgePos>>`, EdgePos = Intra { graph, edge } | Cross(usize) (lookup only). Mutations are collected into a Vec<(EdgePos, Evidence)>, sorted by position and applied after every lookup, so nothing depends on HashMap order.
CONFIRM RULE for a SCIP triple (from, to, cat) with a glia edge e at pos: old = Evidence::of(e); stage = old emitter's stage. (a) stage not in {parser, extractor, graph} (resolver, pass, docs, overlay, history, scip) -> confirmed_other += 1, untouched (a merge recomputes resolver / pass edges by emitter). (b) t = why::tier_of(old.as_ref(), e).0 == fact -> confirmed_fact += 1, untouched. (c) heuristic or derived -> evidence::attach(e, Evidence::emitter(format!("scip:{tool}")).rule(format!("confirms:{old_emitter}{}", old_rule.map(|r| format!("/{r}")).unwrap_or_default())).at(path, line)) and e.confidence = Confidence::Strong; upgraded += 1 (attach replaces the one EVIDENCE cell, code-domain/src/evidence.rs attach). Duplicate glia edges on one key are all re-stamped. why.rs: for a rule starting `confirms:` tier_of's note is `confirmed by a SCIP index (<tool>) at <file>:<line+1>; first emitted by <old emitter>[ (<old rule>)]`; the tier stays the scip stage's FACT.
RELATIONSHIPS: for every symbol A bound to node a and every id B in A.implements bound to node b (a != b): category = IMPLEMENTS when b's kind is INTERFACE, or both are FUNCTION / METHOD (a method implementing an interface method, the shape glia's method-level IMPLEMENTS takes), else INHERITS_FROM. Then the confirm rule on (a, b, category); absent -> push a Strong cross edge with Evidence rule `implementation` located at A's definition row. An existing (a, b) edge of the other heritage category counts category_differs and adds nothing.
CONTRADICTIONS: for every glia edge whose tier is heuristic, whose evidence has a site (file, line), whose category is CALLS / USES / INHERITS_FROM / IMPLEMENTS and whose document is not stale: if the snapshot has, at that exact (file, line), a reference (or for heritage a definition with implements) bound to a node other than the edge's `to`, and no row there bound to the edge's `to` -> contradicted += 1 and one stderr line (sorted by file, line; capped at 20) `[scip] contradicts <from qname> -[<CAT> <emitter>/<rule>]-> <to qname> at <file>:<line+1>; index says <qname>`. The edge stays.
MARKER (a second line, once per repo with a snapshot): `[scip] confirm repo=<label> upgraded=<u> confirmed_fact=<f> confirmed_other=<o> relationships=<r> added_implements=<i> added_inherits=<h> contradicted=<c>`.

packets.title: Shared parse cache, engine half 1/2: a content address per cached file (blake3 over stamp, repo identity, language, path, module form, Go context, content) and ParseCache export - the keys and payloads the CLI's transport moves; no transport in the engine
packets.area: CE-2 shared cache - engine keys and export
packets.rationale: The parse cache (engine/src/cache.rs ParseCache ~246) is per checkout: a fresh clone, a CI runner or a second worktree pays every tree-sitter parse again. MEASURED at HEAD 2170ff8 with target/debug/glia on git-archive copies: glia itself cold `glia build` 9.66 s (routed 1630 files, reparsed 1435) vs warm 6.86 s (reused 1435), sidecar 38,024,576 bytes; quokka-stack cold 0.81 s vs warm 0.47 s (213 entries, 4,676,807 bytes). What a cached parse depends on, verified in code: the build stamp (CACHE_VERSION = glia_stamp::BUILD_STAMP, cache.rs ~46), the repo identity key baked into every NodeId (repo_canonical, `git:<remote>[/<rel>]` / `gitdir:` / `dir:<basename>`, walk_gating::repo_identity ~527), the language, the path, the MODULE form (route.rs ModuleQnames::plan ~1140 names a file's module by file name when a same-stem sibling exists; cached_under_other_form ~1278 rejects a parse cached under the other form), the go.mod module set for Go files only (extract.rs parse_one_as passes `go` to the Go parser alone; ParseCache.go_modules), and the content. The per-file key today is xxhash64 (content_hash, cache.rs ~95) - fine locally, but a shared store accepts objects from other machines, so the address and the authenticity check need a cryptographic hash. blake3 1.8.5 is in the local cargo registry but not in Cargo.lock (neither is sha2); blake3 has keyed hashing built in (a MAC with no hmac crate). bincode 1.3.3 is the cache codec (engine/Cargo.toml). SECURITY.md lists 'a crafted source file, manifest or .gmap that crashes the parser or loader' as in scope: an object fetched from a store is untrusted bincode until verified. PLACEMENT (James 2026-09-30): the shared-cache transport - `glia cache push|pull|gc`, the signed object format, the directory and HTTPS stores, parallel fetch, GC - is CLI-only (CE.2c, CE.2e); the engine keeps only what needs its internals: the content-addressed keys (they hash the build stamp, the repo identity, the router's module plan and the Go context) and import / export on ParseCache (CE.2a exports, CE.2b imports), plus the whole-layout key / export / install (CE.2d). Nothing HTTP or transport-related ships in glia_engine or the glia-py wheel.

CacheKey::to_hex = 64 lower-hex chars, from_hex the inverse (Err on anything else). The key is an address, not a secret: the CLI's object MAC (CE.2c) authenticates.
PLAN (route.rs cache_plan): the walked files (walk_source_files) -> for every file with parser_route Some(lang): PlanRow { path, lang, module_qname: modules.module_qname(path), source: &str } - the same ModuleQnames::plan the build uses, so a key names exactly the form route_one checks.
ROWS (export.rs cache_rows): ident = repo_identity(root); walk; go = go_modules_for(...); plan -> `CacheRows { stamp: &'static str /* BUILD_STAMP */, repo_label, rows: Vec<CacheRow> }`, `CacheRow { path, lang, module_qname, key: CacheKey, content_hash: u64 /* the cache's xxhash of the bytes */ }`, rows in path order; #[non_exhaustive], serde::Serialize.
EXPORT (export.rs export_entries): rows as above; cache = ParseCache::load(repo_path); if cache.context() != (ident.key, go.context_key()) every row is stale (the sidecar was written under another identity) and nothing is exported; else per row: payload = cache.entry_payload(path, content_hash, lang) whose parse is not cached_under_other_form(parse, path, module_qname) -> `ExportedEntry { path, key, payload }`, else stale += 1. `Export { stamp, repo_label, entries, stale }` (#[non_exhaustive], Serialize). PAYLOAD: exactly `bincode::serialize` of that entry's CacheEntry { content_hash, lang, parse } (the parse through canonical_parse, cache.rs, LC.11, so equal parses give equal bytes) - `ParseCache::entry_payload`. It is per entry and independent of how the whole sidecar file is framed on disk: CD.7a's lz4 frame wraps the whole parse_cache.bin, never an entry, so this payload is the same with or without it. packets.title: Shared parse cache, engine half 2/2: ParseCache import - which files a checkout is missing, and a verified import of fetched payloads (content hash, language, module form, a random re-parse sample; one mismatch writes nothing) into the local parse cache
packets.area: CE-2 shared cache - engine import and verification
packets.rationale: Import is where trust matters: payloads come from another machine and are decoded with bincode, and a poisoned parse would put forged nodes and edges into a graph that answers as FACT. The local build already re-checks what it can (ParseCache::get compares the xxhash and the language, cache.rs ~323; route.rs ~985-994 rejects a parse cached under another MODULE form), but it cannot tell a correct parse of the right bytes from a crafted one. The trust model, as specced and kept by James 2026-09-30, has two modes: a keyed store (a MAC from a key only the CI writer and the team hold, checked by the CLI's object decode, CE.2c) and an explicitly trusted unsigned store (--unsigned), which pays for its trust with a random re-parse sample (default 32 entries). The checks that need the engine - the content hash and module form of the bytes checked out now, and a re-parse with the build's own parse code - live here; the MAC, the key match and the size cap are the transport's (CE.2c). The build must stay offline: an import only fills `<repo>/.glia/graph/parse_cache.bin`, after which an ordinary incremental build reuses the entries (LA.12's `[incremental] ... reused <n>` marker proves it). LC.11 (ParseCache::save skips an unchanged file) keeps a no-op import from rewriting the sidecar. PLACEMENT (James 2026-09-30): the shared-cache transport - `glia cache push|pull|gc`, the signed object format, the directory and HTTPS stores, parallel fetch, GC - is CLI-only (CE.2c, CE.2e); the engine keeps only what needs its internals: the content-addressed keys (they hash the build stamp, the repo identity, the router's module plan and the Go context) and import / export on ParseCache (CE.2a exports, CE.2b imports), plus the whole-layout key / export / install (CE.2d). Nothing HTTP or transport-related ships in glia_engine or the glia-py wheel.

packets.title: Whole-layout cache: a clean checkout at a known git tree pulls the finished `.glia/graph/` layout (keyed by stamp, repo identity, HEAD tree and the `.glia` input fingerprint) instead of building - engine layout key / export / verified install, CLI `--layout` transport
packets.rationale: Sharing parses saves only the parse phase: on glia itself (debug build, HEAD 2170ff8) a warm incremental build is still 6.86 s of the 9.66 s cold build (/tmp/claude-1000/-home-ivy-Code-glia/3ee9830a-1863-4451-a43c-2c46aa30c444/scratchpad/spec051/probe/CE/gliacopy), because the walk, the per-language graph builds, the 15 resolvers and the post-passes all rerun (the per-phase split is CA-9's measurement). A clean checkout at a commit CI already built can skip all of it: the layout (`<repo>/.glia/graph/`: manifest.json + shards + cross_stack.gmap; 77 MB / 32 files for glia) is a pure function of the build stamp, the repo identity, the tracked tree and the `.glia` inputs. Verified in code: NodeIds are path-independent (repo identity key, LB.1); POSITION files are repo-relative; the manifest records repo roots relative to the layout dir (persist.rs layout_meta ~130) and the `.glia` input fingerprint (store/src/layout.rs Manifest.external_inputs ~128, external_inputs_fingerprint ~1051); is_gmap_stale (~948) checks the build stamp, the input fingerprint and source mtimes newer than the manifest. git access already exists read-only in engine/src/git_rev.rs (fn git ~109 with GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0; resolve_rev ~126). The labels in the manifest's `repos` are the checkout's directory name (arch.rs repo_label_map ~407) and differ between machines, so a pulled manifest's labels are rewritten locally. This is read-mostly by construction: a layout is written whole into one checkout's own `.glia/graph/`, never shared for writes (the 0.5.0 Not-doing list excludes shared-gmap multi-agent writes). PLACEMENT (James 2026-09-30: CLI-only transport, CE.2d kept): the engine computes the layout key and exports / installs a layout (it owns persist, the manifest labels, load_layout and is_gmap_stale); the CLI packs the entries into a signed object and moves it through CE.2c's stores.

KEY (engine layout.rs layout_key): clean_head_tree(root) None -> LayoutKey::Dirty; else blake3 derive_key("glia layout object v1") over length-framed BUILD_STAMP, repo identity key, the HEAD tree id, and the external_inputs_fingerprint(root) map serialised as sorted `path\0hash\n` lines (the exact map the manifest records), the target facts `std::env::consts::ARCH`, pointer width and endianness (rkyv shard bytes are only reused on the same layout target; no packet verifies cross-target rkyv), plus the literal `overlay=on` (only the default overlay-applied layout is ever cached) -> LayoutKey::Clean { key: CacheKey, tree }.
EXPORT (export_layout): Dirty -> LayoutExport::Dirty; the layout must exist and be fresh (is_gmap_stale false) else ::Stale; else ::Ready { key, tree, entries: Vec<(name, bytes)> } - every regular file of the layout dir except parse_cache.bin (shared per file by CE.2a / CE.2b) and `*.tmp`, names validated to `[A-Za-z0-9._+-]{1,128}` with no `/`, sorted by name; total <= 1 GiB, per entry <= 512 MiB, else Err.
INSTALL (install_layout): re-derive layout_key locally; Dirty -> ::Dirty; a key that differs from the offered one -> ::Rejected("key mismatch"); names validated again (no path can leave the layout dir); unpack into `<layout>.pull.<pid>.tmp/` (a sibling dir), rewrite manifest.json's `repos[].label` to the local repo_label_map label and `repos[].root` to the local relative root (serde_json round trip of the manifest; nothing else touched), then move the entries into the layout dir (shards first, manifest.json last - a reader never sees a manifest naming shards not yet there), remove shards the new manifest does not name, and write the layout's self-ignoring .gitignore (persist::write_self_ignore). Then persist::load_layout(dir) must succeed and is_gmap_stale(dir, root) must be false; otherwise the new files are removed, the previous layout (kept aside in the tmp dir until this check) is restored, and the result is ::Rejected(reason). Success -> ::Installed. The enums are #[non_exhaustive].
CLI (cli/src/cmd/store/cache/layout.rs): OBJECT `b"GLIALY01"` | flags | key | entry_count u32 | per entry: name_len u16, name, data_len u64, data | MAC (CE.2c's Signing and keyed MAC; the same caps checked BEFORE allocation); rel = `v1/<stamp>/layout/<key>.gla`. `--layout` on push: export_layout -> Dirty / Stale print their result; store.has(rel) -> `present`; else pack + put -> `pushed`. packets.implementation:
BUILD: BuildOptions stays #[non_exhaustive] Clone + Debug + PartialEq + Eq. The override applies to the PRIMARY repo only (generate_one's repo; generate_many's first path): a candidate targets one repo's file. Walk sections are still read from disk; parse_candidate refuses a candidate carrying [walk] / [[project]], so the two cannot disagree (a merged text that keeps the base file's own [walk] passes the same content through). Only the overlay loop sets overlay_text (no CLI flag, no pyo3 parameter), and its builds are never persisted; BuildOptions' doc states that a build with overlay_text must never be written to a repo's default layout dir (the rule --no-overlay builds already follow).
CANDIDATE: a TOML text holding only [constants], [entrypoints] qnames, [[route_prefix]], [[wrapper]], [[edge]] (anything else -> Err naming the section: 'a candidate carries only overlay sections and entrypoints'), optional `version = 1`. A stanza names the gap(s) it targets with comment lines `# gap: gap:<16 hex>` directly above its table header (the table's decor prefix in toml_edit) or, for a constant, above its key. parse_candidate: toml_edit::DocumentMut::from_str; per stanza a StanzaRef { section: &'static str, index: usize /* 1-based within the candidate */, key: Option<String> /* constant name / entrypoints pattern */, gaps: Vec<String> /* parsed from the decor */ }; then glia_config::parse_str on the text (with `version = 1` prepended when absent) must report zero errors, else Err listing them (a candidate is all-valid or refused). StanzaRef displays as `wrapper#2`, `edge#1`, `route_prefix#1`, `constants.GATEWAY`, `entrypoints#3` - the handle try / accept / the CLI use.
MERGE(base_text, cand, only): base = DocumentMut of the base text, or `version = 1\n` when there is no file; per chosen stanza: array-of-tables -> push a clone of the candidate table (its `# gap:` decor kept, a harmless provenance note) onto base's array, created if absent; constants -> insert into base's [constants] (created if absent) - a name present with a different value is Err('constant <n> already pinned to <v>'), the same value is skipped (duplicates += 1); entrypoints -> append patterns not already in base's qnames. `Merged { text: String, refs: Vec<(StanzaRef, Location)>, duplicates: usize }` where Location is where each stanza landed (section, array index / key) so `without` removes exactly it. The merged text re-parsed with parse_str must have exactly the base's errors and section counts = base + added - duplicates; else Err (the writer can never produce a file the loader would drop). WITHOUT(merged_text, ref): remove that array element / key / array item from a DocumentMut of the merged text and render.
MARKER once per parsed candidate: `[overlay] candidate file=<path or -> stanzas=<n> (route_prefix=<a> wrapper=<b> edge=<c> constants=<d> entrypoints=<e>) gap_links=<g> errors=<x>` (printed by the caller that names the file: try / accept / the CLI). DEPENDENCY: engine gains toml_edit directly (already locked as toml's parser); `display` adds toml_write to Cargo.lock.
INTEGRATOR (0.5.1 merge): the Cargo.toml / Cargo.lock change described in this packet is made by C0.7 (wave 0, all 0.5.1 dependencies in one commit, exact spec as written here); this packet only uses the crate and touches no manifest. `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)] pub struct TryOptions { pub leave_one_out: bool /* default true */, pub surface: &'static str }`. `#[non_exhaustive] #[derive(Serialize, Debug, Clone)] pub struct TryReport { pub stanzas: Vec<StanzaTrial>, pub base: GraphCounts, pub with: GraphCounts, pub verdict: &'static str, pub closed: Vec<String> /* target gap ids present in base, absent with */, pub builds: usize }` and `pub struct StanzaTrial { pub stanza: String /* StanzaRef display */, pub gaps: Vec<String>, pub closes: Vec<String>, pub marginal: GraphDelta, pub verdict: &'static str }`, `pub struct GraphDelta { pub nodes: BTreeMap<&'static str, i64>, pub edges: BTreeMap<&'static str, i64>, pub gaps: BTreeMap<&'static str, i64> }` (zero entries left out).
FLOW: primary = repo_paths[0]; base_text = read `<primary>/.glia/overlay.toml` if present; cand = parse_candidate(candidate_text) (CE.3b; Err -> Err); merged = merge(base_text, &cand, None). Builds (all with BuildOptions::default().with_overlay_text(..)): base (base_text or "version = 1"), with (merged.text), and when leave_one_out, one per stanza: without(merged.text, ref). Single repo: one `ParseCache::load(primary)` threaded through generate_one_with_cache_opts for every build and saved ONCE at the end (LC.11: no write when unchanged) - parse cost paid at most once. Several repos (`--with`): generate_many_opts(repo_paths, true, ..) per build (each repo's sidecar is loaded and saved per build; LC.11 makes the repeated saves no-ops). Each build -> graph_counts(merged) and the gaps_report(merged, &[], ..) row ids of the GRAPH categories (a HashSet of ids, lookup only).
closes(stanza) = its `# gap:` link ids present in base, absent in `with`, and present again in `without(stanza)` (so the closure is this stanza's). marginal = with - without(stanza). stanza verdict = verdict(without, with) (CE.3a's rule), upgraded to `keep` when closes is non-empty and no gap category rose. packets.title: overlay propose and accept: the gap work list with ids and source snippets for the model step, and the only writer of `.glia/overlay.toml` - add chosen candidate stanzas, remove orphaned / redundant rules by gap id, validate, write atomically
packets.area: CE-3 overlay loop - propose and accept
packets.rationale: The loop's two ends. Propose: the model needs, per gap, the code around it; today an agent must run `glia gaps` and then open every file:line itself. Accept: the loop's edit to a checked-in, reviewed input must be exact, format-preserving and refuse to write anything the loader would drop (the loader ignores the whole file on a syntax error or unknown key, code-domain/src/glia_config.rs; docs/overlay.md 'Validation'). The gaps report already names overlay rot to remove: orphaned_rule and redundant_rule rows (engine/src/gaps.rs ~1225-1270) suggest `remove`, and docs/overlay.md step 3 says such rules 'should be removed' - with no command to do it. `./target/debug/glia overlay propose /tmp` at HEAD: `error: unrecognized subcommand 'overlay'` (measured).
entry_points: engine/src/overlay_loop/propose.rs (new) - pub fn propose(repo_paths: &[String], opts: &ProposeOptions) -> Result<Proposal, String>
engine/src/overlay_loop/accept.rs (new) - pub fn accept(repo_path: &str, candidate_text: Option<&str>, opts: &AcceptOptions) -> Result<AcceptSummary, String>
engine/src/overlay_loop/mod.rs - `mod propose; mod accept;` + pub use
packets.implementation:
PROPOSE: `ProposeOptions { categories: Vec<String> /* default: every category whose suggest is not none */, top_k: usize /* 20 per category */, snippet_lines: usize /* 3 */, surface }`. Builds like `glia gaps` (generate_one / generate_many, not persisted), gaps_report with roots, then per row `ProposedGap { gap: GapRow /* id included; CD.3b's `overlay` stanza when present */, snippet: Option<Snippet { file, start_line, lines: Vec<String> }> }`: the snippet is lines [line - k, line + k] (1-based, clamped) read from the row's repo root + file - GapRow carries no repo, so the root is the first of repo_paths (argument order) whose root holds that file; when two roots hold it the snippet is omitted and counted `ambiguous_root` (never a guess) - only for files inside that root, each line capped at 240 chars (char boundary), the whole file skipped when over 2 MiB; a `.glia/overlay.toml` row reads that file. Proposal { rows: Vec<ProposedGap>, counts: BTreeMap<&str, usize>, guide: &'static str } where guide is one paragraph pointing at docs/overlay.md sections per `suggest` value. Snippet text is source code the user owns (same as `read`); no redaction beyond what the repo holds, and nothing is stored.
ACCEPT: `AcceptOptions { only: Vec<String> /* StanzaRef displays; empty = all */, remove: Vec<String> /* gap ids */, dry_run: bool, surface }`. Steps: base_text = the file or none; with a candidate: parse_candidate + merge(base, cand, only) (CE.3b; unknown refs in `only` -> Err listing the valid ones). Removal: build the repo (default overlay), gaps_report with roots, keep rows of orphaned_rule / redundant_rule whose id is in `remove` (an id not found or of another category -> Err naming it), and delete each named stanza from the DocumentMut by its identity (edge from/to/category, wrapper call/kind, route_prefix scope/prefix, constant name, entrypoints pattern, constraint/decision/note id) - never by line. Validate: parse_str(new) must have no error the old text did not have, and section counts must equal old + added - removed; else Err and nothing written. Write: unless dry_run, `<repo>/.glia/overlay.toml.<pid>.tmp` then rename (a *.tmp under .glia is excluded from the input fingerprint, store/src/layout.rs is_store_output_name), creating `.glia/` when absent. AcceptSummary { added: BTreeMap<&str, usize>, removed: usize, duplicates: usize, file: String, dry_run: bool, diff: String /* unified diff of old -> new, for review */ }. PAGE: `pub struct Page { pub kind: DocSourceKind, pub container: String, pub title: String, pub url: String, pub version: String, pub body: PageBody, pub slug_hint: Option<String> }` (slug_hint: a source whose titles can repeat inside one container - the wiki directory, CE.4b - names the manifest stem; every other source passes None and slugs the title), `pub enum PageBody { ConfluenceStorage(String), Markdown(String) }` (CE.4c adds Wikitext). record_from_page: body -> markdown (storage_to_markdown for ConfluenceStorage, as-is for Markdown); prepend `# <title>` UNLESS the first non-blank line is a `#`/`##` heading whose slug equals slug(title); then redact_untrusted(text) -> (text, n) with n added to the caller's redaction count (`record_from_page` returns (DocRecord, usize)); rel_path = `<tag>/<container>/<slug(slug_hint or title)>.md` with tag confluence | notion | wiki (Confluence: byte-identical to today); provenance { kind, url, container, version }.
WRITER: `pub struct SnapshotSource { pub kind: DocSourceKind, pub container: String }`; `pub fn write_snapshot(repo_root, source: &SnapshotSource, records: &[DocRecord], redacted: usize) -> Result<SnapshotWrite, String>` (`redacted` = the sum record_from_page returned, reported in the marker): read the existing manifest (a line that does not parse is dropped and counted `dropped_lines`), keep every record whose (kind, container) differs from `source`, add `records`, sort by (tag, container, rel_path), dedupe on rel_path keeping the new record, write `manifest.jsonl.<pid>.tmp` and rename. `SnapshotWrite { path, written, kept_other, replaced, dropped_lines }`. The Confluence sync's 'refusing to overwrite the snapshot with an empty manifest' guard (cli docs.rs ~99) stays: an empty fetch for one container refuses rather than deleting that container's records.

packets.rationale: GitHub and GitLab wikis are git repositories of Markdown pages that live beside the code repo (`<repo>.wiki.git`), not inside it, so glia's repo walk never sees them (only `.md` under the repo's own tree: engine/src/docs.rs include_doc). A local checkout is the cheapest adapter (no API, no token) and the only one with no network at all. packets.title: Wikitext to Markdown: a dependency-free MediaWiki markup converter that keeps code spans and headings for the doc linker, used for `.mediawiki` / `.wiki` pages in a wiki directory
packets.rationale: MediaWiki stores pages as wikitext (the API's revisions.slots.main.content with formatversion=2), and GitHub wikis also accept `.mediawiki` pages. The plan's lead named html5ever (convert the API's rendered HTML); VERIFIED: html5ever is not in Cargo.lock and brings markup5ever / string_cache / phf / tendril (a lock change and a PARSER_STAMP move, doc-sources being in the workspace), and quick-xml (already used for Confluence storage format) cannot parse non-XHTML HTML5. The linker needs only headings (DOC_SECTION chunking at `#` / `##`, engine/src/docs.rs chunk_markdown) and code spans (backticks and fenced blocks - the Confluence converter's stated purpose, doc-sources/src/confluence.rs module doc), and wikitext carries both literally: `== H ==`, `<code>`, `<tt>`, `<pre>`, `<syntaxhighlight lang=..>` / `<source lang=..>`. Template output ({{...}}) is lost without rendering - the accepted trade-off, reported as a count. The plan's lead (html5ever over the API's rendered HTML) is replaced by converting wikitext directly: no lock change, and the doc linker needs only headings and code spans, which wikitext carries literally.

A line-oriented pass plus an inline pass, char-based (never byte-sliced mid-char; every index comes from char_indices or a find of an ASCII delimiter): - block: `^(={1,6})\s*(.*?)\s*\1\s*$` -> that many `#` + text (level 1-2 become `#`/`##`, which is what chunk_markdown splits on); `` / `` ... closing tag -> ```x fenced block with the body verbatim (entities < > & " decoded); `
` ... `
` -> ``` block; a line starting with one space (wikitext preformatted) -> an indented code line kept as a ``` block run; `*` / `#` / `:` / `;` list prefixes -> `- ` / `1. ` / indentation (depth = prefix length); `{|` ... `|}` tables -> one line per row, cells joined by ` | `, header / style attributes dropped; `----` -> `---`; - inline: `x` / `x` -> `` `x` `` (backticks inside -> double-backtick fence); `'''b'''` -> `**b**`, `''i''` -> `*i*`; `[[Target|label]]` -> `label`, `[[Target]]` -> `Target`, `[[File:..]]` / `[[Category:..]]` dropped; `[https://u label]` -> `[label](https://u)`; bare URLs kept; - dropped: `{{ ... }}` with nesting (a depth counter over `{{` / `}}`, unbalanced -> dropped to end of page and counted), ``, `...` and ``, `__TOC__`-style magic words, `` tags (content kept literally). WikitextStats { headings, code_blocks, inline_code, links, templates_dropped, unbalanced }. Output ends with a newline; no trailing spaces. record_from_page: PageBody::Wikitext(t) -> wikitext_to_markdown(t).0 then CE.4a's title / redaction steps. wikidir: `.mediawiki` and `.wiki` files -> PageBody::Wikitext, summed stats. packets.title: MediaWiki API adapter: `glia docs sync <repo> --source mediawiki --api <.../api.php> --namespace N | --category C` pulls one namespace or category through the Action API (never by following links)
packets.rationale: Many internal wikis are MediaWiki. The Action API enumerates pages without crawling: `action=query&generator=allpages&gapnamespace=N` (or `generator=categorymembers&gcmtitle=Category:X`) with `prop=revisions&rvprop=content|ids|timestamp&rvslots=main` returns each page's wikitext and revision id; with a generator, content is limited to 50 pages per request (mediawiki.org API:Revisions: 'If rvprop=content ... is used, the limit is 50'), and continuation is the response's `continue` object echoed back. Gate check (SECURITY.md, the 0.5.0 Gated list 'HTML sitemap-crawl doc adapter'): this adapter reads exactly the namespace or category the user names through the API and never fetches a page URL or follows a link, the same shape as the Confluence space pull (doc-sources/src/confluence_rest.rs pull_space ~98). Reuses CE.4a's transport (plain http only to loopback) and test server (headers for Retry-After), and CE.4c's converter.

cli/src/cmd/docs.rs DocsCmd::Sync - `--source mediawiki` with `--api`, `--namespace`, `--category`, `--max-pages` (default 5000)
packets.implementation:
REQUEST: GET `<api>?action=query&format=json&formatversion=2&maxlag=5&prop=revisions|info&rvprop=content|ids|timestamp&rvslots=main&inprop=url` + selection: Namespace(n) -> `&generator=allpages&gapnamespace=<n>&gaplimit=50`; Category(c) -> `&generator=categorymembers&gcmtitle=Category:<c>&gcmtype=page&gcmlimit=50` (parameters percent-encoded); continuation: every key of the response's `continue` object is appended to the next request, until the response has no `continue` or max_pages is reached (then PullStats.truncated). Per page in `query.pages` (sorted by title for determinism): skip `missing` / `invalid`; content = revisions[0].slots.main.content (fallback revisions[0].content); contentmodel must be `wikitext` (others counted skipped_model); Page { kind: Wiki, container, title, url: fullurl, version: revisions[0].revid as string, body: PageBody::Wikitext(content) }. container = --container or the API URL's host. Headers: `User-Agent: glia/<RELEASE> (docs sync)` (MediaWiki etiquette requires a UA), `Authorization: Bearer <token>` when a token resolved (an OAuth 2 owner-only consumer token; no cookie login - ureq is built without its cookie feature and adding it would change the lock). ERRORS: a JSON `error` with code `maxlag`, or HTTP 429 / 503 with Retry-After -> sleep min(Retry-After or 5, 30) s, at most 3 retries per request; other `error` -> Err("<code>: <info>"). Origin through transport::checked_origin (https, or http to loopback only).
CLI: `glia docs sync <REPO> --source mediawiki --api <URL> (--namespace <N> | --category <NAME>) [--container <C>] [--max-pages <N>] [--token <T>] [--include/--exclude]` (exactly one of --namespace / --category; clap ArgGroup). packets.title: Notion adapter: `glia docs sync <repo> --source notion --database <id>` pulls a database's pages through the Notion API (Notion-Version 2025-09-03 data sources) and converts their blocks to Markdown
packets.rationale: Notion is the other common team wiki (0.5.0 plan §6 'Later: Notion / wiki adapters'; code-domain already has DocSourceKind::Notion and engine/src/docs.rs source_tag maps it to `notion`). VERIFIED against the Notion developer docs 2026-09-30: since API version 2025-09-03 a database holds data sources - `GET /v1/databases/{database_id}` returns `data_sources: [{id, name}]`, and pages are listed with `POST /v1/data_sources/{data_source_id}/query` (body `start_cursor`, `page_size`; response `results`, `has_more`, `next_cursor`); the latest Notion-Version is 2026-03-11, and versions are pinned by header, so pinning 2025-09-03 keeps the adapter stable. Page content is `GET /v1/blocks/{page_id}/children?page_size=100&start_cursor=` (paginated the same way). Auth is `Authorization: Bearer <integration token>`. `--source notion` at HEAD: `error: unexpected argument '--source' found`.

packets.title: Notion adapter, complete: nested blocks (lists, toggles, callouts, synced blocks, columns), to-dos, tables, bookmarks and child pages, a page-tree mode (`--page <id>`), and 429 Retry-After handling
packets.area: CE-4 doc adapters - Notion blocks and page trees
packets.rationale: Real Notion docs nest: list items, toggles and callouts hold child blocks (`has_children: true`, fetched with another GET /v1/blocks/{id}/children), code often sits inside toggles, and team wikis are page trees (child_page blocks) as often as databases. Without nesting, CE.4e's converter drops everything inside a toggle - including the code spans the linker needs. Notion rate-limits at an average of three requests per second and answers 429 with Retry-After; a page tree of a few hundred pages will hit it. The test server gained response headers in CE.4a, so 429 handling is testable offline.
entry_points: doc-sources/src/notion_md.rs - nested rendering and the remaining block types

doc-sources/src/notion.rs - fn children_tree(cfg, block_id, depth) (recursive fetch for has_children, depth <= 8), pub fn pull_page_tree(cfg, root_page_id, max_pages) (child_page recursion, depth <= 5), 429 / 5xx retry in the request helper
cli/src/cmd/docs.rs - `--page <ID>` as the alternative to `--database` (ArgGroup)
doc-sources/tests/notion_stub.rs (new in CE.4e) - the nesting, page-tree and retry tests
packets.implementation:
FETCH: blocks with has_children (except child_page / child_database, which are pages, not content) get their children fetched recursively (depth <= 8; deeper -> NotionStats.depth_capped) and attached as `children` before conversion. RENDER (depth-aware, two spaces per level): bulleted / numbered items with children indent their children; toggle -> `- <summary>` with indented children; callout -> `> <icon emoji> <text>` with children quoted; quote children quoted; synced_block / column_list / column -> children inline (the synced original's children only; a synced copy whose `synced_from` points elsewhere fetches that block's children); to_do -> `- [ ] ` / `- [x] `; table -> a Markdown table from table_row cells (first row a header when has_column_header, else an empty header row); bookmark / embed / link_preview -> `[<caption or url>](url)`; image / file / pdf / video -> `[<caption or file name>](<external or file url>)` (never downloaded); equation -> `$<expression>$`; child_page -> `- [<title>](notion page)` line (and, in page-tree mode, a page of its own); child_database -> its title; link_to_page -> the linked page id as a link; breadcrumb / table_of_contents -> dropped (counted).
PAGE TREE: pull_page_tree(root): GET /v1/pages/{root} for its title / url / last_edited_time, its blocks, then every child_page block becomes a Page too (breadth-first, sorted by the block order, depth <= 5, at most max_pages); container = the root page id (hyphens removed).
RETRY: HTTP 429 -> sleep min(Retry-After seconds (default 1), 30), HTTP 502 / 503 / 504 -> sleep 1 s; at most 3 retries per request; NotionStats.retries counts them and appears in the marker. CLI: `--page <ID>` or `--database <ID>` (exactly one). Marker unchanged in shape, plus `retries=<t> depth_capped=<c>` and `root=<page id>` instead of `database=` in page-tree mode. Surface regenerated.

packets.title: TypeScript / JavaScript class fields whose value is an arrow function or a function expression are METHOD nodes (qname <Class>::<field>) that carry their body's calls, so `private handleX = (e) => { this.stop() }` and `this.handleX()` join the call graph in Angular, React and Vue classes alike
packets.rationale:
VERIFIER (HEAD 90d1076, after CB.4 84a3581 and CB.12 f683e2b landed): visit_class (parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs:294) still sends `public_field_definition` only to visit_field (:342 -> :569); visit_method (:913) now builds its cells with build_cells_from(&n, first_decorator(n), ..) (CB.4). Re-measured: target/debug/glia (built 01:32 from this tree) `analyze --format json` on the probe fixture lists METHODs ngAfterViewInit / stopAnimation / renderFrame / persist / bump / render / notify and no field METHOD; the leap wheel grades METHOD 0/6, CALLS 0/6, DEFINES 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0 (identical to 2170ff8). The member survey re-run on the git-archive copies gives quokka_web 5 and Kina frontend 11 arrow fields, as below. Graph query: repo-graph find `visit_field` (TS :569, Java / C# visit_field_decl).
parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs visit_class (:294 at 2170ff8) sends a `method_definition` member to visit_method (:913), which mints the METHOD, its DEFINES edge, the `class_methods` entry that `this.m()` binds through, and walks the body with collect_calls_in(body, method_id, Some(class_id)) (:959). A `public_field_definition` member goes to visit_field (:342 -> :569), which only records a class-typed field type (A6.2b) or an `inject(T)` candidate (A7.1) and returns: it mints no node and never walks the value, so an arrow-function field's body calls belong to nobody (not even the class).
MEASURED at HEAD (target/debug/glia, GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 analyze --format json on git-archive copies under the scratchpad probe dir CA-engram): quokka a77d4cb - `...ascii-quokka-hero.component::AsciiQuokkaHeroComponent` has 13 METHOD children and no node for applyAsciiColor (ascii-quokka-hero.component.ts:445) or handleMotionPreferenceChange (:470); the CLASS has only DEFINES out-edges; stopAnimation's callers are ngOnDestroy and setupObservers only (the :474 call is lost), and `this.applyAsciiColor()` in ngAfterViewInit (:92) binds to nothing. STACKED PARSERS: parsers/code/react, angular and vue are thin wrappers over glia_parser_typescript::parse_file (vue passes the <script> block); .js / .jsx route to `typescript` (engine/src/extract.rs detect_language). The framework extractors (extractors/src/react.rs scan_component_names / scan_hook_names, angular.rs, vue.rs) scan top-level declaration lines and mint COMPONENT / HOOK overlays; none reads class members. So one visitor in the TS parser covers Angular components, React class components (probe: a `class Counter extends React.Component { handleClick = () => { this.bump(); } ... render() { return <button .../> } }` in a .jsx parses to CLASS + bump + render METHODs today, handleClick missing) and Vue class components.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN: a function-valued class field IS a method for every consumer (it is called as `this.f()`, passed as a handler, and holds behaviour), so it takes the METHOD kind and the exact treatment visit_method gives a method; no new kind, category or cell. Alternatives weighed: attributing the field body's calls to the CLASS (loses the handler as a unit, and the class would 'call' every handler's callees) or to the constructor (field initialisers run there, but a handler's body runs later, on the event) - both wrong for the Engram / trace question 'what does this handler do'.
1. visit_class: before the member loop, `let method_names: HashSet<&str>` = the `name` text of every `method_definition` child of the body. In the loop, the `public_field_definition` arm becomes `{ visit_field(member, src, module_id, class_id, acc); visit_function_field(member, src, file_rel, &class_qname, class_id, repo, &method_names, acc); }` (visit_field first and unchanged, so A6.2b field types and A7.1 inject() candidates are exactly as today).
2. `fn visit_function_field(field, src, file_rel, class_qname, class_id, repo, method_names, acc)`: value = field.child_by_field_name("value"); return unless value.kind() is `arrow_function`, `function_expression` or `generator_function`. name node = field.child_by_field_name("name"), kind `property_identifier` or `private_property_identifier` (a computed `[k]`, string or number name mints nothing); name = its text (`#tick` keeps its `#`, as visit_method already does for `#m() {}`). If method_names contains name, or acc.class_methods already holds (class_id, name): acc.fn_fields.shadowed += 1 and return (a same-named method keeps its node; TS rejects both, a JS class would let the field shadow the prototype method at runtime, and one NodeId must not be pushed twice). Else: method_qname = format!("{class_qname}::{name}"); method_id = NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, node_kind::METHOD, &method_qname); push Node { cells: build_cells(&field, src, file_rel) } - the FIELD node's span: tree-sitter-typescript puts a field's decorators INSIDE public_field_definition (collect_inject_repository already reads `@InjectRepository(User) repo` off the field node), so CB.4's first_decorator widening, which exists because a method_definition's decorators are class_body siblings, does not apply; DEFINES class -> method with empty cells (as visit_method; fill_evidence_sites stamps it); acc.class_methods.insert((class_id, name), method_id); acc.nav.record(method_id, name, &method_qname, node_kind::METHOD, Some(class_id)); then `if let Some(body) = value.child_by_field_name("body") { collect_calls_in(body, src, method_id, Some(class_id), acc) }` - an expression body (`isBuyer = () => this.trade()?.buyerId === ...`) or a statement_block alike; nested callbacks descend as in any method; parameters are not walked (visit_method walks none either). Counters: arrow / function (function_expression + generator_function), calls = acc.unresolved.len() + acc.endpoints.len() delta across the body walk.
3. Because the field METHOD sits in class_methods before resolve_intra_file runs, `this.applyColor()` from any method of the class (declared before or after the field) resolves in-file as SelfMethod -> an intra_file CALLS edge with the call row (LC.3b), and calls in the field body (`this.stopAnimation()`) resolve the same way from the field METHOD. try_detect_endpoint / try_detect_typeorm_access / record_member_ref inside the body get from = the field METHOD.
4. Marker (per file, only when fields + shadowed > 0), printed in parse_file after the typeorm line: `[ts-fields] function fields=<n> (arrow=<a> function=<f>) calls=<c> shadowed=<s> file=<file_rel>`.
5. Unchanged on purpose: non-function field values (`rafId = 0`, `state = {..}`, `users$ = this.api.list()`, `form = this.fb.group(..)`, `x = computed(() => ..)`) mint no node and their calls stay unattributed (reported as an open question with counts, not taken here); object-literal methods, class_expression bodies and abstract_class_declaration are outside visit_class today and stay so.
6. TESTS (parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs mod tests, `repo()` helper, NodeId::from_parts lookups):

DESIGN: make the CODE cell what the POSITION already says - the whole section - rather than teach the linker to re-read files: `glia merge` drops pass-made edges and re-runs link_doc_sections over loaded layouts (engine/src/merge.rs module doc), and external (Confluence / wiki) sections have no file to re-read, so the text the linker needs must be in the stored graph. After CD.7c (CODE cells as spans) a whole-section CODE cell of a repo file is stored as a span, so the store does not grow for file docs.
1. docs.rs: `const SECTION_TEXT_CAP: usize = 64 * 1024;` and `fn bound_section(s: &str) -> (String, bool)`: trim; if len <= cap return it whole; else cut at the last char boundary <= cap, then at the last `
` before it, and report truncated=true (a data dump, not prose). flush stores bound_section(&buf.join("
")).0 (empty after trim -> no chunk, as today); the fallback stores bound_section(text).0. cap_prose is deleted. A section of <= 500 bytes is byte-identical to today (cap_prose returned it trimmed and whole).
2. build_docs_graph counts sections whose stored text exceeds 500 bytes, the longest length and the truncated ones; marker once per build when the first count > 0: `[docs] section text: <n> sections longer than 500 bytes kept whole (longest=<b> bytes, truncated_at_64k=<t>)`.
3. passes.rs link_doc_sections: unchanged matching (backtick spans only, tiers, linkable kinds, MAX_LINKS_PER_DOC = 25) with ONE guard the wider text needs: a span containing `
` is skipped (`if span.contains('
') { continue; }`) - backtick_spans returns a fenced block's whole body (three backticks leave it at an odd index) or a runaway span as one multi-line segment, never an inline mention; the guard drops no link HEAD makes (0 multi-line spans among quokka / Kina / glia's current links) and the one fence link whole sections would add on quokka. Also add a counter of sections that hit the 25 cap and, when > 0, print `[doclink] <k> sections reached the 25-link cap` after the existing line (the existing `[doclink] N DOCUMENTS edges (...)` line keeps its format).
4. engram-export/src/lib.rs: `fn cap_prose(s: &str) -> String` - the removed engine rule verbatim (500 bytes, char-boundary safe, last `. ` inside the cap) with a doc line saying it keeps Engram's Proposition text what it was before CG.3; pass 2's is_doc branch uses `cap_prose(&code_cell(&n.cells).unwrap_or_else(|| name.clone()))`. Engram therefore gets byte-identical Propositions and only the extra Documents edges.
5. TESTS: docs.rs `a_long_section_keeps_its_whole_text` - chunk_markdown over the fixture's docs/orders.md: the `refunds` chunk text ends with `can still be traced.` and is > 500 bytes, the `placing-orders` chunk equals its old capped text; `bound_section_cuts_only_past_64k` - a 70,000-byte single-section doc stores <= 65,536 bytes ending at a line end and reports truncated; markdown_chunking_and_include_rules keeps its include asserts unchanged. passes.rs passes_tests `doc_mention_skips_fenced_blocks` - a merge built with the existing `Hand` harness (Hand::add with a CODE Text cell) holding one DOC_SECTION whose CODE is ~700 bytes: inline `OrderService.refund` at byte ~640, a fenced block "```python
OrderService.cancel

fixtures.purpose: CA-12 recall: a backticked mention past byte 500 of its section links, and the CODE cell holds the whole section; precision: a symbol named only as a prose word (Shipment) never links
fixtures.source_sketch:
--- app/__init__.py

--- app/orders.py
class OrderService:
    def place(self, order):
        return order

    def refund(self, order):
        return order


class Shipment:
    pass

--- docs/orders.md
# Orders

How orders move through the shop.

## Placing orders

Call `OrderService.place` to place an order.

## Refunds

Refunds are the slowest part of the order lifecycle, and most of the support load comes from them. A customer asks for a refund through the help centre, an agent checks the order history, and the finance team approves anything above the automatic threshold. The threshold is reviewed every quarter and is deliberately conservative, because a refund that is issued twice is very hard to claw back once the card network has settled it. Agents must never issue a refund by hand from the payment provider dashboard, since that bypasses the audit trail the finance team relies on at the end of each month.

Every refund goes through `OrderService.refund`, which records the reason and the approving agent before it calls the payment provider.

A refunded order keeps its Shipment record so that returns can still be traced.

packets.title: TypeScript `abstract class` declarations are CLASS nodes: concrete and abstract members are METHODs (an abstract member has no body: METHOD + DEFINES + POSITION / CODE, no calls), in-class `this.m()` binds to them, a subclass's `extends` binds INHERITS_FROM, constructor DI emits INJECTS, and a decorated abstract class gets its Angular role (the extractor's missing `abstract` skip is fixed)
packets.rationale:
MEASURED at HEAD f8a46c0 (target/debug/glia built 08:26 from b1a4e61; only docs / tests changed since, so it is HEAD's code). parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs visit_top (:289) matches `"class_declaration"` only (:311); tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 (Cargo.lock) parses `abstract class X` as `abstract_class_declaration`, whose fields (name / body / decorator / type_parameters + a class_heritage child, node-types.json) are exactly class_declaration's, and it falls to `_ => {}`. visit_class's member match (:400ff) sends method_definition and public_field_definition only, so a class_body `abstract_method_signature` (fields name / parameters / return_type) is dropped too.
Probe fixture ts-abstract-class (below) graded with the leap wheel at HEAD: nodes 0/7, CALLS 0/3, DEFINES 0/1, INHERITS_FROM 0/1, INJECTS 0/1, ROLE cells 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0; stderr `[heritage] refs bound: ... typescript=0 unresolved: ... typescript=1` (UserRepo extends BaseRepo cannot bind: no BaseRepo node).
A second, hidden gap: parsers/code/extractors/src/angular.rs extract_class_name (:159) strips `export ` and `default ` but NOT `abstract ` (its caller find_next_class_name's doc at :132 claims it does), so `@Injectable()\nexport abstract class FilterDataService` yields no SERVICE overlay at all: the fixture prints `[roles] folded 1 overlays into declarations (... SERVICE=1 ...)` (ProductService only).
REAL REPOS: quokka-stack a77d4cb and Kina a448fb3 declare no abstract class (grep of git-archive copies). /home/ivy/Code/webplatformfrontend (an Angular monorepo, NOT a git repo) declares 8, among them libs/aol/pages/filter-page/src/services/filter-page-data.service.ts `@Injectable() export abstract class FilterPageDataService<TPageData>` whose getPageDataWithFilterableProductListing calls its own `protected abstract getMainFilterData(...)`, implemented by CategoryFilterPageDataService and SearchResultsFilterPageDataService, and src/app/shared/directives/analytics/analytics.directive.ts `@Directive() export abstract class AnalyticsDirective` whose subclasses call `super.onEvent(event)`. A cp -r slice (libs/aol/pages/{filter-page,category-filter-page,search-results-filter-page}, src/app/shared/directives/analytics, libs/shared/features/google-maps, libs/shared/components/search-autocomplete, package.json, tsconfig*.json; 535 nodes) analysed at HEAD: none of the 8 abstract classes is a node, `[heritage] refs bound: ... typescript=11 unresolved: ... typescript=30`, and CategoryFilterPageDataService has no INHERITS_FROM.
STACKED PARSERS: react / angular / vue parse through glia_parser_typescript::parse_file (CG.1's finding), so the one visitor covers every TS-family file. Graph queries run (repo-graph MCP, 0.5.0 build, so it lags the 0.5.1 waves): find `visit_class` (5 parsers; TS at lib.rs:342), find `extract_class_name` (angular.rs:159, marked ⊘), find `extract_call_qualifier` (TS lib.rs:1864); visit_top and class_body handling read directly.

SERVICE=1` and `[heritage] refs bound: manifest=0 typescript=0 unresolved: manifest=0 typescript=1`. tree-sitter-typescript 0.23.2 node-types.json: abstract_class_declaration has fields body / decorator / name / type_parameters + a class_heritage child; class_body children include abstract_method_signature (fields name / parameters / return_type). The react / angular / vue crates all call glia_parser_typescript::parse_file (react/src/lib.rs:13, angular/src/lib.rs:13, vue/src/lib.rs:14), so one visitor covers them. packets.implementation:
DESIGN: in TypeScript every method is virtual and `this.m()` names the receiver's own class chain, so an unbound SelfMethod whose class `extends` another binds to the nearest ancestor defining `m`, the lookup the runtime performs; `super.m()` is the same lookup starting one level up. It runs in the graph crate (parsers extract, the graph resolves), after resolve_refs has bound the heritage edges, and only for the TS family. Alternatives weighed: (a) run it inside build_typescript: that builder also serves Dart / Solidity / Terraform through lang_build's `_` arm, and Solidity's bare internal calls are SelfMethod, so their graphs would change unmeasured; a TS-family entry point keeps the item's scope (the walk is language-free, so another builder adopts it with one call once its own packet measures it). (b) Detect abstract-ness without a fact, from the METHOD's CODE cell text: fragile (decorators and modifiers precede the keyword) and reads a persisted output as a build input; NavFact is the build-time carrier for exactly this. (c) Pair every override with the member it overrides: a concrete override is not an implementation of a declaration (A6.6's IMPLEMENTS means `implements a declared member`), and dispatch to a concrete override is left as it is. 1. code-domain/src/lib.rs NavFact, appended LAST: `/// TypeScript (CH.1b): this METHOD is an `abstract` member declared without a body (recorded by the TS parser's visit_abstract_method); graph emit_abstract_implements pairs a subclass method of the same name with it as a method-level IMPLEMENTS.` `AbstractMethod,`. CH.3b / CH.5a append their variants in whatever order the packets land, each at the end when it lands (the enum doc's rule; the parse cache discards on the PARSER_STAMP move anyway). engine/src/cache.rs every_nav_fact pushes `NavFact::AbstractMethod`. 2. parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs: in CH.1's visit_abstract_method, right after `nav.record(method_id, ..)`: `acc.nav.record_fact(method_id, NavFact::AbstractMethod);` (a repeated signature returns before the record, so one fact per METHOD). extract_call_qualifier, member_expression arm: object kind `"super"` -> `Some(CallQualifier::SuperMethod(name))`, before the `this` arm. `super(...)` (callee kind `super`, not a member) still returns None. resolve_intra_file has no SuperMethod arm, so the site reaches out.calls exactly as the ComplexReceiver did. 3. graph/src/calls.rs: a. `pub(crate) struct InheritStats { self_bound: usize, super_bound: usize, ambiguous: usize, implements: usize }` with `pub(crate) fn report(&self)` printing `[ts-inherit] calls bound through superclasses: (self= super=

ambiguous=) abstract implements=` when any count is > 0. b. `fn superclasses(g: &RepoGraph) -> BTreeMap>`: every INHERITS_FROM edge whose two ends have nav kind CLASS, keyed by from.0, each list sorted by .0 and deduped (no HashMap order reaches an edge). c. `pub(crate) fn resolve_inherited_calls(g: &mut RepoGraph, stats: &mut InheritStats)`: `let pending = std::mem::take(&mut g.unresolved_calls);` for each site IN ORDER: qualifier SelfMethod(name) or SuperMethod(name), else push back; owner = enclosing_class_or_struct(&g.nav, site.from) with nav kind CLASS, else push back. Level walk from superclasses[owner] (both qualifiers start one level up: the own class already failed for SelfMethod and `super` skips it by definition), a visited set, at most 16 levels: at each level collect the DISTINCT targets `g.symbols.class_methods[base][name]` over the level's bases; exactly one -> bind; two or more -> stats.ambiguous += 1, push back; none -> next level = the union of the level's superclasses not yet visited, sorted. Bind = `push_edge(g, site.from, to, edge_category::CALLS, graph_evidence("graph:calls", "inherited_method").line(site.line))` (the call's own row, LC.3b) and count self / super. Unbound sites go back to g.unresolved_calls in their original order. symbols.class_methods holds METHOD children only (build_symbol_table), so a CH.2 STATE_VAR is never an inherited target. d. `pub(crate) fn emit_abstract_implements(g: &mut RepoGraph, stats: &mut InheritStats)`: for each (sub, bases) of superclasses(g) in key order: the sub's methods class_methods[sub] collected and sorted by name; for each (name, sub_mid): walk the ancestors level by level (visited, 16 levels) to the FIRST level where any base's class_methods has `name`; exactly one such method that carries NavFact::AbstractMethod in g.nav.nav_facts -> pair (sub_mid, abstract_mid); a concrete definer at that level stops the walk (it is what the sub overrides); two definers -> no pair. Pairs sorted by (from.0, to.0), deduped, existing IMPLEMENTS (from, to) dropped, then `push_edge_with(g, from, to, edge_category::IMPLEMENTS, graph_evidence("graph:iface", "abstract_override"), Confidence::Strong)` (an explicit `extends` plus the same name; A6.6's direction impl -> declared). A grandchild implementing a grandparent's abstract member pairs too when no class between defines the name. 4. graph/src/build.rs: build_typescript's body moves into `fn build_ts_like(repo, parses, resolve_source, inherit: bool)`; build_typescript calls it with false (unchanged output); new `pub fn build_typescript_family(repo, parses, resolve_source)` calls it with true, which runs, after `resolve_refs(&mut g, &all_refs, &mut tally);`: `let mut inh = InheritStats::default(); resolve_inherited_calls(&mut g, &mut inh); emit_abstract_implements(&mut g, &mut inh); inh.report();`, then the existing emit_method_level_implements / tally.report(). The build module is glob re-exported, so the fn is `glia_graph::build_typescript_family` without a facade edit (CLAUDE.md facade rule 1). Its doc names the reason for two entry points (the `_`-arm languages). method_level_implements_is_idempotent_and_runs_in_every_builder also builds through build_typescript_family. 5. engine/src/build/lang_build.rs build_language_graphs: the TS_GROUP arm calls `glia_graph::build_typescript_family(repo, parses, |from, spec| resolve_ts_source_aliased(from, spec, ts_aliases))`; the `_` arm keeps `glia_graph::build_typescript(repo, parses, resolve_relative_source)`. 6. TESTS. graph/src/calls.rs mod tests (hand-built FileParses with heritage_ref, through build_typescript_family; NavFact::AbstractMethod recorded on the abstract METHOD's nav): (a) self_call_binds_through_superclasses - A { load } <- B { find: this.load() } <- C { go: this.load(); this.find() }: CALLS B::find -> A::load, C::go -> A::load, C::go -> B::find, each with evidence emitter graph:calls, rule inherited_method and the site line; C { go: this.describe() } with A::describe and B::describe binds B::describe (nearest), never A::describe. (b) super_call_skips_own_override - A { d } <- B { d: super.d() }: CALLS B::d -> A::d, none B::d -> B::d. (c) abstract_override_implements - A { abstract f (fact), concrete d, abstract g (fact) } <- B { f, d } <- C { f }; D extends A with f only; E extends B with g: IMPLEMENTS B::f -> A::f, D::f -> A::f, E::g -> A::g (grandchild, B defines no g), each rule abstract_override and Strong; none B::d -> A::d (concrete), none from C::f (its first definer is B, concrete). (d) inherit_walk_is_deterministic_and_ts_family_only - the same parses reversed give an identical sorted edge list; `this.nope()` and a site whose class's INHERITS_FROM never bound stay in unresolved_calls in their original order; build_typescript over the same parses leaves every inherited site unresolved and pairs nothing (the `_`-arm builder). parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs mod tests: (e) abstract_member_carries_the_fact - CH.1's BaseRepo source: nav.nav_facts[fetchOne] == [NavFact::AbstractMethod], load has no entry. (f) super_call_is_super_method - `class B { m() {} }\nclass C extends B {\n m() { super.m(); this.n(); }\n n() {}\n}`: a CallSite SuperMethod("m") from C::m at line 2, no ComplexReceiver{receiver:"super"}, the intra_file CALLS C::m -> C::n unchanged. 7. Fixture bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/ts-inherited-calls (below): an abstract BaseRepo, a two-level hierarchy across files, a `super.describe()`, a nearest-definer `this.describe()` and an @OnEvent listener as the entry, so liveness carries find -> load -> fetchOne (abstract) -> the implementer UserRepo::fetchOne.

packets.risks: Precision: the nearest-ancestor rule is the runtime's own binding, so depth is no risk; two distinct definers at one level (a mixin `extends Mix(A, B)` heritage ref that bound twice) stay unresolved and are counted ambiguous. A base reached only through a heritage ref resolve_refs could not bind leaves the call unresolved (no guess); a global_unique heritage bind (a repo-unique class name, e.g. through a barrel import) is followed like any other INHERITS_FROM. A `this.m()` inside a nested `function () {}` in a method still climbs to the enclosing class (enclosing_class_or_struct's existing behaviour). Receiver-typed calls of an inherited method (`this.repo.inheritedM()`) and dispatch to CONCRETE overrides stay as they are. Cycles (`A extends B`, `B extends A` across a bad merge) are cut by the visited set and the 16-level cap. Determinism: BTreeMap / sorted vectors only; unresolved_calls keep their order, so byte_identical holds at any GLIA_THREADS. Liveness and gaps move (more reached methods), which is the point; no cli / py pin reads a TS inherited call (grep). The Dart / Solidity / Terraform graphs keep build_typescript and are untouched. NavFact::AbstractMethod, CH.3b's and CH.5a's variants each go last when they land: whichever lands later appends after the earlier ones (no tag is renumbered). UTF-8: no new text slicing. Per-file panic isolation unchanged (no new unwrap in the parser).

packets.title: `glia gaps` dead_symbol counts a METHOD that IMPLEMENTS a called METHOD as called (the dead-row half of A7.8's implementer step): an override of a called abstract member, or an implementation of a called interface method, is no longer reported dead when nothing reaches the caller from an entrypoint
packets.area: CH-1 TS abstract classes (3/3: dead_symbol through dispatch)
packets.rationale:
DECISION (James 2026-10-01): CH.1b's acceptance must show subclass implementations of abstract members no longer read as dead_symbol. Liveness already carries them when the abstract member is reached (engine/src/answers.rs live_walk, A7.8 implementer step: an IMPLEMENTS edge reversed, method level included). But `glia gaps` dead_symbol (engine/src/gaps.rs:1024) is `outside entrypoint_reachable AND no incoming carry edge (View::build carry_in, :680) AND not ORIGIN test_fixture`, and its row text is `no entrypoint reaches it; no incoming call or use`. A declared member that is called but whose caller is not reached drops out (it has the incoming CALLS) while every implementation of it stays a row, although dispatch from that call is exactly what reaches the implementation. The template-method shape the decision names is this case on the webplatformfrontend slice: FilterPageDataService::getMainFilterData (abstract) is called by getPageDataWithFilterableProductListing, whose only caller FilterPageEffects is itself a dead_symbol CLASS at HEAD (NgRx effects are no entry kind), so after CH.1 + CH.1b the two getMainFilterData implementations stay rows.
MEASURED at HEAD f8a46c0 (debug CLI; for each repo `glia gaps <copy> --json --category dead_symbol --top-k 1000000` against the same copy's `glia analyze --format json` edges, counting METHOD rows that are the `from` of a METHOD -> METHOD IMPLEMENTS whose `to` has an incoming CALLS or USES; script spec051b/probe/CH/b2/sim_impl2.py): quokka-stack a77d4cb 0 of 851 rows; Kina a448fb3 0 of 562; grpc-go 6f50403 84 of 2686 (e.g. grpclog componentData::Fatal -> internal::loggerv2::LoggerV2::Fatal, pemfile pluginBuilder::Name -> certprovider Builder::Name); lapse 35 of 327 (every internal::registers::*::Slug -> internal::pipeline::interface::RegisterPipeline::Slug); wpf slice 0 of 142 (no abstract pairs before CH.1b). A Java probe (interface Store { save }, PgStore implements Store, Svc.run calls store.save, no entry) lists 5 rows at HEAD, PgStore::save among them, with `CALLS Svc::run -> Store::save` and `IMPLEMENTS PgStore::save -> Store::save` present. The TS fixture without its listener (no entry) lists 6 rows at HEAD, UserRepo::fetchOne among them. Every one of those rows is an implementation of a method the build sees called. No cli / py / engine dead_symbol pin has an interface or abstract member in its sources (grep `interface|implements|abstract` over cli/tests/gaps_cli.rs, cli/tests/overlay_loop_cli.rs, engine/tests/gaps_report.rs, engine/tests/overlay_loop.rs, engine/tests/overlay_wrappers.rs, py/tests/surface/test_gaps.py: 0 each; the go-overlay-data-wrapper fixture declares no interface), and neither the repo-graph wrapper nor neuropil reads dead_symbol (grep). Graph queries run (repo-graph MCP): find `entrypoint_reachable` (answers.rs:130), find `NavFact`; gaps.rs View::build / the dead_symbol arm read directly.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN: mirror A7.8's implementer step on the dead row's second half, not in liveness: liveness feeds blast / trace / effects / pack rankings and already carries reached members to their implementations, while the gaps row's own claim is `no incoming call or use`. Alternatives weighed: (a) widen liveness to count `called` members as live: changes every liveness consumer and reaches code from callers nothing reaches; (b) restrict the rule to CH.1b's abstract_override edges: fits the motivating case only; the measured interface cases (lapse 35, grpc-go 84, the Java probe) are the same claim made false the same way; (c) count any carry edge into the declared member as a call: a member that is only DOCUMENTED or TESTED vouches for no dispatch, so only CALLS / USES count, the row text's own `call or use`.
1. View gains `dispatch_in: HashSet<NodeId>`. In View::build's node loop, `methods: HashSet<NodeId>` collects every METHOD id; in the edge loop, `called: HashSet<NodeId>` collects the `to` of every CALLS / USES edge with from != to. After the edge loop, one more pass over merged.all_edges(): an IMPLEMENTS edge whose from and to are both in `methods` and whose `to` is in `called` inserts `from` into dispatch_in. One hop: A6.6, CA.3b and CH.1b pair an implementation with the member it implements directly. Sets only, never iterated into output, so rows keep view.nodes order.
2. gaps_report's FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS arm: the row is pushed when `!live.contains(id) && !view.carry_in.contains(id) && !provenance_is(.., "test_fixture")` AND `!view.dispatch_in.contains(id)`; when only dispatch_in withholds it, `withheld += 1`. After the node loop, when DEAD_SYMBOL is wanted and withheld > 0: `eprintln!("[dead-dispatch] dead_symbol rows withheld: {withheld} (implementations of a called method)")`. Counts (`rep.count`) are the rows reported, as today.
3. Module doc table, dead_symbol row: `a FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS outside entrypoint_reachable, with no incoming carry edge, not a METHOD that IMPLEMENTS a METHOD with an incoming CALLS / USES (dispatch reaches it, CH.1c), not ORIGIN test_fixture`.
4. TESTS engine/tests/dead_dispatch.rs (generate_one over tempfile repos, gaps_report with GapsOptions::default(), rows filtered to DEAD_SYMBOL, matched by qname suffix): (a) java_implementation_of_a_called_interface_method_is_not_dead - the Java probe (src/main/java/shop/Store.java `public interface Store { void save(String id); }`, PgStore.java `public class PgStore implements Store { public void save(String id) { System.out.println(id); } }`, Svc.java with a `private final Store store` field, a constructor and `public void run(String id) { store.save(id); }`): no PgStore::save row; Svc::run, Svc and PgStore are rows (controls: nothing calls them); PgStore::save is NOT in entrypoint_reachable (liveness untouched). Fails at HEAD. (b) uncalled_declaration_vouches_for_nothing - the same with Svc::run's body emptied: PgStore::save IS a row. (c) ts_override_of_a_called_abstract_member_is_not_dead - CH.1b's ts-inherited-calls sources without src/users.listener.ts (no entry): no UserRepo::fetchOne row (BaseRepo::fetchOne is called by BaseRepo::load), AdminRepo::findAdmin and AdminRepo::audit are rows. Fails before CH.1b + this packet. (d) ts_reached_override_is_live - the full fixture with the listener: UserRepo::fetchOne in entrypoint_reachable, dead_symbol rows exactly {AdminRepo, AdminRepo::findAdmin, AdminRepo::audit, UsersListener::constructor} by qname suffix. (e) withheld_rows_are_deterministic - two gaps_report runs over (a)'s graph give equal row ids and counts.

(3) `cargo test -p glia-cli --test gaps_cli --test overlay_loop_cli`, `cargo test -p glia-engine --test gaps_report --test overlay_loop --test overlay_wrappers`, `cargo test -p glia-cli`, `cargo test -p glia-py` and, after the wheel rebuild, `~/.venvs/glia-leap/bin/python -m pytest py/tests/surface/test_gaps.py` green with no pin moved; `--test byte_identical` green (no graph change).

packets.risks: Recall of the dead list, not precision of the graph: an implementation of a called interface method that is in fact never instantiated (a stale implementation nobody wires) is no longer reported, which is the same call A7.8 makes for a reached member; Go's implicit pairs are Medium (method-set inferred), so a type that satisfies an interface by accident and is never used through it drops out too (lapse / grpc-go rows checked by hand in the commit body). packets.title: TypeScript class fields initialised by a call (Angular signal / computed / input / model / toSignal / effect, `x$ = this.subject.asObservable()`, any call but `inject(...)`) are STATE_VAR nodes `<Class>::<field>` whose initializer, arrow bodies included, is walked for calls, so a computed's dependencies, a toSignal's service call and an HttpClient call in a field all join the graph, and `this.<signal>()` reads bind to the STATE_VAR
packets.area: CH-2 call-initialised class fields as STATE_VAR
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/typescript/src/lib.rs visit_class sends a `public_field_definition` to visit_field (:639: field types A6.2b, `inject()` candidates A7.1) and visit_function_field (:726, CG.1: arrow / function values only); nothing walks any other initializer, so every call inside `x = computed(() => ...)`, `x = toSignal(this.api.list())`, `x = effect(() => ...)` or `users$ = this.subject.asObservable()` belongs to nobody, not even the class. CG.1's own doc names the gap ("`users$ = this.api.list()`, `x = computed(() => …)` ... mint no node and their calls stay unattributed").
SURVEY (regex over class bodies of the git-archive copies, *.spec.ts excluded, fields at member indentation): Kina frontend a448fb3 has 1,983 initialised class fields: computed 487, signal 432, inject 359, input 223, other calls 165 (input.required / model.required / Array.from ...), output 64, toSignal 30, model 23, `this.x.y()` 19, viewChild 6, contentChild 2, linkedSignal 2, plus 85 literals, 6 `new`; quokka_web a77d4cb has 396: 333 literals, 25 `new`, 13 `x$ = this.xSubject.asObservable()`, 9 other calls, 2 signal, 2 computed. So ≈1,450 Kina and ≈26 quokka fields are call-initialised and not inject(). Examples: Kina pages/trade-view/trade-view.component.ts:472 `myActiveProposal = computed(() => this.activeProposal(this.currentUserId()))` (activeProposal a METHOD, currentUserId a CG.1 arrow METHOD) and :433 `trade = signal<Trade | null>(null)` read by CG.1's `isBuyer = () => this.trade()?.buyerId === ...` (today an unresolved SelfMethod `trade`); features/kyc/pages/beneficial-owners.page.ts:72 `countries = toSignal(this.kyc.countries(), ...)`.
Probe fixture ts-signal-state-fields graded at HEAD f8a46c0 (leap wheel): STATE_VAR 0/7, ENDPOINT 0/1 (the `toSignal(this.http.get('/api/profile'))` call is extracted nowhere), CALLS 0/7, DEFINES 0/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0. Precedent for the shape: Dart's emit_top_level_var (parsers/code/dart/src/lib.rs, CB.17) mints a STATE_VAR and walks its initializer for calls and client ENDPOINTs from it; Java / C# mint class-level STATE_VARs under the CLASS (G19). `glia gaps` dead_symbol counts FUNCTION / METHOD / CLASS only (engine/src/gaps.rs:22), so the new STATE_VARs add no dead rows. Graph queries run (repo-graph MCP): find `visit_function_field` (lib.rs:726), `emit_top_level_var` (dart lib.rs:1274), `annotated_class_type` (lib.rs:477); visit_class / visit_field read directly.
VERIFIER (HEAD f8a46c0): re-graded the probe fixture: STATE_VAR 0/7, ENDPOINT 0/1, CALLS 0/7, DEFINES 0/1, FORBID 0. Survey re-run over the Kina git-archive copy (frontend/src, *.spec.ts excluded, 2-space member indentation): 1,780 + 19 (`this.x.y()`) call-initialised fields, 357 of them inject(): ~1,442 STATE_VARs, matching the draft's ~1,450; Kina HEAD graph 4,243 nodes / 9,747 edges. A second side effect the draft missed: STATE_VAR is doc-linkable (engine/src/passes.rs is_doc_linkable_symbol, :722) and the doc linker indexes every linkable node by bare name, keeping the lowest NodeId on a collision and dropping the tier to ambiguous; the new STATE_VAR names (label, title, rows, loading ...) can therefore add DOCUMENTS edges or retarget / downgrade an existing bare-name link. Kina has 10 DOC_SECTION nodes, quokka 274 (359 DOCUMENTS edges); quokka's backticked call-field names are all `x$` observables, which the linker's identifier rule (`is_identifier`: alnum / `_` only) never resolves.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN: a field holding the result of a call is state the class owns (an Angular signal is a getter function; an Observable field is a stream), and its initializer runs code. It takes the existing STATE_VAR kind (Java / C# class constants, Dart top-level vars, TS exported consts already use it) parented by the CLASS; no new kind, category or cell. Alternatives weighed: attributing the initializer's calls to the CLASS or the constructor (initializers run there, but a computed body runs on every read: wrong owner for `what does this derived value depend on`); a METHOD (a signal is called like one, but CG.1 reserves METHOD for function-valued fields and `glia gaps` would list ≈1,450 Kina fields as dead_symbol); a narrower set (only fields with an arrow argument) - loses `this.rows()` read targets of inputs and signals, see open question in the group summary.
1. visit_class, public_field_definition arm: after `visit_field(..)` and `visit_function_field(..)` call `visit_state_field(member, src, file_rel, &class_qname, class_id, repo, acc)`.
2. `fn visit_state_field(field, src, file_rel, class_qname, class_id, repo, acc)`: value = field.child_by_field_name("value"); peel `parenthesized_expression`, `as_expression`, `satisfies_expression`, `non_null_expression` to the inner expression for the KIND TEST only; return unless that is a `call_expression`. Exclusion: the call's `function` is an identifier that is `inject` or a local binding of an `inject` import already collected (`inject_import_bindings(&acc.imports)`, A7.1's own rule: `import { inject as di }` makes `di(Foo)` DI too; import statements precede the class in every surveyed file) - A7.1's DI shape keeps its INJECTS ref and field type, and is not state. Name node kind property_identifier / private_property_identifier only (`#x` keeps its `#`). If acc.class_methods holds (class_id, name) -> return (a method or function field of that name keeps its node; TS rejects the clash). qname `{class_qname}::{name}`; id = NodeId::from_parts(GRAPH_TYPE, repo, STATE_VAR, &qname); Node { cells: build_cells(&field, src, file_rel) } (field span: decorators are inside public_field_definition, CG.1's finding; DOC from its JSDoc); DEFINES class -> state (empty cells, parser-stamped); acc.class_methods.insert((class_id, name), id) so `this.<name>()` (a signal / computed / input read) resolves in resolve_intra_file as SelfMethod -> an intra_file CALLS with the call row; acc.nav.record(id, name, &qname, STATE_VAR, Some(class_id)); then `collect_calls_in(value, src, id, Some(class_id), acc)` over the WHOLE initializer (the outer factory call becomes an ordinary unresolved CallSite like any library call; collect_calls_in descends into arrow / function_expression arguments, so computed / effect bodies are walked; try_detect_endpoint / try_detect_typeorm_access / record_member_ref inside get from = the STATE_VAR). Stats: fields += 1; signal += 1 when the callee's leaf name (identifier, or member object identifier for `input.required` / `model.required` / `viewChild.required`) is in SIGNAL_FACTORIES = [signal, computed, linkedSignal, toSignal, effect, input, model, output, outputFromObservable, viewChild, viewChildren, contentChild, contentChildren, resource, rxResource, httpResource]; calls += the acc.unresolved.len() + acc.endpoints.len() delta.
3. Graph side needs nothing: a CallSite from the STATE_VAR resolves like a method's (enclosing_class_or_struct walks STATE_VAR -> CLASS, so A6.2a receiver typing binds `this.countriesApi.list()` through the inject() field's type across files). graph symbols.class_methods stays METHOD-only (build_symbol_table), so a cross-file `this.store.draft()` read of another class's signal stays unresolved (see gaps).
4. Marker, after `[ts-fields]`, when fields > 0: `[ts-state] call fields=<n> (signal=<s> other=<o>) calls=<c> file=<file_rel>`.
5. CG.1 test non_function_fields_mint_nothing: keep the METHOD loop; replace the `no CallSite ... list` assertion with: the `list` CallSite exists and its `from` is NodeId(STATE_VAR, "src::k::K::users$"); add that `rafId` / `label` / `state` / `api` have no STATE_VAR; inject_targets unchanged.
6. TESTS (mod tests): (a) signal_and_computed_fields_are_state_vars - `readonly rows = input.required<string[]>(); readonly page = signal(1); readonly total = computed(() => this.rows().length * this.page());` -> three STATE_VARs, DEFINES from the class, POSITION start_line = each field's row. (b) computed_body_calls_and_signal_reads_bind - total CALLS rows and page (intra_file, Evidence line = the computed's row); `isLong = computed(() => this.longest(this.rows()) > 10)` CALLS longest (METHOD) and rows; `next(): void { this.page.set(this.page() + 1); }` CALLS page. (c) inject_new_and_literal_fields_mint_nothing - `http = inject(HttpClient)`, `store = di(Store)` under `import { inject as di } from '@angular/core'`, `subject = new BehaviorSubject(0)`, `rafId = 0`, `state = { n: 0 }`: no STATE_VAR; both INJECTS refs still emitted. (d) field_http_call_is_the_state_vars - `readonly profile = toSignal(this.http.get<string>('/api/profile'));` with `private readonly http = inject(HttpClient)`: ENDPOINT endpoint:GET:/api/profile whose CALLS in-edge comes from ...::profile. (e) observable_data_field - `readonly count$ = this.subject.asObservable();` STATE_VAR with CallSite ComplexReceiver{this.subject, asObservable} from it.
