packets.implementation:
DESIGN: read what the source states about the URL at the call site and in the caller's own scope chain or class: a builder's literal argument, the builder call a same-class zero-argument URL method returns verbatim, the value of a `const` declared in an enclosing scope before the use, and the initializer of a `readonly` field (or a one-`return` getter) of the caller's own class. Each is the AST's own text at one declaration; no parameter, assignment, `let` / `var`, or return value of an arbitrary call is followed (no value data-flow). Alternatives weighed for the field read: reading every field initializer (a non-readonly field can be reassigned anywhere in the class: precision loss), or scanning the class for `this.<f> =` assignments (more code for a case neither measured repo has): `readonly` or a getter is the cheap sound rule.
1. `fn classify_path_arg(arg, src) -> PathArg { classify_at(arg, src, true) }`; `fn classify_at(arg: TsNode, src: &[u8], indirect_ok: bool) -> PathArg` keeps today's string / template_string / fallback arms and adds, in order:
   a. `call_expression`: `single_literal_arg(arg)` (the `arguments` node's named non-comment children are exactly one `string` or `template_string`) -> classify that literal with today's string / template rules, then confidence = Weak (the builder may transform it: today's tier for a wrapper) and wrapper = Some(leaf name of the callee: an identifier's text or a member_expression's `property`). A template whose static text (the path with every `${…}` removed) holds no `/` is not a URL (`this.i18n.t(`errors.${code}`)`): <unresolved>, wrapper None. A plain string keeps today's reading (find_first_string_literal already took it) and gains only the wrapper field.
   b. else, `call_expression`, when indirect_ok and the call is `this.<m>()` with no arguments: same_class_method_return(arg, m) -> classify_at(expr, src, false).
   c. else `call_expression`: today's find_first_string_literal fallback, unchanged (wrapper None).
   d. `identifier`, when indirect_ok: local_const_value(arg) -> classify_at(value, src, false); None -> today's <unresolved>.
   e. `member_expression` whose object is `this`, when indirect_ok: class_member_value(arg) -> classify_at(value, src, false); None -> today's <unresolved>.
   f. The `/` rule for indirect results: a method-arm (b) result read through arm a (a builder call: wrapper Some) keeps arm a's reading, so `this.healthUrl()` returning `this.urls.buildApiRootUrl('healthz')` reads like the direct call (`/healthz`): the class wrote that method to return a URL. Every other indirect result, including a local / field (d, e) whose value is a single-literal call, is <unresolved> when its static text (the path with every `${…}` removed) holds no `/`: `const id = this.route.snapshot.paramMap.get('id')` read through arm a gives `id` and stays <unresolved> (a local's value can be any one-literal call), `const key = 'draft'` is a bare value, and a URL held whole in a substitution, `const u = `${x}``, would normalise to `/{}`, which BaseFold folds onto `/`. Confidence of d / e is the value's own (a const literal is as good as the literal: Strong for a string, Medium for a template, Weak through a builder). Depth is one: classify_at(.., false) never follows a second indirection.
2. `fn same_class_method_return(call, m) -> Option<TsNode>`: nearest ancestor `class_body`; a `method_definition` named m with no get / set token, `parameters` with no named children, and a body of exactly one named non-comment statement, a `return_statement` with an expression -> that expression (so `this.sessionUrl()` -> `this.apiUrlBuilder.buildApiUrl('protected/user/profile')`). Anything else -> None.
3. `fn local_const_value(ident) -> Option<TsNode>`: name = ident text; walk the ancestors of ident. At a `statement_block` or `program`: among its named children that END before ident starts (a declaration after the use is in the TDZ), find the LAST binding of name: a `lexical_declaration` / `variable_declaration` declarator (an `export_statement` wrapping one counts at program level) whose `name` binds it, or a function / class / abstract class declaration of that name. The last binding is a `lexical_declaration` whose `kind` is `const`, with an `identifier` name and a `value` -> Some(value); any other binding (let, var, a destructuring pattern, a function or class) -> None; no binding -> continue upward. At a function-like ancestor (arrow_function, function_expression, function_declaration, generator_function, generator_function_declaration, method_definition) whose `parameters` (or an arrow's single `parameter`) bind name -> None (a parameter shadows every outer const: `fetch(path)` stays unresolved). At a `for_in_statement` whose `left`, a `for_statement` whose `initializer`, or a `catch_clause` whose `parameter` binds name -> None. `fn binds_name(pattern, name) -> bool`: the pattern is an identifier equal to name, or any `identifier` / `shorthand_property_identifier_pattern` descendant of it is (a defaulted parameter `path = '/def'` binds `path`).
4. `fn class_member_value(member) -> Option<TsNode>`: property p = the member's `property` (property_identifier or private_property_identifier text); walk ancestors to the nearest `class_body`, returning None at a function_expression / function_declaration / generator_function first (`this` is not the instance there; an arrow keeps it). In that class_body: a `public_field_definition` named p with a `readonly` token and a `value` -> that value; else a `method_definition` with a `get` token named p whose body is one `return_statement` with an expression -> that expression; else None (a non-readonly field, a constructor parameter property without initializer, an inherited member).
5. PathArg { path, template, confidence, wrapper }; push_endpoint copies wrapper into EndpointCandidate; endpoint_hit_cell's Payload gains `#[serde(skip_serializing_if = "Option::is_none")] wrapper: Option<&'a str>` AFTER `template`, so every payload without a wrapper is byte-identical (A3.3's raw / A11.2's template rule). A local / field read carries the read value's own `template` (the const's or field's source text, `${environment.apiUrl}/notifications`), so the engine's endpoint fold (BaseFold) and CG.4a's literal-host rule see exactly what a direct use would give them; the ENDPOINT_HIT `line` / `col` stay the call's.
6. Acc.endpoint_args: EndpointArgStats { wrapper, local, field, method, unresolved }: each HTTP call-site argument counts once, under the outermost arm that read it (method b, local d, field e, else wrapper when arm a set a wrapper) or under unresolved when its final path is <unresolved>; marker per file when wrapper + local + field + method > 0: `[ts-endpoint-args] wrapper=<w> local=<l> field=<f> method=<m> unresolved=<u> file=<file_rel>`.

(c) zero_arg_url_method_is_read - `checkSession() { return this.http.get(this.sessionUrl()); } private sessionUrl(): string { return this.urls.buildApiUrl('protected/user/profile'); }` -> endpoint:GET:/protected/user/profile with wrapper "buildApiUrl"; a sessionUrl with two statements, with a parameter, or that is a getter stays <unresolved>. (d) local_const_and_shadowing - `async reverse(lat: number) { const url = `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=${lat}`; return fetch(url); }` -> endpoint:GET:/reverse, payload raw holding the host and template `https://nominatim.openstreetmap.org/reverse?lat=${lat}`; stay <unresolved>: `download(url: string) { return this.http.get(url); }`, `let u = '/a'; this.http.get(u)`, a `const url` declared AFTER the call, an outer `const url = '/a'` shadowed by an inner `(url) => this.http.get(url)` parameter or a `for (const url of urls)` loop, `const id = this.route.snapshot.paramMap.get('id')` (no `/`), and a module-level `export const API_URL = '/api/x'` read inside a function is endpoint:GET:/api/x. (e) readonly_field_and_getter - `private readonly notificationsUrl = '/api/notifications';` + `this.http.get(this.notificationsUrl)` -> GET /api/notifications Strong; `get usersUrl() { return '/api/users'; }` + `this.http.get(this.usersUrl)` -> GET /api/users; `private draftUrl = '/api/drafts'` (not readonly) and `this.http.get(this.draftUrl)` stays <unresolved>; `this.base` read inside a `function () {}` callback stays <unresolved>. 1. Acc gains `this_refs: Vec<(NodeId, NodeId, String, u32)>` (from, enclosing class, name, 0-based row) and `this_ref_seen: HashSet<(NodeId, String)>` (first site per (from, name) wins: its row is the evidence line).

packets.title: Endpoint fold: a TypeScript call site whose URL was read through a builder (`wrapper`, `wrapper_of`) that carries a UrlPrefixKey fact is re-keyed under the key's one configured path value (`/protected/friends` -> `/api/protected/friends`, ENDPOINT_HIT `prefix` / `prefix_from`), so quokka_web's buildApiUrl calls pair EXACT with the `/api` gin routes while buildApiRootUrl's `/healthz` / `/metrics` stay as they are
packets.area: CH-5 client API prefix (3/4: endpoint fold, TypeScript builders)
packets.rationale:
MEASURED on the quokka-stack git-archive copy (a77d4cb, debug CLI at HEAD): `[http] routes=65 endpoints=48 paired=48 (exact=2 any=0 eprefix=0 rprefix=46 base=0 suffix=0)`, `[evidence-rules] resolver=http exact=2 ... route_prefix=46`; the two exact pairs are GET /healthz and GET /metrics (built by buildApiRootUrl), every other pairing is `/protected/...` or `/auth/...` against `/api/...` routes through the resolver's route-side strip (MatchTier::RoutePrefix, ceiling Medium, graph/src/resolvers/http.rs:392), and one web endpoint (`GET /user/2fa`) pairs two routes at that tier (/api/protected/user/2fa and /api/user/2fa). engine/src/endpoint_fold.rs folds `${base}` templates through the const table (A11.2) but reads nothing for a builder: plan_entry (:247) sees `raw` `protected/friends`, url_split returns no path for it (no leading `/`) and the entry is left alone. With CH.3a (path read through the builder, `wrapper`) and CH.3b (UrlPrefixKey on buildApiUrl, `wrapper_of` = ApiUrlBuilderService) the fold has what it needs; the prefix VALUE is configuration: quokka_web/src/environments/environment{,.development,.local}.ts all bind `apiPrefix: '/api'` (const-table keys environment.apiPrefix and bare apiPrefix), and api-url-builder.service.ts's DEFAULT_CONFIG agrees.
NOT THIS PACKET'S EFFECT, contrary to the item text: `glia spec-status` exact / prefix rows. spec-status's `pairing` is the contract-link pass's rule on the op -> ROUTE DOCUMENTS edge (engine/src/spec_status.rs:21); quokka's 37 `prefix` rows are openapi ops (turps/docs/swagger.yaml declares no basePath, so its `/protected/...` paths meet `/api/...` routes) and no client ENDPOINT takes part. The measurable effect is the `[http]` tier counters and the HTTP_CALLS EVIDENCE rules. Graph queries run (repo-graph MCP): find `plan_entry` (endpoint_fold.rs:247); impact `fold_repo` backward depth 2 -> its in-file test callers fold_one (:1278) and marking_is_order_independent_and_idempotent (:1466), which this packet updates; the production caller (engine/src/build/grafts.rs:89; fold_repo is CG.4a code, newer than the MCP's 0.5.0 build) found by grep.
VERIFIER (HEAD f8a46c0): the debug CLI on the quokka git-archive copy prints `[http] routes=65 endpoints=48 paired=48 (exact=2 any=0 eprefix=0 rprefix=46 base=0 suffix=0)` and `[evidence-rules] resolver=http exact=2 ... route_prefix=46`; probe fixture ts-api-prefix-builder re-graded: nodes 1/3, HTTP_CALLS 1/3, ENDPOINT_HIT 0/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1. spec-status (engine/src/spec_status.rs:17-22) pairs a declared op to a ROUTE through the contract-link DOCUMENTS edge; quokka's HEAD spec-status rows read exact/implemented 44, prefix/implemented 37, undeclared 24, declared_missing 2, none of them through a client ENDPOINT, so the item's 'spec-status exact rows rise' is not this packet's effect (recorded in unresolved).

packets.implementation:
1. `pub(crate) struct PrefixContext { builders: BTreeMap<(Option<String>, String, String), Option<(String, String)>>, owners: OwnerIndex }` keyed (owner, class simple name or "" for a module function, method name) -> Some((prefix path, key)) or None when ambiguous. `PrefixContext::build(parses: &[&mut FileParse], consts: &ConstTable, roots: &[ProjectRoot]) -> Self`: owners = http_owner::OwnerIndex::from_roots(roots); for each parse, owner = owners.owner_of(&http_owner::module_file(fp)?); for each (scope, facts) of fp.nav.nav_facts collected into a Vec sorted by scope.0 (no HashMap order), each NavFact::UrlPrefixKey{key}: method = nav.name_by_id[scope]; parent = nav.parent_of[scope]; class = nav.name_by_id[parent] when its kind is CLASS, "" when MODULE (a module function builder); resolve key -> value set: `consts.candidates(key)` plus every `consts.entries()` value whose key ends with `.` + key; map each value to a path (`v` when it starts with `/`, else `url_split(v).1`), cut the query, trim trailing `/`; prefix = the ONE distinct non-empty, non-`/`, `${`-free path, else None (no fold). quokka: candidates("apiPrefix") = ['/api'] and environment.apiPrefix / DEFAULT_CONFIG.apiPrefix = '/api' -> Some("/api"). Insert; a second fact for the same key tuple with a different result -> None.
2. fold_repo(parses, consts, repo, roots): collect parses into the Vec (already done), `let ctx = PrefixContext::build(&parses, consts, roots);` then fold each with `fold_endpoint_paths_with(fp, consts, repo, &ctx)`; mark_external unchanged after. fold_endpoint_paths(fp, consts, repo) = fold_endpoint_paths_with(fp, consts, repo, &PrefixContext::default()) (every existing unit test keeps its call and its expectation).
3. plan_entry(node, nav, consts, repo, ctx): `let path = url_split(input).1;` becomes `let path = url_split(input).1.or_else(|| qpath.starts_with('/').then(|| qpath.to_string()))` (an entry with no readable path keeps its own; nothing about an unplanned entry changes). Then the prefix step: `if let Some(w) = fields.str("wrapper") && host.is_none() && fields.str("host").is_none()` -> look up (owner of fields.str("file"), fields.str("wrapper_of").unwrap_or(""), w) in ctx.builders; when the owner-scoped key misses, try the same (class, method) under any owner if exactly one owner has it. Hit Some((p, key)) and the path is not already under p (`path == p` or `path.starts_with(&format!("{p}/"))`): path = format!("{p}{path}"), fields.set("prefix", p), fields.set("prefix_from", key), confidence = Some(Medium) unless an overlay pin already made it Weak (the builder's transform is now known: Weak -> Medium; one inference step, never Strong). Then the existing `moved` / host / payload / id logic runs unchanged (`folded_from` = the old qname path).
4. FoldStats gains `prefixed_wrapper` (entries moved by the prefix step); report(): when > 0 print `[endpoint-prefix] prefixed <n> endpoint paths (wrapper=<w> base=<b>) prefixes=<p1,..> repo=<label>` (base is CH.5c's, 0 here; prefixes sorted distinct). `[endpoint-fold] folded` keeps counting every moved entry.
5. grafts.rs:89: `endpoint_fold::fold_repo(parses_by_lang.values_mut().flatten(), const_table, repo, roots)`; the two in-file test callers of fold_repo (fold_one, marking_is_order_independent_and_idempotent) pass `&[]` and keep their expectations.

(d) already_prefixed_path_is_untouched - path /api/protected/x stays. (e) other_class_same_method_name_does_not_match - wrapper_of OtherBuilder. packets.title: Endpoint fold: when every resolvable Dio base URL a Dart project declares (ClientBase facts, resolved through a literal, a ValueLiteral getter / constant or an exact const-table key) has the same non-root path, that project's root-relative, host-less Dart client ENDPOINTs are re-keyed under it (quokka_android `/protected/...` -> `/api/protected/...`) and pair EXACT
packets.area: CH-5 client API prefix (4/4: endpoint fold, Dart project base path)
packets.rationale: quokka_android's Dio clients are all built with `BaseOptions(baseUrl: Env.apiBaseUrl)` (api_client.dart:21 and :35; auth_interceptor.dart:57 copies `retry.baseUrl`), and Env.apiBaseUrl returns '$scheme://$host/api' (env.dart:17-21), so every root-relative `dio.<verb>('/protected/...')` is served at `/api/protected/...`. On the git-archive copy at HEAD all 18 plain android call sites pair route_prefix (e.g. `POST:/protected/friends/accept/${…} @quokka_android -> POST /api/protected/friends/accept/:publicId @turps`), and CH.5a adds the 25 generic ones, unprefixed too. CH.5a records the base expressions (NavFact::ClientBase) and the getter's literal (NavFact::ValueLiteral); this packet resolves them per project and applies the path in the same fold CH.5b extended. A Dio call site does not name its client (quokka's clients come from a Riverpod provider), so the rule is per project root (OwnerIndex, the http_owner / CB.24 ClientHost scoping): a project whose bases agree is served under that path. Probe fixture dart-dio-base-path at HEAD (leap wheel): nodes 0/2, CALLS 0/1, HTTP_CALLS 0/2, cells 0/2, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1. RESOLUTION ORDER matters: the const table is repo-wide and language-blind, and quokka_web's environment.ts binds a bare `apiBaseUrl` = 'http://localhost:8080' (scan_object binds every member's bare key too), so a lenient `resolve_expr("Env.apiBaseUrl")` would answer the Dart expression with the Angular app's root URL. Graph queries run (repo-graph MCP): find `OwnerIndex` (engine/src/http_owner.rs:88; the extractors' anchor.rs has an unrelated one), find `resolve_expr_strict` (constants.rs:138); `stamp_client_hosts` (CB.24, grafts.rs:261) is not in the MCP's 0.5.0 graph and was read directly.

1. PrefixContext::build also gathers, per Dart parse (module file ends with `.dart`), owner = owners.owner_of(file) (None for a single-root repo), every NavFact::ClientBase{via:"dio", expr, ..} on its MODULE, and into one `values: BTreeMap<String, Option<String>>` every NavFact::ValueLiteral{name, value} of any Dart parse (a name bound to two different values -> None).
2. `fn resolve_client_base(expr, values, consts) -> Base` where `enum Base { Path(String), Root, Copy, Unresolved }`: (a) a quoted string literal (`'...'` / `"..."`): strip quotes, `$x` / `${x}` -> `${…}`; (b) `values.get(expr)` exact, else the last two dotted segments (`core.Env.apiBaseUrl` -> `Env.apiBaseUrl`); (c) `consts.resolve_expr_strict(expr)` (exact normalised key, never ambiguous; NOT resolve_expr's last-segment fallback, see rationale); (d) expr ends with `.baseUrl` -> Copy (a base copied from an existing request / client); (e) else Unresolved. A value maps to its path: `url_split(v).1` when it holds `://` (`${…}://${…}/api` -> `/api`, the documented `${…}://api/users` behaviour), `v` when it starts with `/`; trailing `/` trimmed, query cut; `/` or empty -> Root.
3. Per owner: any Unresolved -> None (blocked: an unknown client might use another base; print `[endpoint-base] project <owner> not prefixed: unresolved base <expr> repo=<label>` once); else the distinct Path values: exactly one P (Root / Copy ignored) -> Some((P, expr of its first fact in file order)); zero or two+ -> None.

packets.title: Go calls made in a package-level var's initialiser are CALLS of that var's STATE_VAR: calls inside a func literal it holds (`var f = func() {..}`, a grouped `var ( .. )` block, a literal nested in a composite initialiser) and calls made directly in the initialiser (`var svc = New()`, `var logger = grpclog.Component("x")`, a multi-name spec paired by position); no FUNCTION is minted for a literal
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs emit_state_var_spec (:774) pushes one STATE_VAR per name and walks the paired initialiser only with collect_provider_sets_in (A7.6 wire sets); collect_calls_in (:1418) and CA.1's collect_closure_calls (:1482) run only from visit_function (:886) / visit_method (:942). A literal in a package var's initialiser is therefore never walked; CA.1's own spec names it ('Unchanged: package-level var f = func() {..} (not a function body; no calls collected today)').
MEASURED at HEAD f8a46c0 (target/debug/glia built at HEAD; GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 analyze --format json on git-archive copies under the spec scratchpad probe/CI/):
- fixture go-package-var-closures (below), graded with the leap venv wheel: CALLS 1/7 (only the control `Run -> newStore`), HANDLED_BY 1/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0.
- grpc-go 6f50403: `balancer::rls::control_channel::newAdaptiveThrottler` (STATE_VAR; control_channel.go:38 `var newAdaptiveThrottler = func() adaptiveThrottler { return adaptive.New() }`) has 0 outgoing edges, and neither has `xds::googledirectpath::utils::getZone` (utils.go:64, its body a `zoneOnce.Do(func() { getFromMetadata(..) })`). Callers already reach such vars: grpc-go holds 126 CALLS into STATE_VAR nodes (77 from METHOD, 49 from FUNCTION) and none out of one, so every caller -> var -> callee path stops at the var.
- A heuristic source scan (top-level `var` declarations whose initialiser holds a func literal; probe/CI/tools/pkgvar_lits.py) finds 28 declarations / 38 literal bodies / ~61 call sites in grpc-go (20 declarations in non-test files), 1 in quokka-stack a77d4cb (turps/Tasks/seed_litmus_users.go:162, nested in a composite), 0 in Kina a448fb3 and lapse c0ece02. lapse's one ROUTE HANDLED_BY a STATE_VAR (`POST /billing/webhook -> internal::billing::exports::WebhookHandler`, `var WebhookHandler gin.HandlerFunc = handleWebhook`) holds a function value, not a literal: unchanged.
OWNER: the var's STATE_VAR. It exists for every spec that holds a literal (state_var_is_noise skips only a lone literal primitive), callers already bind CALLS to it, and A7.6 already uses it as a ref `from`. The MODULE would pool every var's callees on one node and cut the caller -> var -> callee path; a FUNCTION would invent a declaration Go does not have.
Direct initialiser calls (`var svc = New()`) were an open question in the first spec; James took them into this packet on 2026-10-01 (below).

packets.risks: Over-approximation: a literal held by a var and never called (a test double kept around) still attributes its calls to the var, the same rule CA.1 applies to a literal never invoked; a direct initialiser call runs at package init, so it is a real call, but its caller is the package's init, which a STATE_VAR stands in for (a var nobody reads still keeps its callee off dead_symbol: grpc-go's `var _ = ..` registrations are the intended case). Pairing: by position (`var a, b = f1, func(){..}` -> b); a single multi-value initialiser (`var a, b = two()`) pairs with the first name only. Double counting: emit_state_var_spec must call collect_calls_at INSTEAD of collect_provider_sets_in (deleted), or every wire.NewSet / fx.Provide INJECTS ref is pushed twice; wire_newset_var_emits_injects_from_state_var's exact vec catches it. The walk must start at the value node, not the var_spec (record_body_locals' var_spec arm). Volume: grpc-go's 80 `var logger = grpclog.Component(..)` STATE_VARs each gain one CALLS into grpclog::component::Component (a hub in blast radius; its fan-in rises from ~0 package-init callers to 80, the true runtime shape). File contention: CA-era functions in parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs (collect_calls_in, collect_closure_calls, the marker block) are also edited by CI.2a, CI.3 and CI.5 (struct fields, record_import, route scope) - the scheduler serialises same-file packets. Determinism: calls and literals in tree order, literals drained FIFO; no map iteration added. UTF-8: no byte slicing. Per-file panic isolation unchanged (all inside parse_file). PARSER_STAMP moves (parsers/ is hashed): every parse cache is invalidated once. Verifier additions (HEAD f8a46c0): no route walk runs in a package-var initialiser, so a func literal registered as a handler INSIDE a package-var literal (`var setup = func(r *gin.Engine) { r.GET("/x", func(c *gin.Context) { f() }) }`) is drained like any closure and `f` becomes a CALLS of `setup` (no ROUTE is minted there today either). A ginkgo-style `var _ = Describe("..", func() {..})` in a _test.go file attributes the whole suite's calls (Describe itself included) to the file's `_` STATE_VAR (test-side, per-file qname). graph/src/build.rs go_types_marker counts every non-MODULE local_types scope, so `[go-types] local_scopes=` / `locals=` grow on repos with package-var literal parameters or locals (grpc-go); no test pins it on a real repo (graph/src/build.rs go_types_marker_counts is hand-built) and its doc ('fn / METHOD scopes') is left as is: this packet does not touch graph/src/build.rs.

packets.title: Go imports of the repository-root package are recorded (bound under the import path's package name, or the alias), so IMPORTS, calls, typed receivers and embeds through it resolve; CA.3b's root-package reachability assumption is removed, and its test-side rule is narrowed to the test file's DIRECT imports so the newly recorded root hub cannot widen test-side pairs
packets.rationale:
parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs record_import (:1294) maps an import through GoModules::map_import (:1211) and, for `Some(q) if q.is_empty()` (the import path IS the root go.mod's module path), returns without pushing an ImportStmt ('no package dir to name'). The repository-root package is a directory like any other (its dir is "": go_package_dir, graph/src/build.rs:879), so every importer loses its IMPORTS edge, its import binding, every `pkg.X()` call (GoPackages::package_call needs import_path, :1094), every typed receiver through the root (CA.2b chain_type root_hop), every embed of a root interface (resolve_go_embeds import_paths) and CA.3b's reachability through it; CA.3b papered over the last with GoReach::RootAssumed (:1242), counted in `root_assumed`.
MEASURED at HEAD f8a46c0 (debug CLI, GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1, git-archive copies under probe/CI/):
- grpc-go 6f50403 (root go.mod `module google.golang.org/grpc`, 37 root .go files, `package grpc`): `[iface] go implicit implements: 682 (interfaces=231 types=556 embedded=13 open=10)`, `[iface] go implicit filtered: signature=570 scope=62 (one_method=1 test_side=61) signature_checked=682 root_assumed=10`, `[go-package] dirs=304 multi_file=144 dir_bound_imports=3328 sibling_calls=4998`. 250 non-root files import `google.golang.org/grpc` (non-blank) and spell 1,659 `grpc.X(` selector calls (WithTransportCredentials 306, WithResolvers 185, NewClient 166, NewServer 113, Dial 105 ...); the HEAD graph holds only 8 IMPORTS edges into root-dir MODULEs and 73 CALLS from other dirs into root-dir nodes. 3 interfaces embed a root interface (reflection/serverreflection.go GRPCServer embeds grpc.ServiceRegistrar; reflection/test/grpc_testing_not_regenerate/testv3.go two stream interfaces embed grpc.ClientStream / grpc.ServerStream) and are among the 10 `open` ones.
- Replay of CA.3b's gate (probe/CI/tools/rootsim.py: the dir import graph rebuilt from source with and without root imports, applied to the HEAD graph's gated IMPLEMENTS pairs): the 10 root_assumed pairs (e.g. server::Server -> reflection::serverreflection::ServiceInfoProvider, xds::server::GRPCServer -> server::ServiceRegistrar) are all Reached once root imports exist; no kept pair becomes Unreached. So the assumption CAN go: it only ever stood in for imports the parser dropped. Kept as is, it would still pass every genuinely unreached root-side pair (the fixture's isolated::iso::file -> options::Closer), so CA.3b's 'turns off by itself' holds only for reached pairs: this packet removes it.
- quokka-stack a77d4cb (turps/go.mod `module turps`, its root package is `main`), Kina a448fb3 (backend/go.mod, no root .go file), lapse c0ece02 (no root .go file): none imports its module's own path; their graphs must not move.
- fixture go-root-package-imports (below) graded at HEAD: IMPORTS 0/2, CALLS 0/4, IMPLEMENTS 1/1, FORBID VIOLATIONS 1.
Graph queries run: repo-graph find `record_import` (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs:1294), find `emit_go_implicit_implements` (graph/src/build.rs:2037), find `DirImportGraph` (graph/src/build.rs:1219, its methods scope :1289 / reaches :1271 / start :1278 / closure_of :1256, and GoPackages::dir_import_graph :1183); the MCP lags HEAD, anchors re-read at HEAD.
DECISION 2026-10-01 (James): instead of accepting the wider test-side reach, narrow CA.3b's test-side rule in this packet. THE RULE AT HEAD (graph/src/build.rs DirImportGraph::scope, :1289, with start :1278 and reaches / closure_of): when the type or the interface is declared in a `_test.go` file, that side's start set is its OWN file's imports (of_file), and the pair is kept when the other side's package dir is in the TRANSITIVE import closure of that start set (closure_of follows whole packages' imports, of_dir); two test sides in different dirs never meet; the shared-importer rule applies only with no test side. Test sides no longer walk a closure (the narrowed rule), so the hub cannot widen a test-file pair; neither-test one-method pairs still reach through it transitively, and by the replay the 15 name-covering candidates that opens all fail the signature compare (a future root-package type whose one method matches a far interface by name AND signature would pair: the one-method rule's documented behaviour). CI.5 also edits record_import (its import_dirs insertion sits before the root-path return), so either order composes. packets.risks: False binds: every lookup stays exact-name and unique-or-nothing; a promoted method binds only when the type itself declares no member of that name and exactly one embed supplies it at the shallowest depth (Go's selector rule), so it cannot shadow a declared method; the generic passes run first, so no edge that resolves today changes target. An embed resolved by name only in its own dir: a same-named type in an external `x_test` package of that dir makes it ambiguous (unbound), as for interface embeds. Pointer vs value embedding is not distinguished (method sets merged, as CA.3b merges receivers). Cost: GoPromoted is one bounded BFS per embedding struct (depth <= 8); grpc-go has about 390 embedding structs. Sequencing: depends on CI.3 (a root-package type is embedded through a root import: 22 grpc-go embeds); CI.2b and CI.4 build on GoPromoted; parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs and graph/src/build.rs are shared with CI.1 / CI.3 / CI.5 and CI.2b / CI.4 (the scheduler serialises same-file packets). Determinism: BTree collections, embeds deduped and id-sorted, refs in parse order; byte_identical at any GLIA_THREADS. UTF-8: node text only. PARSER_STAMP moves (parsers, graph). Verifier: `own` (the names that block promotion) is class_methods + field_types keys, and field_types records only fields go_type_name can name, so a slice / map / func-typed field named like a promoted method does not block it (Go would): a rare false promotion, bounded by exact-name, unique-or-nothing lookup. graph/src/build.rs is also claimed by CH.1b (TS inherited calls); the scheduler never puts two claimants of one file in a wave.

packets.risks: Owner by import: a dot-import (`. "x/api"`) makes `Server` unqualified, so its owner is still this package's dir (Go would read the imported one) - rare, unchanged from HEAD. Two imports of one package under two names both map to its dir (fine); an import whose package clause differs from every import_local_names candidate is not mapped, and its owner falls to None -> the unprefixed root, as an outside package. A struct of another package assigned in-file and registered in-file keeps CB.11's in-file Const prefix (correct: one assignment, read in the same body). Parameter-rooted fields: every route on such a field becomes a Param provisional; CB.20 must resolve the caller's CALLS edge to mount it (an unresolved call -> unmounted -> HEAD's qname, never worse). A parameter-rooted field the file also assigns from a literal root disagrees and falls to CB.23's Field mount (both FieldMount facts are recorded today). Sequencing: parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs is shared with CI.1 / CI.2a / CI.3 and engine/src/coverage.rs with CI.3 / CI.2b and CJ.2 (other group); the scheduler never puts two claimants of one file in a wave, and none of these edits overlaps CI.5's functions (record_import is edited by CI.3 too: CI.5 inserts before the root-path return, so either order composes). Determinism: BTreeMap import map, GroupPath order unchanged, Mount equality only; byte_identical must stay green. PARSER_STAMP moves (parsers): provisional qnames live in the parse cache.

packets.title: Go type aliases (`type X = Y`, same-package and cross-package, including protoc-gen-go-grpc's stream aliases to grpc's generic streams) are resolved in CA.3a's method signatures before CA.3b compares them, so a streaming gRPC service IMPLEMENTS its XServer interface
packets.area: CI-6 Go type aliases in method signatures
packets.rationale:
CA.3a records a Go METHOD's signature as text with package qualifiers and parameter names dropped (parsers/code/go/src/lib.rs go_signature :1750 over type_shape :1807, stored in CodeNav.method_sigs); CA.3b's R1 in emit_go_implicit_implements (graph/src/build.rs :2037) rejects a pair whose two texts differ. A type alias is never read: collect_types (:401) skips every type_declaration child that is not a `type_spec` (`if spec.kind() != "type_spec" { continue; }` :413), and tree-sitter-go 0.25.0 (Cargo.lock) parses `type X = Y` as a sibling `type_alias` node (node-types.json: type_declaration children type_alias | type_spec; type_alias fields name / type / type_parameters). So an implementation written with the generated alias and an interface written with the aliased type compare unequal: the CA.3b coverage caveat says so ('a type alias [is] not resolved', engine/src/coverage.rs :170, asserted at :656).
protoc-gen-go-grpc >= 1.4 writes every streaming RPC of an XServer interface with grpc's generic stream type and emits a back-compat alias that user code names: quokka-stack a77d4cb turps/chatpb/quokka_chat_grpc.pb.go:63 `QuokkaChatStream(grpc.BidiStreamingServer[ChatStreamMessage, QuokkaChatStreamResponse]) error`, :103 `type QuokkaChatService_QuokkaChatStreamServer = grpc.BidiStreamingServer[ChatStreamMessage, QuokkaChatStreamResponse]`, and turps/Services/chat/server.go:150 `func (s *Server) QuokkaChatStream(stream pb.QuokkaChatService_QuokkaChatStreamServer) error`. CA.3a texts: interface `(BidiStreamingServer[ChatStreamMessage,QuokkaChatStreamResponse])(error)`, implementation `(QuokkaChatService_QuokkaChatStreamServer)(error)`; the alias target's type_shape is `BidiStreamingServer[ChatStreamMessage,QuokkaChatStreamResponse]`, the interface text exactly, so rewriting the alias name by its target makes the pair compare equal. grpc.BidiStreamingServer itself is out of the repo (quokka) or the root package (grpc-go): it is never resolved, both sides just spell it the same once the in-repo alias is replaced. CI.2b measures the same blocker: after promotion quokka's Server still fails QuokkaChatServiceServer on this signature (its `filtered: signature=3`).
MEASURED at HEAD f8a46c0 (debug CLI built from b1a4e61; only docs / tests changed since) plus a go/ast replay of CA.3a's type_shape and of this packet's rewrite (probe/CI/b2-alias/aliasscan/main.go; it reproduces `[go-sigs] with_signature` exactly on all four repos: grpc-go 6718, quokka-stack 195, Kina 685, lapse 207):

Of the 66, 41 override no XServer method with an alias-typed parameter (CI.2b alone pairs them) and 25 do (9 in _test.go files): every one of the 25 compares equal after the rewrite. Own-method name-covering pairs (no promotion): 10 turn from signature-rejected to equal (HealthServer, LoadBalancerServer and the reflection v1 / v1alpha ServerReflectionServer / ServerReflectionClient pairs, generated without mustEmbed), 0 the other way, 742 unchanged. The rewrite changes 64 METHOD signatures, 0 of them interface elements; tokens with two candidate aliases: 3, all expanding to one shape (reflection/internal names v1's and v1alpha's ServerReflection_ServerReflectionInfoServer); 0 ambiguous, 0 shadowed. `[iface] go implicit implements: 682 ...`, `filtered: signature=570 ...` at HEAD.

packets.implementation:
DESIGN. The parser cannot expand an alias itself: the generated alias lives in another package's file, and a Go parse is per file. So the parser records each alias as a build-time fact and the graph rewrites signatures once every file is merged, before CA.3b compares them. Alternatives weighed: (a) mint a node per alias with an edge to its target: needs a node kind or an edge category id and adds graph content (Engram Symbols, neuropil nodes) for what is a build-time comparison - rejected; (b) record, beside each signature, the (package, name) of every type it names, so `pb.X` resolves through the file's import of `pb` exactly: precise when one file names two same-named types of two packages, at the cost of a second per-method map in CodeNav and the parse cache (about +60 LOC); the scoped bare-name rule below measured 0 ambiguous and 0 shadowed tokens on grpc-go, quokka-stack, Kina and lapse once same-shape candidates count as one, so it is not taken now; (c) a new CodeNav field for the alias table: NavFact (CB.6) is the build-time per-scope carrier already serialised by the parse cache and merged by merge_nav, and every reader matches it non-exhaustively, so one appended variant needs no new field, no CanonicalNav change and no FORMAT_VERSION change (nav facts never reach the store). 1. FACT (code-domain/src/lib.rs). `NavFact::TypeAlias { name: String, shape: String }`, appended after the last variant present when this lands (CH packets may append theirs first; the order does not matter, the parse cache is keyed by PARSER_STAMP): 'Go (CI.6): this MODULE declares the type alias `type = `; `shape` is the target's CA.3a type shape (package qualifiers dropped). Read by the Go build to resolve aliases in method signatures.' 2. PARSER (collect_types). `for spec in type_decl.named_children(..)`: `match spec.kind() { "type_spec" => { today's body } "type_alias" => record_type_alias(spec, src, module_id, acc), _ => {} }`. record_type_alias: name = child_by_field_name("name") text (skip empty); skip when child_by_field_name("type_parameters") is present (a Go 1.24 generic alias: its parameters would leak into the text; a use stays unresolved as today); target = child_by_field_name("type"), skip when absent or has_error(); shape = type_shape(target, src); skip when shape == name (an identity re-export such as `type Status = status.Status`: rewriting it changes nothing and would only add lookups); else `acc.nav.record_fact(module_id, NavFact::TypeAlias { name, shape })`. Grouped `type ( A = B; C struct{} )` declarations reach both arms. Top-level declarations only, as collect_types is today (a function-local alias is not visited). No node, no edge: graph content changes only through the comparison. 3. SCOPE (GoPackages::alias_scope). `pub(crate) struct AliasScope<'p> { dir: &'p str, imported: BTreeSet<&'p str>, test: bool }` for a file MODULE: dir_of[file], every `imported_dir(g, file, local)` over import_path[file] (CI.3 records the repository-root package, dir ""), tests.contains(file). A METHOD's file is file_of(g, m) (split-file methods through method_file, interface elements through the nav parent chain). 4. TABLE. From g.nav.nav_facts over MODULE ids, collected and sorted: `aliases: BTreeMap<(String /*dir*/, String /*name*/), Vec>`, defs sorted by module id; names: BTreeSet of every alias name (a cheap pre-check per token). `own_types: BTreeSet<(String, String)>` = (package dir, name) of every STRUCT / INTERFACE node (dir through file_of + dir_of), for the shadowing rule. 5. EXPAND. `fn expand(text, scope, depth, visiting, memo, stats) -> String`, a single left-to-right pass over `text` with char_indices (UTF-8 safe). An identifier token is a maximal run of `c == '_' || c.is_alphanumeric()`; a token starting with a digit (an array length) is copied. `func`, `map`, `chan` are copied; `struct` / `interface` immediately followed by `{` are copied through the matching `}` (brace depth), so field and method names inside an inline type are never read as types. Any other token in `names`: candidates = the AliasDefs of (d, token) for d in {scope.dir} plus scope.imported, a def from a _test.go file only when scope.test and d == scope.dir (an in-package test alias is invisible to the package's other files). Rules: no candidate -> copy; the token is also an own_types entry of scope.dir while every candidate comes from another dir -> copy, stats.shadowed += 1 (bare `X` is the package's own type; the qualifier that said `pb.X` was dropped); otherwise each candidate's expanded shape = memo[(dir, name)] or `expand(def.shape, alias_scope(def.module), depth + 1, ..)` with (dir, name) in `visiting` while it runs (a token whose alias is in `visiting`, or depth > 8, is copied: `type A = B; type B = A`, which Go rejects but a broken file can parse, ends); all candidates equal -> write that text (two packages generating one alias, grpc-go's reflection v1 / v1alpha, are one answer); different -> copy, stats.ambiguous += 1. The inserted text is already expanded in the alias's own scope and is not rescanned. Pointer / slice / map / chan / func wrappers need nothing: the alias name is replaced inside them (`*pb.X` -> `*`, `[]X` -> `[]`), and type_shape already writes a single func result bare on both sides. 6. REWRITE (resolve_go_alias_sigs). None when the table is empty. For each METHOD id of g.nav.method_sigs, in NodeId order (keys collected and sorted; each rewrite depends only on its own text and scope, so order cannot change a result): skip unless some token of the text is in `names`; scope = alias_scope(file_of(m)) else skip; new = expand(..); when new != old, replace it and count sigs_rewritten (and `interface` when the nav parent is an INTERFACE). Every reader that runs after sees resolved text: CA.3b's R1, CI.2b's promoted method-set entries, the evidence rule (`method_signature` when all compared), CA.3a's `[go-sigs]` count (unchanged: entries are replaced, never added). method_sigs is build-time only, so nothing persisted changes but the edges the comparison admits. 7. GoPackages owns its data (it borrows nothing from g), so the &mut is free. 8. packets.risks: Precision of the bare-name scope: signatures dropped their qualifiers, so a file that names an imported alias `pb.X` and another package's type `other.X` rewrites both; the scope (own package + the file's in-repo imports), the shadowing rule and the equal-shape rule keep that to 0 measured tokens on four repos, and a wrong rewrite can only reject or admit a pair whose names already all match. Qualifier-precise resolution is the recorded alternative (b). An alias declared outside the repo (a dependency's alias) and a generic alias stay unresolved, as today. Determinism: facts are per-MODULE Vecs in source order, the table and own_types are BTree, memoised shapes are BTree, method_sigs keys are sorted before the rewrite and each rewrite depends only on its own text and scope, so byte_identical holds at any GLIA_THREADS; no HashMap order reaches an edge (emit_go_implicit_implements already sorts pairs). UTF-8: tokens are cut on char boundaries (char_indices, char::is_alphanumeric), never by byte offset. Termination: the `visiting` set and the depth cap of 8 end alias cycles, and inline struct / interface bodies are skipped by brace depth. PARSER_STAMP moves (parsers/ and code-domain/ are hashed), so parse caches are invalidated once; the NavFact variant is appended last so older bincode tags hold (CH packets appending NavFact variants touch the same enum and every_nav_fact: append after whatever is there). Per-file panic isolation: the parser arm adds no unwrap. Order: the rewrite must run after GoPackages::build and before emit_go_implicit_implements (CI.2b's method sets read method_sigs); CA.2a's receiver typing does not read aliases (a call on an alias-typed value still types through the alias name: out of scope). Liveness and dead_symbol counts move on Go gRPC repos; any cli / py pin on a Go IMPLEMENTS count must be re-verified (none known: grep).

Names such as `queue_consumer:QueueFramework::BullMQ, &[`, `queue_producer:.expect(`, `queue_consumer:...` and `queue_consumer:/` (the last two are the `⟁ ... [queue_consumer] ·89 reached ⧉ cross-service` and `⟁ / [queue_consumer] ·64 reached` entries repo-graph `orient` lists for glia) come straight out of needle-table string literals, `///` doc comments and `#[cfg(test)]` source literals. 136 of the 296 QUEUE_FLOWS and 12 of the 31 EVENT_FLOWS edges touch one of them, so glia's own cross-service flows are mostly phantom. Every one of the 176 sites sits inside a Rust or Python string literal or comment: a Python port of `cli::CodeMap` (LA.20a's lexer) over the copy, checking each recorded CODE/POSITION site line for a queue / event needle at a code byte, keeps none of them and drops none of the 13 fixture-sited QUEUE/EVENT nodes in .rs / .py fixture files. The 177th, queue_producer:sidekiq_, is a code-position hit: the Sidekiq Receiver row's bare needle `perform_async` matches inside the test fn name `sidekiq_perform_async_uses_class` (queues.rs) and `receiver_before` reads `sidekiq_`.
WHY NOT A PATH SKIP-LIST (the item's wording): the phantoms come from 26 files across extractors, parsers, graph, engine/cli/py tests and scripts, not only the scanners' own sources; skipping those paths would also drop their real code, and it would help no other repo that embeds sample source in strings (linters, codegen, test suites). The CLI extractor already states the rule this packet generalises: `CodeMap` (parsers/code/extractors/src/cli.rs:413) - 'A needle in a doc comment or a string (a test fixture, a scanner's own needle table) is not a declaration'. Scope: Rust and Python only, the two languages glia and its tests are written in; their needles (rdkafka `.subscribe(&[`, lapin / pika `basic_publish(`, `FutureRecord::to(`, celery decorators, pyee `.emit(`, ...) always start in code, while the topic literal they read sits AFTER the needle, so checking only the needle's first byte keeps every real site. Every other language is byte-identical.
PROBE FIXTURE self-scan-literal-needles, graded at HEAD (`~/.venvs/glia-leap/bin/python bench/substrate-gap/grade.py <dir>`, leap wheel = HEAD; `./target/debug/glia analyze --format json` agrees): expect_nodes 3/3, FORBID VIOLATIONS 4 - queue_consumer:payments (Rust rdkafka, code), queue_producer:invoices (Python pika, code) and queue_producer:HardWorker (Ruby) are minted, and so are the phantoms queue_producer:orders and queue_producer:`orders\", data);\n` (a Rust test literal), queue_producer:refunds (a Python string), event_emit:user.created (a Rust test literal / doc comment) and queue_producer:sidekiq_ (a Rust fn name).
Graph queries run: repo-graph `orient` (the phantom queue entry points above), `find extract_queues` (queues.rs:582 extract_queue_consumer_nodes, :602 extract_queue_producer_nodes, :656 extract_queue_nodes_with_consts), then reads of emit_queue_nodes (:761), queue_topic::scan (:165), eventbus emit_event_nodes (:507) / find_gated (:1040) / scan_type_needles (:1641), cli::CodeMap (:420) and engine/src/extract.rs apply_cross_cutting_extractors (:232).
VERIFIER RE-MEASURE (HEAD f8a46c0, own git-archive copy, `GLIA_NO_PERSIST=1 ./target/debug/glia build <copy> --out <dir> --no-incremental`, read with the leap wheel's nodes_json / node_cells / edges_json): the same 177 (83 / 78 / 7 / 9) outside the four fixture roots, 136 / 296 QUEUE_FLOWS and 12 / 31 EVENT_FLOWS edges touching them. A line-level port of CodeMap over every site: 176 needles start in a literal or comment, queue_producer:sidekiq_ is the one code-position hit, and all 13 fixture-sited queue / event nodes in .rs / .py fixture files keep a code-position needle. FOUND BY THE VERIFIER: CodeMap::script(Python) lexes a whole f-string as a literal, so `f"redis://{os.getenv('REDIS_HOST')}"`, a common settings.py shape, would lose a real read once CJ.1c guards config reads. An f-string's replacement fields are expressions, so this packet's guard treats every byte of an f-string (prefix f / F / rf / fr, any case) as code: HEAD behaviour inside f-strings, the guard everywhere else. packets.implementation:
1. cli.rs: `struct CodeMap` -> `pub(crate) struct CodeMap`, `fn new` / `fn is_code` / `fn script` -> pub(crate), `enum Script` -> pub(crate) enum, and one new `pub(crate) fn literal_start(&self, pos: usize) -> Option<usize>` (partition_point as in is_code; the start of the skip range holding `pos`, None when `pos` is code; CJ.1c's quoted-key rule reads it too). Nothing else in cli.rs changes (its own scans keep calling the same functions); its doc gains one line naming code_guard as the second user.
2. code_guard.rs (new, `mod code_guard;` in lib.rs):
   - `fn lexer_for(path: &str) -> Option<(&'static str, Option<Script>)>`: by the LAST extension, ASCII case-folded: `rs` -> ("rust", None = CodeMap::new: `".."` with escapes, b"..", raw r#".."#, char literals, `//` and nesting `/* */`), `py` | `pyw` | `pyi` -> ("python", Some(Script::Python): `#` comments, `'..'`, `".."`, triple-quoted); anything else, and an empty path, -> None.
   - `pub(crate) struct CodeGuard<'a> { map: CodeMap, src: &'a [u8], lang: &'static str }` with `pub(crate) fn for_path(path, source) -> Option<CodeGuard>`, `pub(crate) fn literal_start(&self, pos) -> Option<usize>` (CodeMap::literal_start), `pub(crate) fn lang(&self) -> &'static str` and `pub(crate) fn is_code(&self, pos) -> bool` = CodeMap::is_code(pos), or, for Python only, `pos` sits in a literal whose opening quote (`literal_start`) is preceded by a string prefix of 1-2 ASCII letters from [fFrRbBuU] containing f / F, with a non-identifier byte (or the file start) before the prefix: an f-string's `{..}` replacement fields are expressions (`f"{os.getenv('X')}"`, `f'{producer.send(..)}'`), so the whole f-string reads as code - exactly HEAD's behaviour there - while a plain, raw, byte or triple-quoted string and every comment stay refused. Rust needs no such rule (format! arguments sit outside the literal; inline `{x}` holds identifiers only).
   - `pub(crate) struct LazyGuard<'a> { path: &'a str, source: &'a str, built: Option<Option<CodeGuard>>, dropped: usize }`: `new(path, source)` lexes nothing; `admits(&mut self, pos) -> bool` builds the guard on its first call (most files never reach a candidate needle), returns true when the file has no guard or `pos` is code, and counts a refusal in `dropped`; `report(&self, scanner: &str)` prints, only when dropped > 0, `[code-guard] <scanner> lang=<rust|python> dropped=<n> path=<path>`.
   Alternative weighed: the engine lexes once per file and passes `Option<&CodeGuard>` into every scanner - rejected because the guard type would have to become `pub` API of the extractors crate and every scanner signature would change; the queue / ws / cron scanners already take `path`, and the lazy build keeps the cost to files that hold a needle.
3. queue_topic.rs: `pub(crate) fn scan_guarded(source, needle, rule, guard: &mut LazyGuard<'_>) -> Vec<TopicHit>` = today's scan body with the occurrence iterator `source.match_indices(needle)` filtered, IN THIS ORDER, by (a) `bare_word_ok(source, offset, needle, rule)` and (b) `guard.admits(offset)`, then `.take(MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE)` - so 32 literal occurrences can no longer crowd a real call out of the cap. `bare_word_ok` is true unless rule == TopicRule::Receiver AND the needle's first byte is an identifier byte (the Sidekiq rows `perform_async` / `perform_in`), in which case the byte before the occurrence and the byte after the needle must both be non-identifier bytes (`HardWorker.perform_async(` and `perform_async(1)` are sites; `sidekiq_perform_async_uses_class` and `MyJob.perform_inline(` are not). `pub fn scan` keeps its signature as `scan_guarded(source, needle, rule, &mut LazyGuard::new("", source))` (no guard), so its tests and callers are unchanged.
4. queues.rs emit_queue_nodes: `let mut guard = LazyGuard::new(path, source);` before the pattern loop; `queue_topic::scan(source, pattern, *rule)` -> `queue_topic::scan_guarded(source, pattern, *rule, &mut guard)`; after the loop `guard.report(if kind == node_kind::QUEUE_CONSUMER { "queue_consumer" } else { "queue_producer" })`. Everything downstream of the hits (claimed spans, generic-verb guard, const fold, record_site, the framework-tag fallback when no hit named a topic, consumer callbacks, MESSAGE_TYPE offsets) is unchanged and only ever sees admitted hits, so a file whose every occurrence of a needle is refused mints neither a topic node nor its `unresolved:*` tag. The post-cache fold (extract_queue_nodes_with_consts) runs through the same function with the same path, so the cached pass and the fold agree.
5. eventbus.rs: `extract_event_emitter_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo)` / `extract_event_handler_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo)`; `emit_event_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo, side, resolve, counts)` (extract_event_nodes_with_consts passes its path) builds `let mut guard = LazyGuard::new(path, source);`, skips a typed site `(name, at)` from `(side.typed)(source)` when `!guard.admits(at)`, and passes `&mut guard` to `find_gated`, whose `while let` loop does `if !guard.admits(at) { continue; }` right after advancing `from` (before the queue_owned_publish and verb-gate checks, so a refused occurrence is never tallied as a gate rejection); at the end `guard.report("event_" + side.label)` (event_emitter / event_handler). The 32 existing test call sites of the two pub fns pass `""` (no guard, assertions unchanged).

packets.risks: A mis-lexed Rust or Python file could hide a real call: CodeMap is LA.20a's lexer, already pinned by cli.rs code_map_skips_literals_and_comments / script_code_map_skips_literals_comments_and_heredocs; a Python f-string is read as code whole (its replacement fields are expressions), so a needle in an f-string's literal text still mints, as at HEAD; known gaps, both on unusual source: a Python 3.12 f-string nesting the same quote (`f"{d["k"]}"`) ends early, and an unterminated literal runs to end of file. Recall must not move: run.py --check over every fixture, and the fixture probe found no fixture-sited .rs / .py queue or event node whose needle starts in a literal. The bare-word rule applies only to Receiver rows whose needle starts with an identifier byte (perform_async, perform_in), never to `producer.send` / `.delay(` rows (a `my_producer.send(` must keep matching). Determinism: a pure function of the file's bytes, built once per scanner call, no HashMap iteration; the cached per-file pass and the post-cache const fold use the same path and guard, so a clean and an incremental build agree (byte_identical). UTF-8: offsets come from match_indices (char boundaries); CodeMap steps bytes only to compare ASCII. Panic isolation unchanged (no new slicing). PARSER_STAMP moves (extractors are hashed), so every parse cache rebuilds once. Shared files with group CL: queues.rs / queue_topic.rs (CL.1-CL.4), eventbus.rs (CL.8), cli.rs (CL.10) - whichever lands second rebases onto the other; CL.1's tag-fallback rewrite of emit_queue_nodes must keep scan_guarded as its occurrence source.

Uses CJ.1a's code_guard::LazyGuard (no new type). Every change is 'refuse an occurrence whose needle byte is not code before anything else looks at it':
1. websocket.rs: scan builds `let mut guard = LazyGuard::new(path, source);` and calls `sites(source, r.needle, &mut guard)`; sites keeps its word-bound filter and adds `.filter(|&i| guard.admits(i))` BEFORE `.take(MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE)`; after the rows `guard.report(side.kind == WS_HANDLER ? "ws_handler" : "ws_client")`. The existing `[ws] <label> framework=..` lines are unchanged and simply count fewer nodes.
2. grpc.rs: `extract_grpc_client_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo)`, `extract_known_grpc_client_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo, known)`, `extract_grpc_server_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo, known, nodes, nav)`. suffix_pattern_hits(source, guard: &mut LazyGuard) does `if !guard.admits(pos) { continue; }` after advancing `search_from`; suffix_pattern_names passes the guard through. The known-client loop skips a refused `pos` the same way. server_hits(source, known, guard) extends its retain to `guard.admits(h.at) && !in_comment_line(..) && !follows_decl_keyword(..)` (rust_trait_impl_hits and node_add_service_hits are filtered by the same retain). Each pub fn ends with `guard.report("grpc_client" | "grpc_server")`. The ~35 existing grpc.rs test calls pass `""`.
3. graphql.rs: `extract_graphql_operation_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo)` builds the guard; scan_operation_needles(source, guard) - inside `line.match_indices(pattern).any(|(at, _)| ..)` the first test is `guard.admits(line_start + at)`; extract_gql_template_operations(source, guard) skips a `tag` the guard refuses. `guard.report("graphql_op")`. Resolver / SDL extraction (LA.27 marked literals, LA.38 decorators) is NOT guarded: an SDL schema legitimately lives in a string literal. The 7 existing test calls of the pub fn pass `""`, and the 4 direct scan_operation_needles test calls (graphql.rs ~:2337 / :2399 / :2407 / :2415) pass `&mut LazyGuard::new("", src)`.
4. engine: extract.rs passes `path` to extract_graphql_operation_nodes and extract_grpc_client_nodes; build/rpc_needles.rs needle_one already holds `path` and passes it to the known-client and server calls.

packets.implementation:
Uses CJ.1a's code_guard (CodeGuard, LazyGuard, CodeMap::literal_start; Python f-strings already count as code there).
1. code_guard.rs: `CodeGuard::opens_literal(&self, pos) -> bool` = self.literal_start(pos) == Some(pos); `LazyGuard::admits_key(&mut self, pos) -> bool` = no guard, or opens_literal(pos); a refusal counts in `dropped` like admits.
2. cron.rs: extract_cron_nodes builds `let mut guard = LazyGuard::new(path, source);` and passes `&mut guard` to extract_node_cron (skip a `cron.schedule(` / `cronTime:` occurrence the guard refuses), extract_scheduled_annotation (skip a refused `@Scheduled(`) and extract_celery_beat, whose `'schedule':` and `"schedule":` loops skip `pos` unless `guard.admits_key(pos)`: in .rs a `'schedule':` inside `".."` / `r#".."#` or a `//` comment is refused (a bare `'schedule':` in Rust code lexes as code, never as its own literal, so it is refused too - Celery beat is Python); in .py a dict key opens its own literal and is admitted, a key inside a larger string or a `#` comment is refused. The value read (celery_schedule_expr), the task look-back, the k8s / GitHub Actions / LA.19a / LA.19b schedulers and every non-Rust / non-Python file are unchanged. `guard.report("cron")` at the end.
3. data_sources.rs: `extract_data_source_nodes(source, path, module_id, repo)`; for each pattern, `source.match_indices(pattern).any(|(at, _)| guard.admits(at))` (stops at the first admitted occurrence) replaces `source.contains(pattern)`; the per-file provider dedup and the node / edge shape are unchanged. `guard.report("data_sources")`.
4. config.rs: `extract_config_reads(source, path, module_id, repo)`; after collecting `reads`, `reads.retain(|(_, offset)| guard.admits(*offset))` (each offset is the read needle's start, capture_first_string_arg / the process.env scan; LE.4b), then defs and sites as today. `guard.report("config")`.
5. secrets_flags.rs: `extract_secret_refs(source, path, module_id, repo)`, `extract_feature_flags(source, path, module_id, repo)`; `scan(source, rows, guard)` skips an occurrence `at` the guard refuses (after advancing `from`). Reports `secrets` / `flags`. The existing per-file `[secrets]` marker is unchanged.
6. engine/src/extract.rs passes `path` to the four calls; existing extractor tests (data_sources 4, config 11, secrets_flags 5 call sites) pass `""` (no guard, assertions unchanged).
7. TESTS. cron.rs literal_schedules_mint_nothing_in_rust (`"cron.schedule('*/5 * * * *', tick);"` and `// @Scheduled(cron = "0 4 * * * *")` in x.rs -> no job; the same text as x.js / x.java -> the HEAD jobs) and celery_beat_key_must_open_its_literal (x.py real dict `'schedule': crontab(minute=0)` -> job, `"schedule": EVERY_MINUTE` -> job as at HEAD; x.py `S = "{'schedule': crontab()}"` and `# 'schedule': crontab()` -> none; x.rs `let s = "{'schedule': crontab()}";` -> none; the same Rust text as x.ts -> the HEAD job). data_sources.rs literal_patterns_mint_nothing_in_rust_and_python (`let db = "new MongoClient(url)";` in x.rs -> none; `import redis\nr = redis.Redis()` in x.py -> data_source:redis; the same Rust text as x.ts -> mongodb). config.rs literal_env_reads_mint_nothing_in_rust_and_python (`std::env::var("APP_MODE")` in code -> config:env:APP_MODE with its site; `"os.getenv('JWT_SECRET')"` in a Rust string -> nothing; `os.getenv("DB_URL")` and `f"redis://{os.getenv('REDIS_HOST')}"` in x.py -> both reads, sites at the needle). secrets_flags.rs literal_flag_checks_mint_nothing_in_rust (`"ldClient.variation('beta-search', ctx, false)"` in x.rs -> no flag; as x.ts -> flag).

packets.rationale:
WHAT EXISTS (read at HEAD f8a46c0): the walk collects every `.md` (engine/src/walk.rs:471, G18) and build_docs_graph (engine/src/docs.rs:335) keeps a repo file only when include_doc (docs.rs:32) admits it: the eight exact-case repo-root names of is_wellknown_doc (:15), anything under a top-level `docs/` or `.ai/`, or an ADR directory (is_adr_path :52, LF.4b); licence files never. link_doc_sections (engine/src/passes.rs:205) then links a DOC_SECTION to a symbol only through a single-backtick span (backtick_spans :740, A16.3 tiers, MAX_LINKS_PER_DOC 25, CG.3's multi-line-span guard). Nothing declares this scope: the only DOCUMENTS caveat row (engine/src/coverage.rs:68) is about contract JSON size, so `glia docs-for x` answering 'no DOCUMENTS edge reaches x' never says a README in a sub-project or a feature spec was not read. The Engram battery named three quokka doc mentions; CG's spec (7.3) found them outside ingestion by design and left the widening to James, who took it (7.4: 'doc ingestion widened to project-root well-known docs + SDD feature docs ... keeping the backtick rule and a coverage caveat').
MEASURED on a git-archive copy of quokka-stack a77d4cb: HEAD ingests 20 docs - `[docs] sections=133 from 20 doc(s) ... dir_scoped=19`, `[doclink] 179 DOCUMENTS edges (strong=5 qualified, medium=112 unique, weak=62 ambiguous) over 314 doc sections`. Project roots (`glia projects`): quokka_android, quokka_android/android, quokka_android/android/app, quokka_web, tools/ui-state-map/editor/.vite/deps, turps. (a) well-known docs at a PROJECT root: 5 files (quokka_android/README.md, quokka_web/README.md, turps/{CHANGELOG,CLAUDE,README}.md); (b) SDD feature docs: 36 files, features/<12 features>/{backend, current-state, ui}.md (their feature.yaml siblings are contracts already); no spec-kit dir (docs/superpowers/specs/ is under docs/ already). Probe: the 41 files copied under docs/__a__/ and docs/__b__/ of a second copy (which HEAD ingests; linking is text-only, so the edge count carries over): `[docs] sections=401 from 61 doc(s) ... dir_scoped=60`, `[doclink] 961 DOCUMENTS edges (strong=43, medium=725, weak=193)` (the verifier's re-run of the same relocation, features under docs/__b__/features/<f>/: 962, strong=44 - one more qualified mention; 179 old + 12 + 771): +12 edges out of 3 of the 5 project-root docs - incl. the turps README section 'Messaging and Fanout' (line 31) -> turps::Services::chat::ChatOps::ChatOps::EnsureUserReadyForChat, the mention at turps/README.md:50 the Engram battery asked for - and +770 out of 35 of the 36 feature docs. glia copy: +2 docs (bench/lens/README.md, py/README.md; glia has 187 project roots, no features/ or spec-kit dir). Precision: 'NOT any markdown in source trees' - a README beside code (`services/orders/internal/README.md`, Angular's `web/src/app/features/cart/README.md`) and a non-feature `specs/drafts/` stay out; the fixture's forbid rows pin all three. Graph queries run: repo-graph find `include_doc` (docs.rs:32, ⊘: reached only through build_docs_graph), read of build_docs_graph and link_doc_sections.
VERIFIER CHECKS: HEAD quokka copy `[docs] sections=133 from 20 doc(s) ... dir_scoped=19`, `[doclink] 179 DOCUMENTS edges` (identical); `glia projects` lists the six roots named; the relocation probe holds docs::docs::__a__::turps::README::messaging-and-fanout -DOCUMENTS-> turps::Services::chat::ChatOps::ChatOps::EnsureUserReadyForChat. The fixture's three forbid qnames are the exact qnames the rule would mint (relocating the six fixture docs under docs/ mints docs::docs::services::orders::internal::README::internal, docs::docs::web::src::app::features::cart::README::cart and docs::docs::specs::drafts::ideas::ideas, and the three expected edges), so the precision gate is live. No existing bench fixture holds a markdown file the widened rule admits (scan of every fixture and matrix probe for a well-known name at a manifest dir, features/<f>/*.md, specs/<NNN-slug>/); no engine / cli / py test writes one (contract_breaks.rs's web/README.md has no manifest beside it; live_records.rs's api/README.md is a repo root).
DECISION 2026-10-01 (James, on the CJ-2 open question): (a) every .md under specs/<NNN-slug>/ (contracts/ and checklists/ included) and (b) case-insensitive README*.md variants stay as specced; (c) a PROJECT root's own `docs/` tree is ADMITTED by the same rule as the repo-root `docs/` (any depth below it, licence files out). A rule simulation over the copy's 69 tracked .md files (walk minus .ai/repo-graph/, which the walk skips) gives the same split: root 1, docs/ 3, .ai/ 16, project-root well-known 5, feature 36, spec-kit 0, project-root docs/ 0. glia copy (git archive f8a46c0, 187 project roots): the only non-root project with a docs/ dir is bench/substrate-gap/fixtures/contract-openapi-swaggo-yaml (no .md), so (c) adds 0 there too; Kina a448fb3 tracks no docs/*.md at all, and no tracked repo under /home/ivy/Code has a markdown file under a manifest-rooted project's docs/ (git ls-tree scan of every repo there). (c) is therefore exercised by the fixture only: services/orders/docs/runbook.md (services/orders has go.mod) is ingested and services/docs/overview.md (services/ is not a project root) is not; grade.py at HEAD on the extended fixture: DOCUMENTS 0/4, FORBID VIOLATIONS 0. Relocating the fixture's eight markdown files under docs/ (HEAD ingests that) mints docs::docs::services::orders::docs::runbook::runbook and docs::docs::services::docs::overview::overview, so the new expect row and the new forbid name the exact qname shapes the rule produces (the forbid is live). Vendored dependency trees (node_modules, vendor, bower_components, .venv, site-packages) are collapsed by walk_gating before the docs records exist, so a checked-in package's docs/ never reaches the rule.

SLOT. py/src/overlay_loop.rs and its `mod overlay_loop;` line in py/src/lib.rs are created doc-only by the integrator's py slot packet (slot_requests: `py module overlay_loop`); this packet fills the file and never edits py/src/lib.rs. Module name mirrors the engine slot (glia_engine::overlay_loop), as py/src/timeline.rs mirrors glia_engine::timeline.

1. FUNCTIONS (module functions, not PyGraph methods: each builds the tree itself from repo paths, as `overlay_delta` does; one module so the api_surface test's no-duplicate-name rule sees the family together):
```rust
#[pyfunction]
#[pyo3(signature = (repo_paths, categories=None, top_k=20, snippet_lines=3))]
fn overlay_propose(py: Python<'_>, repo_paths: Vec<String>, categories: Option<Vec<String>>, top_k: usize, snippet_lines: usize) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>>
#[pyfunction]
#[pyo3(signature = (repo_paths, candidate, leave_one_out=true))]
fn overlay_try(py: Python<'_>, repo_paths: Vec<String>, candidate: &str, leave_one_out: bool) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>>
#[pyfunction]
#[pyo3(signature = (repo_path, candidate=None, only=None, remove=None, dry_run=false))]
fn overlay_accept(py: Python<'_>, repo_path: &str, candidate: Option<&str>, only: Option<Vec<String>>, remove: Option<Vec<String>>, dry_run: bool) -> PyResult<Py<PyAny>>
```
Each body is `to_py(py, serde_json::to_string(&<helper>(..).map_err(PyValueError::new_err)?))` (LD.2: a native dict whose keys are the engine struct's serde fields in field order: propose {rows, counts, snippets, ambiguous_root, guide}, a row = the `glia gaps` row (id first) + `snippet` ({file, start_line, lines} or None); try {stanzas, base, with, delta, verdict, closed, builds}, a stanza {stanza, gaps, closes, marginal, verdict}, base / with {nodes_by_kind, edges_by_category, gaps_by_category}; accept {added, removed, duplicates, file, dry_run, written, diff}). `repo_paths`: the first is the primary repo (whose .glia/overlay.toml the loop reads), the rest merge in (the CLI's --with). `candidate` is the candidate's TOML TEXT, not a path: the MCP's model step produces text, and a temp file is a CLI convenience (`pathlib.Path(f).read_text()` covers a file). The fix stays in diff.rs, not in hint generation: the base of an upgrade diff is a gmap an older exporter wrote, whose hints cannot change, so only the matching can make 'the same diff pair correctly'. diff_gmaps stays a pure function of the two gmaps (no history graph argument; module doc's content-address promise). 1. HELPERS (private, diff.rs): - `fn hint_slot(n: &GmapNode) -> Option<(&str, &str)>`: (file token, kind) of a `::` hint, split from the right with rsplitn(3, ':') as lib.rs prior_tokens does; None unless the ordinal is all digits and kind and token are non-empty (a NatSpec fact's `#natspec:..` and an unhinted node are None). - `fn is_route(n) -> bool`: hint_slot kind == glia_code_domain::node_kind::ROUTE.0 rendered as decimal (engram-export already depends on glia-code-domain; never the literal 5). - `fn route_of(key: &str) -> Option<(&str, &str)>`: (verb, path) of a ROUTE key in every shape the tree emits, through the canonical parsers, never a hand-rolled split: `let (q, _) = glia_code_domain::endpoint::split_owner(key);` (the house rule: every consumer that parses a ROUTE / ENDPOINT / page qname strips the owner with it), then `let path = glia_graph::nav::nav_route_path(q)?;` (`page:

` LB.4c client-router pages, `route:

` go / ts_routes, `

` with an upper-case method and a '/'-rooted path); the path is a suffix slice of q, so the verb is `q[..q.len() - path.len()].trim_end()`: `page:`, `route:` or the METHOD. engram-export already depends on glia-code-domain and glia-graph (engram-export/Cargo.toml); no dependency change. The owner is not compared (a project-root rename relabels every route of a service). Why all three shapes: Kina's HEAD graph holds 57 `page:` ROUTEs beside 91 ` ` ones (measured on the spec probe's kina_head.json), and a `page:/kyc` -> `page:/admin` ordinal pair is the same cross-pairing the item forbids. - `fn alike_paths(a: &str, b: &str) -> bool`: equal, or the shorter starts with '/', is not "/", and the longer ends with it (a `route:` path that is not '/'-rooted is alike only when equal). Since the shorter starts with '/', the match always starts on a segment boundary: `/trades/:id/fund` ~ `/api/trades/:id/fund` (a mount prefix gained, CB.23) or lost; `/xtrades/:id` !~ `/trades/:id`; `/trades/:id/dispute` !~ `/trades/:id/dispute/propose`. "/" is alike only to "/": join_path("/api", "/") is "/api", but "/" as a suffix would make every route of a file a candidate. - `fn route_pair_ok(b, t) -> bool`: true unless both are routes whose keys parse; then same verb && alike_paths. A ROUTE key with no path in any of the three shapes keeps today's behaviour (true). (The spec probe's prototype returned false there; it changes nothing measured: no such pair reached the hint pass on Kina or quokka-stack.) 2. PASS B - routes (`fn pair_routes(base, target, pair, taken) -> usize`): group the unmatched ROUTEs of each side by (file token, verb) in a BTreeMap<(&str, &str), Vec<(index, path)>>. For each group on both sides, two tiers: EXACT (path == path) then TAIL (alike_paths). In a tier, snapshot the free base and target entries; pair base b with target t only when t is b's ONLY fitting free target and b is t's ONLY fitting free base (mutual uniqueness makes the result independent of iteration order); the TAIL tier re-snapshots after EXACT. Returns the pairs made (stats.by_route). Ambiguous tails (offers.go: `/offers` fits `/api/offers` and `/api/user/offers`) stay unmatched for the guarded hint pass. Alternative weighed: longest-tail-wins with iteration; rejected - more rules, and the measured ambiguous pairs (2 on Kina) already pair right through the guarded hint. 3. PASS C - names (`fn pair_names(..) -> usize`): unmatched Content::Symbol nodes that are not ROUTEs, grouped by (file token, kind, Symbol.name) in BTreeMaps; a group with exactly one base and one target pairs (stats.by_name). This is LB.6's move-stable shape (kind + file + local name) read off the gmap: a file moved along a --since chain keeps its token, every key changes, and a function inserted ahead would otherwise shift its siblings' ordinals. Propositions (no name) and unhinted nodes skip it. Alternative weighed: pass the bin's LB.6 MoveMap.nodes (old_qname -> new_qname) into diff_gmaps; rejected - it needs the prior history graph, which the measured upgrade did not have (`prior graph unavailable ... old format v2`), and it would make the diff depend on more than the two gmaps. 4. PASS D - hints: as today (unique on both sides among the still-unmatched, BTreeMap by hint), plus `if !route_pair_ok(&base.nodes[b], &target.nodes[t]) { stats.hint_refused += 1; continue; }` before pairing; pairs made count stats.by_hint. A refused base is removed and its target added (a route whose method or path really changed is a new contract; Engram mints it a fresh FactId instead of inheriting a neighbour's salience). 5. STATS: DiffStats gains `pub by_route, by_name, by_hint, hint_refused: usize` (doc: pairs per pass; on a glia export, whose keys are unique, every pass B-D pair changes the key, so by_route + by_name + by_hint == moved). identical_is_empty's `DiffStats::default()` still holds (key pairs are not counted). add_remove_modify's literal adds the four fields at 0. 6. BIN: right after the `v6 since:` eprintln (glia-export-engram.rs:319, inside `if let Some((base, ds)) = since`): `eprintln!("[engram-export] v6 since pairing: route={} name={} hint={} hint_refused={}", ds.by_route, ds.by_name, ds.by_hint, ds.hint_refused)`. A separate line, so the `v6 since: base=` line (since_v6.rs since_line, Engram's docs) keeps its shape. 7. No dependency or Cargo.lock change. Lands after CK.2 (same bin file and tests/since_v6.rs). The meta sidecar is written after files.json and before the diff / history: a crash between the gmap rename and the meta rename leaves the previous run's meta beside the new gmap, which its gmap_digest exposes (a reader compares it with content_digest of the gmap bytes); the meta is never read by glia itself, so a stale or missing one changes no glia behaviour. Keys go through a BTreeMap so serde_json's preserve_order feature (pulled by other crates through feature unification) cannot reorder them. The meta holds no repo path, no source text and no value data, only build identity and a digest.

packets.title: Queue row semantics: a framework tag is minted only for an unexplained topic-less call, declaring a RabbitMQ queue is not consuming it (it names the file's unnamed consume), amqplib publishes to its routing key, a BullMQ job name is not a topic, and a Python `.delay(` on a from-imported task fires without a celery import
packets.area: CL-1 matrix none/partial: queue row semantics (python/amqp, csharp/amqp, typescript/amqp, typescript/taskq, python/taskq)
packets.rationale:
Five Tier-1 cells fail on the SAME emit loop, parsers/code/extractors/src/queues.rs emit_queue_nodes, and its row tables. Measured at HEAD f8a46c0 (grade.py, venv wheel = HEAD; matrix.py --check OK, 346/482):
- matrix/python/amqp PARTIAL (extract 2/2 literal 2/2 route 1/1 forbid 1/3): FORBID VIOLATIONS 2 - `queue_consumer:orders` matched=2 max=1 (the producer's own `channel.queue_declare(queue="orders")` hits the CONSUMER row `queue_declare(`), and `queue_producer:unresolved:rabbitmq` matched=1 (the ArgLiteral row `channel.basic_publish` reads arg #0 = `exchange=""`, finds nothing and tags the SAME call the Keyed row `basic_publish(` named `orders`).
- matrix/csharp/amqp PARTIAL (forbid 2/3): `queue_consumer:orders` matched=2 max=1 - `.QueueDeclare(` is a consumer row, so Producer.cs mints a consumer; `.BasicConsume(` has NO row (the consumer is found only because the tutorial also declares the queue).
- matrix/typescript/amqp PARTIAL (literal 1/2 route 0/1 forbid 3/4): `channel.publish('shop', 'orders', buf)` is ArgLiteral over arg #0, the EXCHANGE: XX QUEUE_PRODUCER 'orders', XX `queue_producer:shop` matched=1.
- matrix/typescript/taskq PARTIAL (forbid 2/3): `queue.add('process-order', data)` is ArgLiteral, so the BullMQ JOB name is minted as a topic (`queue_producer:process-order`); the queue identity already comes from `new Queue('orders')`.
- python/taskq NONE (extract 3/4 literal 3/4 route 1/2): fixtures/xcut-queue-py-celery is full, matrix/python/taskq reads XX QUEUE_PRODUCER 'process_order' - `.delay(` is gated on ['celery', '@shared_task'] and the canonical caller only does `from tasks import process_order` + `process_order.delay(order_id)`.
Root cause of the tag rows: the fallback is decided PER NEEDLE ROW (`if sites.is_empty() && !matches!(rule, TopicRule::NoIdentity)`), so a second row reading the same call, or a liveness row in a file another row already named, mints a sentinel. No key.json expects a tag: `unresolved:` occurs only in 61 forbid rows (grep over fixtures/ and matrix/). The same machinery is what CL.2 / CL.3 need for go/kafka (`writer.WriteMessages` / `reader.ReadMessage` tags beside named nodes), csharp/nats (`nc.Publish` prefix-matching `nc.PublishAsync`), java/sqs_sns (`sqs.receiveMessage(request)`) and go/amqp (`ch.Consume(q.Name, ..)` after `ch.QueueDeclare("orders")`). Graph queries run: repo-graph find QueueFramework (the MCP index is 0.5.0 and shows glia's own phantom QUEUE_* nodes - CJ's self-scan item), find resolve_calls; the rest read by symbol.
