packets.implementation:
1. EXPLAINED-HIT TAG RULE (replaces the per-row fallback, monotone: it only ever REMOVES a tag HEAD minted). While scanning, push every hit of every row into `spans: Vec<HitSpan { start, end, framework, named: Option<usize /*pending idx*/>, no_identity: bool, has_expr: bool, declared: Option<usize> }>`. A row whose sites are empty and whose rule is not NoIdentity (HEAD's condition) becomes a `DeferredTag { row, framework, hits }` instead of an immediate record_site. After the last row (and after the DECLARE pass on the consumer side) each deferred hit is EXPLAINED when (i) its needle span overlaps the span of a hit of the SAME framework that named a topic or belongs to a NoIdentity row (two rows reading one call: pika `channel.basic_publish` + `basic_publish(`; segmentio `reader.ReadMessage` + `.ReadMessage(`); (ii) it carries no identifier expression (`h.expr == None`) and `pending` holds a named node of that framework (a liveness call such as `sqs.receiveMessage(request)` in a file whose request builder named the queue); or (iii) the DECLARE pass bound it. A deferred tag whose hits are ALL explained is not recorded; any unexplained hit records it exactly as HEAD (Weak, first hit's site, LA.33 callbacks). Callbacks of a suppressed tag move to the node that explained the hit ((i) the overlapping named node, (iii) the bound declared node, (ii) the single named node of that framework, or are dropped and counted when there are several). Deferred tags are recorded in row order after the named nodes, so a file whose tag survives lists it last (deterministic; node order changes only in files that also hold a named node of the same framework). Alternative weighed: a per-file 'any named node silences every tag of the framework' rule - rejected, it would hide a genuinely unresolved second topic (a kafkajs file publishing to 'orders' and to `topicVar` keeps its tag under this rule).
2. DECLARE BINDING. `queue_declare(` / `.QueueDeclare(` / `.QueueDeclareAsync(` move to DECLARE_PATTERNS, scanned only on the consumer side. Their topics are DECLARED queues, never consumer sites by themselves. Unnamed consume hits = consumer-row hits of the same framework with no topic and a non-NoIdentity rule. When the file declares EXACTLY ONE queue of that framework, each unnamed consume hit becomes a consumer site of it at the CONSUME call's offset (so LE.4c anchors it to the consuming function) and is explained (iii); zero or two-plus declared queues bind nothing (ambiguous - the tag survives as HEAD's). So a producer file that declares the queue it publishes to mints no consumer (python/amqp, csharp/amqp), and Go's `q, _ := ch.QueueDeclare("orders", ..)` + `ch.Consume(q.Name, ..)` (CL.2 adds the Go rows) names `orders`.
3. ROWS. CONSUMER: `.BasicConsume(` / `.BasicConsumeAsync(` ["rabbitmq.client"] KeyedOrArg(&["queue"]) (v6 `BasicConsume(queue: "orders", autoAck: true, consumer: c)` and positional; v7 async). PRODUCER: `.BasicPublishAsync(` ["rabbitmq.client"] ArgIndex(1) (v7, named `routingKey:` sits in arg #1); `channel.publish` -> ArgIndexOr(1, 0) (amqplib `publish(exchange, routingKey, content)`: the routing key names the queue on the default and direct exchanges; an empty key - fanout - falls back to the exchange, HEAD's identity); `.sendToQueue(` ["amqplib"] ArgLiteral (the default-exchange shortcut, no row at HEAD); `queue.add(` -> NoIdentity (a BullMQ job name is dispatch metadata the worker reads as `job.name`; the queue identity is `new Queue('x')` / `@InjectQueue('x')`); `@InjectQueue(` ["@nestjs/bull"] ArgLiteral (NestJS producers inject the queue by name and call `this.q.add(..)`). ArgIndexOr lives in queue_topic.rs: topic_at reads arg_literal(region, n); when arg n is present and is an empty literal ('' / ""), it reads arg_literal(region, m); expr_at mirrors it (arg n's expression, else arg m's).
4. CELERY IMPORT GATE. A const `IMPORT_GATED_ROWS: &[&str] = &[".delay("]`: when such a row's library gate fails, the file path ends in `.py` / `.pyw`, the hits are still scanned and a hit is kept iff its TopicRule::Receiver symbol is a BARE name (no `.` in the receiver chain) bound by a `from <mod> import ...` line of the same file (python_imported_names: comma lists, `as` aliases bind the alias, parenthesised multi-line lists, `import *` binds nothing). `pygame.time.delay(100)` (dotted chain) and jQuery `.delay(` (not Python) stay out; `from x import time` + `time.delay(..)` would fire (accepted, recorded as a known imprecision in the doc comment). `.apply_async(` is already ungated.
5. MARKERS (GLIA_QUEUE_DEBUG=1, beside the existing `[queues] needle` lines): `[queues] tag-suppressed needle='<n>' framework=<F> side=<consumer|producer> by=<overlap|named|declare> file=<path>`, `[queues] declare-bound queue=<q> framework=<F> consume='<needle>' consumes=<k> file=<path>`, `[queues] declare-unbound declared=<d> framework=<F> file=<path>` (d != 1), `[queues] import-gated needle='.delay(' receiver=<sym> file=<path>`.
6. TESTS (queues.rs mod tests): declaring_a_queue_is_not_consuming_it (pika and RabbitMQ.Client producer files: no consumer; the BasicConsume file: queue_consumer:orders); declared_queue_names_an_unnamed_consume (pika `queue_declare(queue="jobs")` + `basic_consume(queue=qname, on_message_callback=cb)` -> queue_consumer:jobs, no tag, the callback still bound; two declared queues -> no binding, tag kept); same_call_read_by_two_rows_mints_no_tag (python/amqp's producer shape -> exactly [queue_producer:orders]); liveness_call_beside_a_named_node_mints_no_tag (a no-expression consume hit + another row naming the queue -> one node); unexplained_hit_keeps_its_tag (kafkajs `producer.send({ topic: 'orders', messages })` + `producer.produce(topicVar, msg)` -> [orders, unresolved:kafka], exactly HEAD's output); amqplib_publish_reads_the_routing_key (`channel.publish('shop', 'orders', b)` -> orders; `channel.publish('logs', '', b)` -> logs; `channel.sendToQueue('jobs', b)` -> jobs); bullmq_job_name_is_not_a_topic (typescript/taskq's producer -> [queue_producer:orders]); inject_queue_names_the_producer (`@InjectQueue('audio') private q: Queue` -> queue_producer:audio); celery_delay_on_an_imported_task (`from tasks import process_order` + `process_order.delay(1)` -> queue_producer:process_order; `import pygame` + `pygame.time.delay(1)` -> nothing); arg_index_or_falls_back_only_on_an_empty_literal (queue_topic.rs). backtick_literal is rewritten over `new Queue(\`emails\`, ..)` (its subject is the backtick reader, not queue.add).
INTEGRATOR (finishing-batch merge): lands after CJ.1a (depends_on), which rewrites the same emit_queue_nodes: one LazyGuard over `path`, queue_topic::scan_guarded in place of scan (a refused occurrence is dropped before the MAX_HITS_PER_NEEDLE cap), guard.report(..) at the end. Keep scan_guarded as the occurrence source of every row loop this packet adds or moves (DECLARE_PATTERNS included) and run the deferred-tag pass over the guarded hits only, so a refused Rust / Python literal neither mints nor explains a tag. CL.2-CL.4's new needle literals in queues.rs / queue_topic.rs are then guarded in glia's own build, and CJ.1a's measured phantom counts stay true.

packets.implementation:
1. TopicRule::Chain(keys). chain_region(source, after): from the needle's end, walk bytes tracking bracket depth and quotes (region_body's rules) and stop at the first of: a depth-0 `;`; a closing bracket that takes depth below 0 (the chain is an argument / initializer); a depth-0 newline whose next non-blank byte is not `.` and whose previous non-blank byte is not `.` (Scala / Kotlin / Go statements end at a newline, Java / C# continuation lines start with `.`); MAX_REGION. topic_at: keyed_literal(chain_region, keys) - keyed_literal already reads a builder METHOD key (`.queueName("x")`, `.WithTopic("x")`, `.queueUrl("x")`) with `(` as the separator when a `.` precedes the key (A2.6). expr_at: keyed_expr over the same region, so `.queueName(QUEUE)` folds through LA.4. Keys are tried in table order: queueName before topicName, so a topic receiver `.receiver().topicName("t").subscriptionName("s")` reads the TOPIC, the existing `CreateProcessor(` precedent (arg #0 joins the sender). Alternative weighed: needles spelling the whole chain (`.sender().queueName(`) - rejected, it misses the line-broken builder (java/sqs_sns's consumer, every Azure sample) and `.connectionString(c)` in between.
2. GENERIC ARGUMENTS. arg_region: when the needle does not end in a bracket and the trimmed rest starts with `<`, skip the balanced `<...>` (depth-counted, `>>` closes two levels, at most MAX_REGION bytes, a `;` / newline / `(` before the close aborts) and continue at the `(` / `{` / `[`. NATS `.SubscribeAsync<string>("orders")`, Hangfire `Enqueue<Jobs>(x => ..)` (CL.4). The `ProducerRecord<>(` KNOWN MISS comment in PRODUCER_PATTERNS is updated: `new ProducerRecord<String, String>(` is now readable by a `ProducerRecord<` row - not added here (no failing cell; noted for 0.5.2).
3. GENERIC-VERB GUARD by needle: is_generic_verb_row(pattern, framework) is true only for the bare verb needles listed above on RedisPubSub / Mqtt rows (every such row at HEAD), so the MQTTnet builder / SubscribeAsync rows read their topic normally and still yield nothing they should not (they are not shared verbs). Behaviour of every HEAD row is unchanged.
4. ROWS as listed in entry_points. Gates (lowercase): Azure Java / Scala `com.azure.messaging.servicebus` -> "azure.messaging.servicebus" (the C# namespace lowercases to the same text; `.sender()` / `.receiver()` do not occur in the C# API); Spring Cloud GCP `com.google.cloud.spring.pubsub` / `org.springframework.cloud.gcp.pubsub`; Spring Data Redis; AWS SDK v2 `software.amazon.awssdk.services.sqs` / `.sns`; NATS.Net `NATS.Client.Core` / `NATS.Net`; `MQTTnet`; `Google.Cloud.PubSub.V1`. The NATS rows are receiver-agnostic (`.PublishAsync(`), unlike the HEAD `nc.` rows; the HEAD `nc.Publish` / `nc.Subscribe` prefix hits on `nc.PublishAsync(` overlap the new named hits, so CL.1 (i) drops their tags. java/sqs_sns's `sqs.receiveMessage(request)` has no expression in a `queueUrl` slot, so CL.1 (ii) drops its tag once `ReceiveMessageRequest.builder()` named `orders`.

packets.risks: appsettings.json values are untrusted text: they go only into env_cell (A13.7 redaction) and never into a qname or name. serde_json's Map iterates either sorted (default) or in file order (preserve_order; Cargo.lock lists indexmap under serde_json, so feature unification may have it on) - both deterministic for a given file; tests must assert the key SET, and build_sided's qname dedupe keeps output stable. A `config["k"]` on a user dictionary named config would read as a setting (gated by the IConfiguration mention). engine/src/walk.rs is also a likely target of CJ's doc-ingestion item (cross-group deps). The Cargo.lock does not move (serde_json is already a dependency of glia-code-extractors). PARSER_STAMP moves (extractor + engine route source). ENV OVERRIDE: a non-.NET repo that names an env var with `__` (some Python settings libraries use it for nesting too) gains a config:setting: node nothing reads - additive, no answer lists an unread CONFIG_KEY (gaps / check have no config-unread row), and none exists in any tracked repo under /home/ivy/Code (measured). The override edge must carry its own EVIDENCE (emitter + rule) before route.rs's stamp_missing runs, or it is filed under the sibling's bare emitter and the rule is lost; the expansion keeps item order, so NodeId order and edge order stay deterministic. The value cell goes through env_cell, never into the qname.

packets.rationale: go/eventbus = none (extract 0/2 literal 0/2 route 0/1) at HEAD f8a46c0: matrix/go/eventbus/bus.go is `bus := evbus.New(); bus.Subscribe("order:placed", SendReceipt); bus.Publish("order:placed", "o-1")` with `import evbus "github.com/asaskevich/EventBus"`. parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs EMITTER_PATTERNS / HANDLER_PATTERNS spell `publish(` / `.subscribe(` - Go's capitalised API matches none. The receiver `bus` is bus-shaped (BUS_RECEIVER_SUFFIXES) and the event name is a literal, so LA.29's Bus gate and CB.3a's naming rule already apply once the needles exist.
entry_points: parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:41 EMITTER_PATTERNS - `(".Publish(", NameRule::Literal, true, VerbGate::Bus)`
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:52 HANDLER_PATTERNS - `.Subscribe(`, `.SubscribeAsync(`, `.SubscribeOnce(`, `.SubscribeOnceAsync(` each `(NameRule::Literal, true, VerbGate::Bus)`
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:249 PUBSUB_IMPORTS - "asaskevich/eventbus" (lower-case: the check reads the lowered source)
parsers/code/extractors/src/eventbus.rs:1811 mod tests - five new tests
packets.implementation:
The rows are broker-ambiguous (`true`): in a file carrying any broker signal - NATS `nc.Publish`, paho `client.Publish`, streadway / amqp091 (CL.2), confluent `consumer.Subscribe` - they are skipped outright (A2.9), so Go broker traffic stays QUEUE_*. VerbGate::Bus keeps a call only on a bus-shaped receiver (`bus.`, `eventBus.`, `publisher.`) or in a file importing an in-process pub/sub library (the new PUBSUB_IMPORTS entry covers `eb := EventBus.New()`). judge_verb's `new ` check keeps MediatR's `.Publish(new X())` a type site; NameRule::Literal mints nothing for `.Publish(evt)` (CB.3a). A Go method DECLARATION `func (b *Bus) Publish(` is never matched: the needles are dotted. Event names keep LA.41's rule (`order:placed` passes). TESTS: go_asaskevich_bus_pairs (bus.go -> event_emit:order:placed + event_handle:order:placed); go_bus_alias_through_the_import (`eb := EventBus.New(); eb.Subscribe("x", h)` -> handler x via=import); go_nats_publish_stays_broker_traffic (`nc.Publish("x", b)` with a nats import -> no EVENT node); csharp_rx_subscribe_is_not_a_bus (`source.Subscribe(x => ..)` -> nothing); mediatr_publish_new_is_a_type_site_not_a_string (`_mediator.Publish(new OrderPlaced())` -> exactly HEAD's typed node).
INTEGRATOR (finishing-batch merge): lands after CJ.1a (depends_on): emit_event_nodes / find_gated then take `path` and skip an occurrence the Rust / Python literal guard refuses. The new `.Publish(` / `.Subscribe*(` rows go through find_gated unchanged, so their needle literals in eventbus.rs mint no phantom EVENT_* node in glia's own build.

packets.implementation:
1. extract_nest_schedule: every `@Cron(` occurrence: the first argument - a quoted literal -> normalise_schedule (a 6-field NestJS expression with seconds passes looks_like_cron_expr's 5..=7 fields); a `CronExpression.<MEMBER>` member -> the schedule is the member path verbatim (`CronExpression.EVERY_DAY_AT_3AM`, a stable identity; the enum's literal values are not tabled); anything else -> no job. `@Interval(` - a numeric literal (or `'name', n`) -> schedule `@every <n>ms`. `@Timeout(` is a one-shot, not a schedule: not read. Handler: the method after the decorator (stacked decorators skipped), scoped by enclosing_class_name -> CallQualifier::Attribute { base: class, name: method } at the decorator's row (LC.3b), the Spring precedent; target = the method name.
